title: Evaluation of Carbon-Dots (CDs) as Antiviral Candidates Against SARS-CoV-2 Using a Chemical Crosslinking Method
abstract: The chemical crosslinking method has been effective in previous studies for interaction-based drug screening. Although CDs have been widely explored as antiviral candidates, studies that use chemical crosslinking to select effective CDs against SARS-CoV-2 remain limited. To address this gap, this study uses chemical crosslinking to test CDs as antiviral compounds. The objective of this study is to screen and determine the potential of CDs as candidate antiviral compounds for inhibiting the dimerization of the SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein using a chemical crosslinking method. Recombinant SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein was expressed, purified, and precipitated for compound testing with chemical crosslinking. The concentration ranges used in the dimerization inhibition testing were 0-2,000 ppm (pyrrolic-N CDs) and 0-6,000 ppm (pyridinic-N, graphitic-N, and nuciferine-derived CDs). The study’s results show that CDs have the potential to inhibit dimerization of the SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein. Among the four compounds tested, pyrrolic-N CDs showed the best inhibitory potential, as they inhibited dimerization at the lowest concentration (2,000 ppm), had the smallest percentage of dimer bands to total protein, and achieved the highest dimerization inhibition efficiency. However, further research, including in vitro and in vivo tests, is needed to comprehensively evaluate the potential of pyrrolic-N CDs.

title: Case Report: Thrombotic and haemorrhagic disseminated intravascular coagulation in COVID-19
abstract: Background COVID-19-associated coagulopathy has been predominantly characterised as a hypercoagulable state with fibrinolytic shutdown. However, the full phenotypic spectrum of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) in COVID-19 remains incompletely characterised. This report adds two cases demonstrating that COVID-19-associated DIC can manifest as two distinct phenotypes at opposite ends of the coagulation spectrum. Case summary We report two cases of severe COVID-19 with diametrically opposed DIC phenotypes. Case 1: a 23-year-old immunosuppressed male with SARS-CoV-2 bloodstream and central nervous system infection developed haemorrhagic DIC, characterised by severe hypofibrinogenemia (0.76 g/L), markedly elevated PIC (>40 μg/mL), and preserved platelet counts (>100 × 10 9 /L). He was successfully treated with titrated tranexamic acid. Case 2: a 54-year-old previously healthy female with severe COVID-19 pneumonia developed thrombotic DIC, characterised by significant thrombocytopenia (platelets 65 × 10 9 /L, nadir 40 × 10 9 /L), multi-organ injury, and lower extremity venous thrombosis. She was successfully treated with low-molecular-weight heparin. Conclusion COVID-19-associated DIC spans two phenotypes—thrombotic (platelet consumption, requiring anticoagulation) and haemorrhagic (fibrinogen consumption with hyperfibrinolysis, requiring antifibrinolytics)—validating the 2025 ISTH classification and highlighting the need for phenotype-specific therapy guided by serial coagulation monitoring.

title: Thrombotic Complications in Patients With Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19): Two Contrasting Clinical Presentations Viewed Through the Concept of Thromboinflammation
abstract: Thrombotic complications are well-recognized extrapulmonary manifestations of coronavirus disease 2019 .Although initially attributed to virus-specific endothelial injury, increasing evidence suggests that these events are better explained by thromboinflammatory mechanisms involving immunothrombosis.We present two contrasting thrombotic complications observed during acute severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and discuss them within the framework of thromboinflammation and host susceptibility.The first patient was a previously healthy 35-year-old postpartum woman who developed acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, neurological deterioration, reduced ADAMTS13 activity, and a favorable response to therapeutic plasma exchange.Despite hematological recovery, distal ischemic injury resulted in digital amputation.The second patient was a 61-year-old man with a heavy smoking history and a radiologically suspicious pulmonary malignancy who developed acute right femoral artery thrombosis during severe COVID-19 pneumonia, requiring emergency thromboembolectomy.Although revascularization was successful, distal tissue necrosis developed, whereas ischemic manifestations in the remaining extremities resolved with combined medical therapy.Both cases demonstrated distinct thrombotic phenotypes despite a common inflammatory trigger.These contrasting cases support the concept that severe systemic inflammation may produce different thrombotic manifestations according to underlying host susceptibility rather than reflecting a unique SARS-CoV-2-specific vasculopathy.The COVID-19 pandemic provided an unprecedented opportunity to observe diverse thromboinflammatory phenotypes, contributing to a broader understanding of thromboinflammation beyond COVID-19 itself.

media_mentions.content_title: Thrombotic Complications in Patients With Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19): Two Contrasting Clinical Presentations Viewed Through the Concept of Thromboinflammation
media_mentions.content: Abstract Thrombotic complications are well-recognized extrapulmonary manifestations of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). Although initially attributed to virus-specific endothelial injury, increasing evidence suggests that these events are better explained by thromboinflammatory mechanisms involving immunothrombosis. We present two contrasting thrombotic complications observed during acute severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and discuss them within the framework of thromboinflammation and host susceptibility. The first patient was a previously healthy 35-year-old postpartum woman who developed acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, neurological deterioration, reduced ADAMTS13 activity, and a favorable response to therapeutic plasma exchange. Despite hematological recovery, distal ischemic injury resulted in digital amputation. The second patient was a 61-year-old man with a heavy smoking history and a radiologically suspicious pulmonary malignancy who developed acute right femoral artery thrombosis during severe COVID-19 pneumonia, requiring emergency thromboembolectomy. Although revascularization was successful, distal tissue necrosis developed, whereas ischemic manifestations in the remaining extremities resolved with combined medical therapy. Both cases demonstrated distinct thrombotic phenotypes despite a common inflammatory trigger. These contrasting cases support the concept that severe systemic inflammation may produce different thrombotic manifestations according to underlying host susceptibility rather than reflecting a unique SARS-CoV-2-specific vasculopathy. The COVID-19 pandemic provided an unprecedented opportunity to observe diverse thromboinflammatory phenotypes, contributing to a broader understanding of thromboinflammation beyond COVID-19 itself. Introduction Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) was initially recognized as a predominantly respiratory illness characterized by pneumonia and hypoxemic respiratory failure [1]. As clinical experience accumulated, however, it became evident that thrombotic complications represented an important contributor to morbidity and mortality among affected patients [2,3]. Venous thromboembolism, arterial thrombosis, thrombotic microangiopathy-like syndromes, and disseminated intravascular coagulation-like presentations have all been reported across a broad spectrum of disease severity [2-4]. The unprecedented number of critically ill patients during the pandemic provided a unique opportunity to observe these uncommon vascular manifestations more frequently than in routine clinical practice, stimulating extensive investigation into their underlying mechanisms. Early reports proposed that severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) might directly infect endothelial cells through angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptors, resulting in endothelial injury and diffuse endotheliitis [5]. Histopathological studies demonstrating endothelial disruption, microvascular thrombosis, and angiogenesis further supported the concept of COVID-19 as a unique vascular disease [6,7]. Consequently, the terms "COVID-19-associated vasculopathy" and "COVID-19-associated coagulopathy" entered the scientific literature to describe these phenomena [5-7]. However, subsequent evidence suggested that the pathophysiology of thrombosis in COVID-19 is more complex than direct virus-induced vasculopathy alone. Activation of innate immune pathways, excessive cytokine release, complement activation, platelet activation, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and tissue factor expression collectively contribute to a thromboinflammatory state known as immunothrombosis [8-10]. Although these mechanisms promote endothelial dysfunction and coagulation activation, they are not unique to SARS-CoV-2 infection and have also been described in other severe infections and hyperinflammatory conditions [8-10]. Importantly, thrombotic complications during COVID-19 are remarkably heterogeneous. While some patients develop predominantly microvascular manifestations resembling thrombotic microangiopathy, others experience large-vessel arterial thrombosis despite exposure to a similar inflammatory stimulus. These observations suggest that the clinical expression of thrombosis may reflect not only the intensity of systemic inflammation but also the underlying susceptibility of the host [4]. In this report, we present two contrasting cases observed during the COVID-19 pandemic: one patient with thrombotic microangiopathy requiring therapeutic plasma exchange and another with femoral artery thrombosis requiring emergency surgical thromboembolectomy. Rather than interpreting these cases as evidence of a unique COVID-19-specific vasculopathy, we discuss them within the current concept of thromboinflammation, in which a common immunothrombotic response may give rise to distinct clinical presentations according to individual host susceptibility. By integrating these cases with the current literature, we aim to illustrate how the COVID-19 pandemic provided a unique opportunity to advance our clinical understanding of thromboinflammatory vascular disease beyond SARS-CoV-2 infection itself. Case 1 was presented at the 19th Annual Congress of the Society of Turkish Intensivists and the 11th Euro-Asian Critical Care Meeting on November 9-12, 2022 (poster PS-08; J Crit Intensive Care. 2022;13[Suppl 1]). Case 2 was presented at the 18th Annual Congress of the Turkish Society of Medical and Surgical Intensive Care Medicine and the 10th Euro-Asian Critical Care E-Meeting on December 6-9, 2021 (poster PS-02; J Crit Intensive Care. 2021;12[Suppl 1]). Case Presentation Case 1 A 35-year-old previously healthy woman, three months postpartum, presented to the internal medicine department with complaints of fatigue and malaise. Initial laboratory investigations revealed elevated liver enzymes and acute kidney injury, prompting hospital admission for further evaluation. During the first day of hospitalization, she developed progressive dyspnea, and a nasopharyngeal reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test for SARS-CoV-2 returned positive. She was subsequently transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) because of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection with multi-organ involvement. On ICU admission, the patient was conscious but lethargic, with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 12 [11]. Her respiratory rate was 24-28 breaths/min, her blood pressure was 150/90 mmHg, and her heart rate was 96 beats/min in sinus rhythm. Physical examination revealed cyanosis and necrotic changes involving the distal portions of all four extremities (Figure 1). Pulse oximetry failed to detect oxygen saturation because of severe peripheral hypoperfusion. Analgesia and supplemental oxygen therapy (4 L/min via nasal cannula) were initiated. Intravenous unfractionated heparin (5,000 IU) was administered initially, followed by enoxaparin at a dose of 40 mg twice daily. Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrated preserved oxygenation, with a PaO2/FiO2 ratio exceeding 200. Contrast-enhanced thoracic and peripheral computed tomography angiography revealed no evidence of large-vessel arterial occlusion. The constellation of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, and schistocytosis raised suspicion for thrombotic microangiopathy. Differential diagnoses included acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS), postpartum-associated thrombotic microangiopathy, disseminated intravascular coagulation, catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome, and systemic vasculitis. Given the absence of marked coagulation abnormalities and the urgency of treatment, acquired TTP was considered the most likely diagnosis. ADAMTS13 activity testing was requested; however, therapeutic plasma exchange was initiated without awaiting the results because delaying treatment could have resulted in a fatal outcome. Diagnostic investigations supporting thrombotic microangiopathy are summarized in Table 1. Following hematology consultation, daily therapeutic plasma exchange was initiated and continued for five consecutive days. High-dose dexamethasone (40 mg/day) was administered concomitantly as adjunctive immunosuppressive therapy for suspected immune-mediated TTP. Platelet and red blood cell transfusions were avoided unless deemed clinically necessary. Intravenous iloprost infusion was started early to improve peripheral microcirculatory perfusion at a dose of 40 μg/day. On the second day of ICU follow-up, the patient's level of consciousness deteriorated, and she became responsive only to painful stimuli. Endotracheal intubation was performed for airway protection, and invasive mechanical ventilation was initiated. During treatment, renal function progressively improved, liver enzyme abnormalities resolved, and hematological parameters normalized. ADAMTS13 activity was subsequently found to be reduced, further supporting the diagnosis of TTP. The patient was successfully liberated from mechanical ventilation after six days of ventilatory support and was extubated on ICU day 7. She was discharged from the ICU on day 10 and subsequently transferred to the general ward. Following a total hospital stay of 19 days, she was discharged from the hospital. Despite hematological recovery and resolution of organ dysfunction, distal ischemic injury progressed to irreversible necrosis of the affected extremities. The patient ultimately required distal amputation because of persistent ischemic tissue loss. The overall clinical presentation, reduced ADAMTS13 activity, and favorable response to plasma exchange and corticosteroid therapy supported the diagnosis of acquired TTP. The postpartum period likely represented an important host susceptibility factor, whereas concurrent SARS-CoV-2 infection may have served as a potent inflammatory trigger rather than the sole etiologic factor in the development of TTP. Case 2 A 61-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history and no known chronic medical conditions presented to the emergency department with a five-day history of cough, fever, and progressively worsening dyspnea. On admission, his respiratory rate was 28 breaths/min, his peripheral oxygen saturation was 84% on room air, his blood pressure was 130/80 mmHg, his heart rate was 108 beats/min, and his body temperature was 38.3°C. Bilateral inspiratory crackles were auscultated predominantly over the lower lung fields. Chest radiography demonstrated bilateral patchy air-space infiltrates involving the middle and lower lung zones. A well-defined left upper lung opacity suspicious for an underlying pulmonary mass was also evident. Thoracic computed tomography confirmed bilateral peripheral and basal predominant ground-glass opacities consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia and further characterized the left upper lobe lesion as a lobulated spiculated solid mass highly suspicious for primary lung malignancy (Figure 2). Serologic testing was positive for SARS-CoV-2 IgM and negative for IgG, supporting a diagnosis of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The patient was admitted to the ICU because of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring non-invasive mechanical ventilation. Initial treatment consisted of favipiravir, enoxaparin (60 mg twice daily), systemic corticosteroids, nebulized budesonide, supplemental oxygen, and supportive care. On ICU day 3, the patient developed pain, numbness, and coldness in the right lower extremity. Simultaneously, impaired peripheral perfusion and coldness were observed in the left lower extremity and in the distal portions of both hands. Acetylsalicylic acid (100 mg/day), clopidogrel (75 mg/day), and intravenous iloprost infusion (40 μg/day) were added because of progressive ischemic findings. Laboratory findings obtained at the onset of acute arterial thrombosis are summarized in Table 2. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated complete absence of contrast enhancement distal to the right femoral artery, consistent with acute arterial occlusion (Figure 3). Cardiovascular surgery consultation was obtained, and the patient underwent catheter-assisted femoral thromboembolectomy. Following revascularization, aggressive hydration, anticoagulation, and close biochemical monitoring were initiated because of concern for reperfusion injury. Following successful revascularization, the patient developed reperfusion-related metabolic complications requiring temporary continuous renal replacement therapy, from which he subsequently recovered. Despite successful restoration of pulsatile flow in the posterior tibial artery, progressive distal tissue necrosis developed in the right foot. In contrast, the ischemic manifestations involving the left lower extremity and both upper extremities resolved completely with combined anticoagulant, antiplatelet, vasodilator, and supportive therapy. The patient's respiratory status gradually improved during ICU follow-up. Renal function recovered sufficiently to allow the discontinuation of renal replacement therapy, and oxygen requirements progressively decreased. At ICU discharge, persistent distal necrosis of the right foot remained, and reconstructive surgical follow-up was planned. The final diagnosis was acute limb ischemia secondary to right femoral artery thrombosis occurring during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Although histopathological confirmation was unavailable, the coexistence of a suspicious pulmonary malignancy, extensive smoking history, and simultaneous macrovascular and peripheral ischemic manifestations suggests that severe systemic inflammation may have precipitated thrombosis in a susceptible host rather than representing a unique virus-specific vasculopathy. Discussion Thrombotic complications rapidly emerged as one of the most important extrapulmonary manifestations of COVID-19 during the pandemic. Early reports documented unexpectedly high rates of venous thromboembolism, arterial thrombosis, disseminated intravascular coagulation-like syndromes, and thrombotic microangiopathy, leading to the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 might represent a unique vascular pathogen [2-4]. Initial studies emphasized direct viral endothelial injury and endotheliitis; however, subsequent experimental and clinical evidence has shifted the focus toward a broader thromboinflammatory paradigm [8-10]. Endothelial activation, platelet activation, complement dysregulation, NET formation, cytokine-mediated inflammation, and activation of the coagulation cascade are now recognized as interconnected components of immunothrombosis rather than isolated pathological events [8-10]. The two patients presented here illustrate the remarkable clinical heterogeneity of thrombotic complications observed during COVID-19. Although both patients were exposed to the same infectious stimulus, one developed immune-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy requiring therapeutic plasma exchange, whereas the other experienced acute femoral artery thrombosis requiring emergency thromboembolectomy. Rather than representing two unrelated diseases, these contrasting presentations support the concept that thromboinflammation may constitute a common biological process capable of producing distinct clinical phenotypes according to underlying host susceptibility [4,12]. An important implication of these observations is that the clinical expression of thromboinflammation appears to depend not only on the intensity of systemic inflammation but also on underlying host susceptibility [4,12]. In the first patient, the postpartum period may have created an immunological milieu favoring the development of acquired TTP. In the second patient, extensive smoking history together with a radiologically suspicious pulmonary malignancy may have represented a pre-existing prothrombotic substrate upon which acute systemic inflammation precipitated large-vessel arterial thrombosis. From this perspective, SARS-CoV-2 may have acted primarily as a potent inflammatory trigger rather than as the sole etiological factor responsible for either vascular complication [4,12]. This interpretation is supported by observations beyond COVID-19. Similar thrombotic syndromes have long been described in association with influenza, bacterial sepsis, HIV infection, malignancy, autoimmune disorders, and other hyperinflammatory conditions [13]. The biological pathways implicated in these disorders, including endothelial dysfunction, complement activation, platelet activation, and NET-mediated immunothrombosis, are not unique to SARS-CoV-2. Consequently, the central question may be less whether COVID-19 causes a distinct virus-specific vasculopathy and more why the pandemic allowed clinicians to observe such an extraordinary diversity of thrombotic syndromes. The unprecedented scale of the COVID-19 pandemic provides a plausible explanation. Millions of individuals worldwide were simultaneously exposed to a common inflammatory stimulus, allowing relatively uncommon thrombotic disorders to be recognized with unprecedented frequency. In this sense, the pandemic functioned as a natural clinical model through which the broader biology of thromboinflammation became more apparent. Rather than discovering entirely new vascular diseases, clinicians gained a unique opportunity to observe familiar thromboinflammatory mechanisms expressed across diverse vascular beds and clinical settings. Our cases also highlight the close relationship between microvascular and macrovascular thrombosis. title: Comparative Short-Term Clinical Events Associated with Molnupiravir and Ensitrelvir for COVID-19: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using Community Pharmacy Records in Japan
abstract: Molnupiravir and ensitrelvir are widely used for outpatient coronavirus disease 2019 treatment; however, real-world safety comparisons remain limited. This retrospective cohort study evaluated acute clinical event risks over a 29-day follow-up using community pharmacy records from Japanese patients newly prescribed either drug between January and September 2023. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using multivariable Cox proportional hazard models. The analysis included 2051 patients prescribed molnupiravir and 563 prescribed ensitrelvir. Patients prescribed molnupiravir were older and had a higher prevalence of comorbidities than those prescribed ensitrelvir. However, after multivariable adjustment, no significant differences in the risk of major symptoms, such as diarrhea or vertigo, or overall add-on drug prescription were observed between the patient groups. An exception was anti-inflammatory drugs, with a significantly higher risk in the molnupiravir group (adjusted HR: 3.44, 95% confidence interval: 1.07–11.06). These results indicate that while short-term acute clinical event profiles were broadly comparable between molnupiravir and ensitrelvir in routine practice, the differences in add-on prescriptions, combined with the observational study design and limited statistical power in sub-analyses, highlight persistent clinical uncertainty. Our findings provide real-world evidence complementary to that from randomized controlled trials and emphasize the need for larger future studies.

title: Parental COVID-19 vaccine mandates and child COVID-19 vaccination among American Indian and Alaska native peoples in the United States
abstract: Background Adult-directed vaccine policies may have consequences within households. Although emergency COVID-19 mandates have ended, measuring these consequences remains relevant to future outbreak responses and immunization programs. Methods We surveyed 563 American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) parents of children aged 5 years or older at six urban health organizations in January–May 2022. Weighted logistic regression with marginal standardization compared reported child vaccination among unvaccinated parents, parents vaccinated due to a school or workplace mandate, and parents vaccinated for other reasons. Results Reported child vaccination was 8.2%, 65.0%, and 72.4%, respectively. Adjusted risk differences relative to unvaccinated parents were 0.49 (95% CI: 0.38, 0.60) for mandate-vaccinated parents and 0.59 (0.50, 0.68) for other-vaccinated parents. Expanded adjustment attenuated both estimates. The other-versus-mandate difference was 0.10 (−0.01, 0.20), providing no clear evidence of a difference. After excluding children whose own school required vaccination, the mandate-versus-unvaccinated difference remained 0.41 (0.30, 0.53), while the other-versus-mandate difference widened to 0.17 (0.06, 0.28). Conclusions Parental COVID-19 vaccination due to a school or workplace mandate is strongly and positively associated with pediatric vaccination in urban AI/AN communities. Reported child vaccination did not differ statistically between mandate-vaccinated and other-vaccinated parents. Small sample size, unobserved mandate exposure among unvaccinated parents, and unknown vaccination timing preclude estimating a causal mandate effect. Future evaluations of adult-directed immunization policies should measure linked, time-stamped household outcomes.

title: Chinese Responses to COVID-19
abstract: Abstract This chapter probes the lessons that China had learned and failed to learn during the COVID-19 pandemic. It begins by examining China’s learning from SARS and explains how SARS became the primary historical analogy for China’s COVID response in the first two months of the pandemic. The chapter then offers a historical analysis of the four phases of China’s pandemic response and identifies what was learned at the end of each phase. It argues that the most important—and problematic—lesson for the Chinese leadership was the Wuhan lockdown and its perceived effectiveness in suppressing virus transmission. Finally, it evaluates Chinese lessons in light of the propositions advanced in Chapter 2 by paying special attention to the Wuhan lockdown lesson and the zero-COVID policy it engendered.

title: Working Remotely from Home During and Post-COVID-19
abstract: Abstract The chapter reviews and analyzes the merits and challenges of people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States regarding working from home in the post-pandemic period when a return to office was mandated by both governments. Both countries had similar legislation regarding reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. The Equality Act 2010 in the United Kingdom was comprehensive, covering disability as one of nine “protected characteristics.” The US ADA Title I focused exclusively on the employment of people with disability. The UK policy showed much more willingness to regulate the labor market during the pandemic and the post-pandemic period and allowed remote working. The US policy demonstrated less interference in the labor market during the pandemic and post-pandemic. The UK government was concerned with employer pushback on remote working and tended to disproportionally affect workers with disability regarding flexible arrangements. The UK policy recognized the right to flexible work, and employees with disabilities still had stronger protection under the “reasonable adjustment” framework. The US federal policy-imposed return-to-office mandate led to a rise in ADA lawsuits regarding the denial of remote work as a reasonable accommodation. The United States carried out the “essesntial functions” test, meaning the key legal question in many US cases was whether remote work eliminated an “essential function” of the job. Although courts aligned with employers vis-à-vis employees’ claims for working remotely, judges in some circuits started considering an employee’s remote work after the pandemic.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: UK and US Policies Regarding Employees with Disabilities During and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic and in a Few Low-Middle-Income-Countries
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, the United Kingdom and United States prioritized flexible working arrangements and adjustments for employees with disabilities, particularly those at higher risk. In the post-pandemic period, both nations have focused on solidifying these flexible arrangements but have also faced criticism over potentially regressive policies related to disability benefits. The UK approach focused on the expansion of access to work. However, the UK government proposed significant welfare reforms aimed at pushing more people into work. The United States prioritized post-pandemic Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) guidance that solidified the legal precedent for remote work as a reasonable accommodation under the ADA. Employers were required to evaluate renewed requests for remote work based on individual circumstances rather than reverting to pre-pandemic policies. Employers were expected to ensure a safe return-to-office (RTO) process but were not required to eliminate essential job functions to accommodate remote work. Finally, case law in the United States continued to evolve regarding what constituted an “undue hardship” for employers denying remote work, often referencing the successful remote work period during the pandemic. The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected employees with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), exacerbating preexisting inequalities in employment, income, and access to services. Post-pandemic policies required a more comprehensive and systematic approach to address the deeper structural barriers to inclusion.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Caring in the New Normal: The Lived Experiences of Nurse Frontliners in the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the conditions under which nurses delivered care, placing them at the intersection of infection risk, isolation, family concern, and rapidly changing clinical protocols. This phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of six nurse frontliners working in the Philippines and abroad while caring for patients during the pandemic. Participants were purposively selected and interviewed using an in-depth guide. Data were analyzed through a selective phenomenological approach informed by Van Manen, with significant statements clustered into shared meanings. Five themes emerged: living with fear and threat; caring behind barriers; adapting and coping in the new normal; professional growth and resilient caring; and calling for stronger systems of support. Participants described fear of infection, heavy workloads, PPE-related strain, altered therapeutic presence, reliance on faith and relationships, and growth in confidence and compassion. They also emphasized staffing, compensation, preparedness, training, and protective resources. The findings underscore that resilient caring depends on both personal adaptation and supportive health systems.

title: COVID-19-associated coagulopathy and its role in gastroduodenal ulceration
abstract: COVID-19-associated coagulopathy is a major manifestation of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection and is characterized by hypercoagulability, endothelial dysfunction, marked systemic inflammation, and microvascular dysfunction. Despite extensive research on hemostatic abnormalities in COVID-19, the role of COVID-19-associated coagulopathy in gastroduodenal ulcerative lesions complicated by gastrointestinal ulceration and gastrointestinal bleeding remains poorly understood. Objective: To characterize COVID-19-associated coagulopathy in patients with gastroduodenal bleeding and determine the relationships between laboratory hemostatic parameters, the severity of lung involvement, hypoxemia, and the endoscopic characteristics of gastroduodenal ulceration. Material and methods. This retrospective study included 72 patients with COVID-19 pneumonia complicated by gastroduodenal bleeding. The analysis included parameters of primary and secondary hemostasis, markers of systemic inflammation, the extent of lung involvement on computed tomography, oxygen saturation, and the morphological characteristics of the ulcers. Correlation and logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with in-hospital mortality. Patients exhibited pronounced COVID-19-associated coagulopathy, with elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen concentrations, increased C-reactive protein levels, and abnormalities of primary hemostasis. The extent of lung involvement and oxygen saturation were significantly associated with the morphological characteristics of the ulcers. In patients with gastroduodenal bleeding, COVID-19-associated coagulopathy is characterized by both hypercoagulability and hypocoagulability in the setting of pronounced systemic inflammation. The extent of gastroduodenal ulceration is associated not only with laboratory manifestations of coagulopathy but also with the severity of lung involvement, hypoxemia, thrombocytopenia, and ulcer morphometry.

title: Western Responses to COVID-19
abstract: Abstract There were three stages of learning about the COVID pandemic. First came lessons learned from past pandemics, four of which appeared relevant. These lessons were re-evaluated when good data became available about the infectivity and lethality of COVID and the effectiveness of various methods for treating patients. These lessons, their application, and the problems and success of public health responses were then re-evaluated in the aftermath of the pandemic. At each stage of learning, the chapter evaluates the relevance of the propositions developed in Chapter 2. The chapter addresses variation across the West in responses to COVID and the reasons for this variation. It also explores the degree and politicization of public health and its consequences.

title: Comorbilidades y gravedad de la COVID-19 en pacientes hospitalizados: revisión narrativa Comorbidities and severity of COVID-19 in hospitalized patients: a narrative review
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la frecuencia de las comorbilidades en los pacientes hospitalizados por COVID-19 y su relación con la gravedad y la mortalidad. Método: revisión narrativa de literatura indexada en PubMed y SciELO; se seleccionaron 15 documentos: series de casos, cohortes nacionales, metaanálisis y ensayos clínicos aleatorizados. Resultados: la hipertensión, la diabetes y la obesidad fueron las comorbilidades más frecuentes en China, Estados Unidos, México y Perú. Tener una comorbilidad aumentó el riesgo de ingreso en cuidados intensivos, ventilación o muerte (HR 1,79), y tener dos o más, aún más (HR 2,59). La lesión renal aguda afectó al 36,6 % de los hospitalizados, y el buen control glucémico se asoció con menor mortalidad. La dexametasona redujo la mortalidad en quienes requerían oxígeno o ventilación. Conclusión: identificar las comorbilidades al ingreso permite estratificar el riesgo y vigilar las complicaciones renales y metabólicas.
journal: Sanitas. Revista arbitrada de ciencias de la salud

Resultados: la hipertensión, la diabetes y la obesidad fueron las comorbilidades más frecuentes en China, Estados Unidos, México y Perú. Tener una comorbilidad aumentó el riesgo de ingreso en cuidados intensivos, ventilación o muerte (HR 1,79), y tener dos o más, aún más (HR 2,59). La lesión renal aguda afectó al 36,6 % de los hospitalizados, y el buen control glucémico se asoció con menor mortalidad. La dexametasona redujo la mortalidad en quienes requerían oxígeno o ventilación. Conclusión: identificar las comorbilidades al ingreso permite estratificar el riesgo y vigilar las complicaciones renales y metabólicas.

title: Alteraciones hepáticas en pacientes con COVID-19 y estrategias terapéuticas: revisión narrativa Liver abnormalities in patients with COVID-19 and therapeutic strategies: a narrative review
abstract: Objetivo: describir la frecuencia, el significado pronóstico y el manejo terapéutico de las alteraciones hepáticas en pacientes con COVID-19. Método: revisión narrativa de la literatura indexada en PubMed y SciELO entre 2020 y 2022; se seleccionaron 15 documentos: seis estudios observacionales, cinco revisiones y cuatro ensayos clínicos aleatorizados. Resultados: la alteración de las pruebas hepáticas osciló entre el 14 % y más del 50 % de los pacientes hospitalizados, predominó la elevación de aminotransferasas y fue más frecuente en la enfermedad grave. En la India, la mortalidad fue del 19,6 % con disfunción hepática frente al 2,1 % sin ella. La dexametasona redujo la mortalidad en pacientes con oxígeno o ventilación; lopinavir/ritonavir, hidroxicloroquina e interferón no mostraron beneficio. Conclusión: las alteraciones hepáticas son frecuentes y suelen ser transitorias, pero señalan mayor gravedad; su manejo exige vigilancia bioquímica y ajuste de fármacos potencialmente hepatotóxicos.

title: Understandings of Ageism and Healthcare in the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Ageism is widespread and intensified during the COVID-19 pandemic, with resource shortages contributing to healthcare guidelines that systematically deprioritised older adults. Whilst the ethical considerations of these guidelines are well documented, perceptions of age and ageism in healthcare allocation remain underexplored. This study examined younger and older adults' perceptions of age and ageism in healthcare during COVID-19 through a social identity approach. Using a story completion method, 22 older and 41 younger adult participants completed a story about a younger or older COVID-19 patient and doctors allocating the last available ventilator. Using thematic analysis, three themes were developed: (1) age determines health, (2) age determines the value of life, and (3) age determines acceptance of death. Results support the need for policies protecting against the influence of ageism in healthcare systems and emphasise the need to understand how internalised ageism may influence perceptions and health behaviours of older patients.

title: Parental Engagement in the Education of Grade 1 Learners During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The purpose of the research was to explore how parents were engaged in the education of Grade 1 learners during the COVID-19 crisis in the Rakwadu 2 Circuit of Limpopo Province. On the 18th of March 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic led to the abrupt closure of all schools in South Africa. The closure of schools was a good move to prevent the virus from spreading among learners and teachers. The study was grounded in Bronfenbrenner's Ecological Systems theory, and the findings were discussed within this framework. An exploratory research design was used. This qualitative research study was conducted with 8 parents and 4 teachers, and data were collected through semi-structured interviews. The thematic analysis was used to analyse the collected data. Before the researchers gathered data, ethical steps, such as obtaining permission from the Department of Basic Education, principals, and teachers, were taken. Hence, the participants were assured of anonymity, confidentiality, the non-violation of their rights, safety, and no interruption to their teaching responsibilities. The findings demonstrated unique issues of a lack of parent involvement in the school environment. The study suggests that schools must provide practical examples to help parents teach their children at home.

title: Investigation of the physical and emotional status of elderly individuals with and without COVID-19: a cross-sectional study
abstract: AIM: This study aimed to compare balance, functional mobility, activities of daily living (ADLs), quality of life (QoL), fear of COVID-19, and depression between older adults with and without a history of COVID-19, and to explore the associations between physical and emotional outcomes in both groups. METHODS: This observational cross-sectional study included 52 older adults with COVID-19 evaluated during the acute pre-discharge phase and 55 older adults without COVID-19 from the same region. Balance, functional mobility, ADLs, QoL, fear of COVID-19, and depression were assessed using validated measures. Between-group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Age-adjusted ANCOVA was conducted as a sensitivity analysis. Spearman correlations and Fisher's z comparisons examined group-specific associations. RESULTS: Older adults with COVID-19 had poorer balance, functional mobility, and ADLs independence, lower QoL, and higher fear of COVID-19 and depression than controls. These differences remained significant after age adjustment. In the COVID-19 group, fear of COVID-19 and depression were associated with poorer functional mobility, lower balance scores, and lower ADLs independence. Fear of COVID-19 was not associated with physical function in controls. Fisher's z comparisons showed stronger negative associations of depression with functional mobility and ADLs independence in the COVID-19 group. CONCLUSIONS: Older adults recovering from COVID-19 showed coexisting physical and emotional impairments. Physical function and emotional status, particularly depression, functional mobility, and ADLs independence, appear interrelated. Rehabilitation and nursing care should address both physical and psychosocial needs to support functional independence and reintegration into daily life after COVID-19 or similar acute health events.

title: Maternal SARS-CoV-2 exposure and neonatal metabolic maturation during the first month of life: a longitudinal urinary metabolomics study
abstract: Abstract The first month of life is characterized by rapid metabolic adaptation as neonates transition from intrauterine to extrauterine life. Whether maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection influences these developmental trajectories remains largely unexplored. In this longitudinal study, we investigated urinary metabolic trajectories during the first month of life in 48 clinically stable full-term neonates, including 27 infants born to mothers who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 at delivery and 21 unexposed controls. Samples were collected at 0–5 days (T0), 6–15 days (T1), and 19–37 days (T2) postpartum and analysed using 1 H NMR spectroscopy combined with multivariate statistics, covariate-adjusted regression models, and linear mixed-effects models. Across all infants, postnatal age emerged as the primary determinant of metabolic variation, with time-dependent changes involving energy metabolism, amino acid turnover, osmolyte regulation, and host–microbiota co-metabolism. The overall structure of the urinary metabolome was primarily shaped by postnatal maturation rather than maternal SARS-CoV-2 exposure, with exposed and unexposed infants displaying largely overlapping metabolic trajectories. A limited number of metabolic-specific differences were associated to maternal SARS-CoV-2 exposure, with transient deviations that were most evident during the second postnatal week. These changes were modest and not supported by stable correlation networks or enriched metabolic pathways. Overall, these findings indicate that early neonatal metabolic maturation is largely preserved in infants born to SARS-CoV-2–infected mothers, with only subtle and time-restricted modulation of a small subset of metabolites within an otherwise resilient developmental framework. This study highlights the value of longitudinal metabolomics for disentangling physiological maturation from exposure-related effects during early life.

title: Safety of cardiopulmonary exercise testing in patients with severe post-COVID-19 condition: a matched case-control study
abstract: Abstract Patients severely affected by post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) exhibit reduced physical capacity, hyperventilation, and a high susceptibility to post-exertional malaise (PEM). Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is considered the gold standard for objectively assessing physical capacity and for exploring underlying physiological limitations. However, evidence regarding the safety and PEM-associated symptoms following CPET remains limited. This study aims to objectively assess physical capacity using CPET, and to systematically investigate changes in the duration and severity of ten PEM-associated symptoms before and after CPET. A total of 18 PCC patients and 18 healthy controls (matched for sex, age, and body mass index) completed a single maximal, symptom-limited CPET on a cycle ergometer. Ten PEM-specific symptoms were assessed daily for 7 days before and 14 days after CPET (scale 0–10). For clinical characterization, the Canadian Consensus Criteria (CCC) were applied, and the Bell Disability Scale and DePaul Symptom Questionnaire Short-Form-PEM (DSQ-PEM) were completed once before the CPET. Among PCC patients, 61% fulfilled ME/CFS criteria, 67% screened positive for DSQ-PEM, and the mean Bell-Score was 37.8 ± 19.3. Physical capacity was markedly reduced compared with healthy controls (Peak power output: 1.1 vs. 2.4 W/kg, p 30, p = 0.276), or ME/CFS status ( p = 0.523). Severely affected PCC patients showed markedly reduced physical capacity compared with healthy controls. A single maximal symptom-limited CPET induced only a transient, clinically non-relevant symptom increase (1–3 days) without prolonged exacerbation. Furthermore, the results of the CPET can be used to provide individualized objective cut-off values aimed at minimizing PEM during exercise therapy and/or activities of daily living. Trial registration: DRKS, DRKS00032394. Registered 28 July 2023, https//drks.de/search/de/trial/DRKS00032394.

title: Elevated central sensitization inventory scores are associated with a multidimensional symptom profile after coronavirus disease 2019
abstract: Abstract Post-COVID-19 condition comprises persistent heterogeneous symptoms, and central sensitization-related manifestations may overlap with neurocognitive, autonomic, affective, and functional complaints. This cross-sectional study examined associations between Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) scores ≥ 40 and persistent clinical manifestations in 153 adults with symptoms after self-reported COVID-19 who attended an outpatient clinic in southern Brazil during 2021–2022. Anxiety, depressive symptoms, sleep quality, functional status, and post-COVID-19 symptoms were assessed. Robust Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios adjusted for age, sex, education, smoking, body mass index, hypertension and diabetes reported after COVID-19, and hospitalization during acute infection. CSI scores ≥ 40 were observed in 56.2% of participants. In fully adjusted exposure-specific models, elevated CSI scores were associated with brain fog (PR = 1.712; 95% CI 1.185–2.473; p = 0.004), abdominal pain (PR = 1.768; 95% CI 1.206–2.592; p = 0.003), exercise intolerance (PR = 1.533; 95% CI 1.112–2.113; p = 0.009), depressive symptoms (PR = 1.246; 95% CI 1.097–1.416; p = 0.001), and functional limitations (PR = 1.180; 95% CI 1.019–1.368; p = 0.027). Elevated CSI scores were therefore associated with a broad post-COVID-19 symptom profile, although longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal direction and determine whether these associations persist across different clinical populations.

title: Serving Through a Crisis: Mental Health Outcomes and Their Predictors Among Filipino Civil Servants During COVID-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic precipitated a global health crisis, entailing profound disruptions to daily life that substantially affected mental health, particularly among essential workers. However, despite facing similar challenges and limited mental health resources across different occupational groups, civil servants, particularly in Southeast Asia, remain underrepresented in existing research. This study addresses that gap by exploring mental health outcomes and their associated factors among Filipino civil servants. In a sample of 572 Filipino civil servants, findings revealed elevated prevalence rates of mental health problems, with 25.9% likely exhibiting generalized anxiety disorder, 30.6% major depression, and 56.5% high psychological distress. Moreover, several sociodemographic variables and pandemic-related experiences were found to be significant risk factors of generalized anxiety, depression, and distress. These findings provide important information for developing targeted interventions to mitigate the psychological burden on this critical population during public health emergencies.

title: SARS-CoV-2 seeds IAPP aggregation and β-cell failure
abstract: The global diabetes incidence has surged post-COVID-19, yet how SARS-CoV-2 drives long-term beta cell (β-cell) failure remains incompletely elucidated. We identified a mechanism whereby SARS-CoV-2 structural proteins directly hijack islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) to induce pathogenic amyloid deposition, disrupting insulin granule maturation, trafficking, and secretion in an age-susceptible islet microenvironment. In macaque models, aged subjects showed extensive islet IAPP aggregation with increased β-cell necroptosis, whereas adult infected animals exhibited minimal IAPP pathology. Multiplex fluorescence in situ hybridization detecting viral sense and antisense RNAs with IAPP immunostaining revealed focal overlap of active viral replication foci with IAPP-rich amyloid regions in aged islets. Molecular docking was used as a hypothesis-generating tool, whereas coimmunoprecipitation, proximity ligation assays, and surface plasmon resonance experimentally confirmed direct spike/nucleocapsid-IAPP binding; interface-guided peptide mutagenesis further showed that five predicted IAPP contact residues are required for binding. Thioflavin-T kinetics and electron microscopy demonstrated that the spike/nucleocapsid markedly accelerated IAPP monomer conversion into dense fibrillar networks. In β cells and primary hIAPP-overexpressing mouse islets, spike/nucleocapsid expression or protein exposure reduced insulin content and induced endoplasmic reticulum stress and inflammatory programs. Integrated spatial islet proteomics linked IAPP-viral complexes to complement activation and vesicle transport dysfunction. Crucially, primary islet qPCR and immunoblotting revealed stalled insulin mRNA with compensatory upregulation of trafficking/exocytosis transcripts but accumulation of insulin precursor proteins, consistent with impaired granule maturation/processing. Thus, SARS-CoV-2 proteins act as pathogenic "seeds" for IAPP assembly, establishing an IAPP aggregation-impaired granule maturation-complement activation-vesicle transport blockade axis underlying age-associated vulnerability to post-COVID-19 diabetes.

title: Inactivated SARS-CoV-2 Exposure Induces Inflammation and Impairs Reproductive Outcomes in Mice
abstract: COVID-19 has been associated with reproductive dysfunction, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of inactivated SARS-CoV-2 (iSARS-CoV-2) exposure on reproductive outcomes in K18-hACE2 mice. Pregnant females exposed during early gestation showed reduced fetal number, increased resorptions and decreased placental efficiency. These alterations were associated with pulmonary inflammation, characterized by elevated TNF-α, IL-6 and IFN-γ levels and histopathological damage. In males, exposure impaired the sperm count, motility and reproductive performance, and negatively affected pregnancy outcomes in untreated females. Notably, inflammatory responses occurred in the absence of viral replication, indicating that viral components can trigger systemic effects. Together, these findings demonstrate that inactivated SARS-CoV-2 induces inflammation that compromises fertility and gestational success in both sexes.

title: A Peek into the Visual World of Bangladeshi Children During and After the COVID-19 Crisis
abstract: Grounded in visual culture theory and components of visual literacy, this qualitative, arts-based, two-phase study explores the evolving visual culture of six Bangladeshi children during and after the COVID-19 crisis. The child participants, initially fourth-grade students in a Dhaka-based non-formal school during the first phase in 2021, continued their participation through the second phase, which concluded in 2024. In both phases, they created drawings of familiar or favored visual scenes inspired by their surroundings and subsequently engaged in group discussions to explore the meanings behind their representations. The first-phase drawings exhibit a distilled visual lexicon, prominently featuring the spiky coronavirus, masked individuals in protective clothing, and, most conspicuously, a locked and desolate school—graphically conveying their loneliness, confinement, absence of friendship, and pervasive fear of the pandemic. Their reflections extended to multiple visual media, from print to digital, reinforcing a heightened vigilance toward the virus and an overarching sense of awareness. By the second phase, their drawings transitioned to more wonted depictions of children at play, birds, trees, balloons, and, most significantly, an open school —suggesting a profound shift in their visual culture. The findings suggest that visual culture during the pandemic served as a vehicle for conveying the severity of the pandemic while also contributing to increased awareness. In the post-pandemic period, visual culture appeared to facilitate psychological restoration, with the children’s artistic expressions embodying a gradual recuperation from the adversities of COVID-19. Teacher’s World: Journal of Education and Research, 51(1), 31-56

title: Exploratory analysis of innate immune gene polymorphisms and COVID-19 in-hospital mortality in a large admixed Brazilian cohort
abstract: COVID-19 in-hospital mortality varies substantially among patients, suggesting a role for host genetic factors beyond established clinical risk predictors. This case-control study investigated the association of the candidate SNPs rs2241880 ( ATG16L1 ), rs1800450 ( MBL2 ), rs10754558 ( NLRP3 ), and rs12252 ( IFITM3 ), alongside clinical variables, with in-hospital mortality in consecutive hospitalized patients including 505 non-survivors and 535 survivors of acute COVID-19 treated at a public hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, between March and August 2020. Baseline demographic, clinical, and genetic characteristics were compared between groups, and independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariate logistic regression with Firth's penalized likelihood as the primary model to address quasi-complete separation. Deceased patients were significantly older, more frequently male, and had a higher comorbidity burden. In the Firth penalized model, male sex [exp( β ) = 2.30; 95% CI: 1.33–4.02; p = 0.003], immunodeficiency [exp( β ) = 5.06; 95% CI: 1.28–24.6; p = 0.019], and mechanical ventilation [exp( β ) = 136; p < 0.001] were independent clinical predictors of mortality. Nominally significant exploratory associations were observed for the rs2241880 G/G genotype [ ATG16L1 ; exp( β ) = 2.27; 95% CI: 1.09–4.87; p = 0.028] and the rs12252 G/G genotype [ IFITM3 ; exp( β ) = 5.83; 95% CI: 1.02–45.7; p = 0.047] with increased mortality risk, and for the rs1800450 T/T genotype [ MBL2 ; exp( β ) = 0.03; 95% CI: 0.00–0.94; p = 0.047] with reduced mortality risk; however, none of these associations survived correction for multiple testing. No association was observed for rs10754558 ( NLRP3 ). Variant allele frequencies differed significantly across ethnic groups, particularly for rs12252, whose G allele was more frequent in Black (21.6%) than in White (13.9%) patients ( p < 0.001), and a sensitivity analysis adjusting for self-reported ethnicity confirmed the directional consistency of genetic associations with marginally attenuated effect sizes. These exploratory findings suggest that innate immune pathways, including autophagy, antiviral restriction, and complement activation, may contribute to COVID-19 mortality risk in the highly admixed Brazilian population and underscore the importance of conducting genetic studies in populations currently underrepresented in global genomic databases. Replication in larger, multi-ancestry cohorts with matched clinical endpoints is warranted to confirm or refute these signals.

title: Turismo en Portoviejo. Adaptación e innovación pos-Covid-19 Tourism in Portoviejo. Adaptation and innovation pos-Covid-19
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la gestión de la calidad en el turismo de Portoviejo, Manabí, considerando la adaptación e innovación ante las nuevas demandas y tendencias del mercado pos-Covid-19. Metodología: se desarrolló una investigación cuantitativa, no experimental, transversal y descriptiva. Se aplicaron dos encuestas estructuradas, con escala de Likert a 112 representantes de establecimientos turísticos y 196 turistas, seleccionados mediante muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia. Los instrumentos evaluaron la calidad del servicio, la innovación tecnológica, bioseguridad, la capacitación del talento humano y el apoyo institucional. Resultados: entre el 2019 y 2025, la oferta turística registrada aumentó un 5,7%. El 74,11% de los prestadores reconoció los beneficios de las tecnologías y el 57,14% indico que no aplica sistemas formales de gestión de la calidad. El 70,9% de los turistas valoró favorablemente la atención al cliente, sin embargó, el 72,64% consideró necesario fortalecer la innovación tecnológica y el 62,2% no identificó certificaciones visibles. Limitaciones: muestreo por conveniencia, baja disposición para responder los cuestionarios y la ausencia de indicadores sobre demanda, ocupación e ingresos. Conclusiones: las medidas de adaptación implementadas durante y después de la pandemia respondieron principalmente a la continuidad operativa de los establecimientos, sin consolidarse plenamente como una transformación estructural de la gestión de la calidad turística.
journal: Estudios Sociales Revista de Alimentación Contemporánea y Desarrollo Regional

Se aplicaron dos encuestas estructuradas, con escala de Likert a 112 representantes de establecimientos turísticos y 196 turistas, seleccionados mediante muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia. Los instrumentos evaluaron la calidad del servicio, la innovación tecnológica, bioseguridad, la capacitación del talento humano y el apoyo institucional. Resultados: entre el 2019 y 2025, la oferta turística registrada aumentó un 5,7%. El 74,11% de los prestadores reconoció los beneficios de las tecnologías y el 57,14% indico que no aplica sistemas formales de gestión de la calidad. El 70,9% de los turistas valoró favorablemente la atención al cliente, sin embargó, el 72,64% consideró necesario fortalecer la innovación tecnológica y el 62,2% no identificó certificaciones visibles. Limitaciones: muestreo por conveniencia, baja disposición para responder los cuestionarios y la ausencia de indicadores sobre demanda, ocupación e ingresos. Conclusiones: las medidas de adaptación implementadas durante y después de la pandemia respondieron principalmente a la continuidad operativa de los establecimientos, sin consolidarse plenamente como una transformación estructural de la gestión de la calidad turística.

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children’s hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The article refers to “Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3” by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics , multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.

title: Cytokine levels in children with SARS-CoV-2-associated multisystem inflammation syndrome (MIS) according to baseline peripheral blood lymphocyte counts
abstract: Study Objective: To evaluate serum cytokine levels in children diagnosed with SARS-CoV-2-associated MIS-C during the initial phase of the disease process, depending on serum lymphocyte levels. Materials and Methods. A total of 101 children aged 5 to 15 years were examined. Seventy-seven children had a confirmed diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2-associated MIS-C upon hospital admission. Two groups were formed: Group 1 with lymphopenia, Group 2 without lymphopenia, and Group 3 a comparison group. The groups were matched for age. All children underwent determination of the concentrations of cytokines IL-4, IL-6, IL-17A, MCP-1, VEGF in the blood serum. A thorough analysis of the content of the following cytokines: IL-4, IL-6, IL-17A, MCP-1, VEGF in the blood serum showed that despite the fact that the average values of the studied parameters significantly exceeded those in the comparison group, statistically significant differences were not found between the main groups. In addition, a wide range of individual values was revealed in the main groups, regardless of the initial level of lymphocytes. This suggests that the lymphocyte count in peripheral blood at the initial stage of the pathological process is not a significant factor determining the development of the pathogenetic process of MIS-C associated with SARS-CoV-2.

title: Risk Factors for the Development of Fungal Infections in COVID-19.
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in a proportion of hospitalized patients is associated with the development of severe disease and secondary infectious complications, among which fungal infections are of particular clinical significance. However, it remains unclear to what extent their occurrence is determined by comorbid conditions and disease severity versus the effects of anti-inflammatory therapy. To assess the impact of comorbidities and pathogenetic therapy on the development of fungal infections in hospitalized patients with COVID-19. A retrospective single-center observational study was conducted, including 797 patients aged ≥18 years with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 who were hospitalized between 2020 and 2023. Patients were stratified according to the presence of fungal infections. Clinical and demographic characteristics, comorbidities, disease severity, extent of lung involvement based on computed tomography, and features of anti-inflammatory therapy were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed with calculation of odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Fungal infections were diagnosed in 181 (22.7%) patients. Their occurrence was significantly more frequent in older patients, those with severe COVID-19, and those with a pronounced comorbid background (p0.001). In univariate analysis, significant factors included cardiovascular diseases, diabetes mellitus, kidney disease, chronic respiratory diseases, and HIV infection, with the strongest association observed for HIV infection (OR 9.10; 95% CI 2.70–30.70; p0.001) and severe lung involvement (CT-4: OR 4.28; 95% CI 1.95–9.42; p0.001). In the etiological structure, fungi of the genus Candida, predominantly Candida albicans, prevailed, whereas Aspergillus spp. were detected rarely and were associated with extremely severe disease. The use of glucocorticosteroids (OR 3.11; 95% CI 2.12–4.56; p0.001) and interleukin-6 inhibitors was associated with an increased risk of fungal infections in univariate analysis; however, in multivariate analysis adjusted for age, a statistically significant association persisted only for glucocorticosteroids (OR 2.09; 95% CI 1.16–3.74; p=0.014). The development of fungal infections in patients with COVID-19 is associated with age, disease severity, and comorbid conditions. The use of glucocorticosteroids represents an independent risk factor, whereas the observed associations with interleukin-6 inhibitors likely reflect disease severity. The limitations of the study include its retrospective design and single-center setting.

title: MF-59 Adjuvant Alum in an Inactivated SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Model: Focusing on Heterologous Antigen-Binding Response
abstract: Background: Clarifying the role of an adjuvant in vaccine formulation on the induction of a higher cross-reactivity response is very important in the vaccine formulation. In this study, the inactivated Wuhan-Hu-1 strain of SARS-CoV-2 virus was formulated in MF-59 and Alum adjuvants and the immunogenicity of these vaccines in the induction of cellular and humoral immune responses was assessed. In addition, the cross-binding IgG response Alpha variant (B.1.1.7) "English variant" was assessed by ELISA. Methods: Experimental BALB/c mice were immunized subcutaneously three times with MF-59- and Alum-based vaccines. Three weeks after the last immunization, lymphocyte proliferation of spleen cells was evaluated by BrdU method, and IL-4 and IFN-γ cytokines were assessed on the spleen cell culture supernatant by quantitative ELISA kits. In addition, specific total IgG and IgG1/IgG2a isotypes were assessed with an optimized indirect ELISA. Furthermore, the cross-binding IgG titer Alpha variant was assessed by ELISA. Results: The results showed that immunization with MF-59-inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine led to a significant increase in lymphocyte proliferation, IFN-γ-associated responses, specific total IgG, and IgG1, and IgG2a isotypes compared with Alum group. In addition, inactivated SARS-CoV-2-MF59 vaccine revealed a numerically higher (70.83%) increase in the cross-binding IgG titer the inactivated SARS-CoV-2-Alum group. Conclusion: MF-59 could be used as a suitable adjuvant in SARS-CoV-2 vaccine development due to a better induction of IgG and IFN-γ responses than alum adjuvant and a higher induction of the cross-binding IgG response the Alpha variant. These findings showed that vaccine formulation is important in inducing cross-binding responses.

title: Helicase dependence in the host-directed functions of SARS-CoV-2 NSP13: a scoping review
abstract: A scoping review mapping the host proteins, RNA species and signalling pathways that coronavirus NSP13 has been reported to act on, and recording for each one the strongest experimental system used, the region of NSP13 mapped as responsible, and whether dependence on catalytic or nucleic-acid-binding function has been directly tested with mutant protein. The review is prompted by a general claim in the secondary literature that NSP13's host-directed activities are helicase-dependent, a claim supported by mutational experiments for only a subset of the pathways. This project holds the registered protocol, the search records and the screening and extraction data for that review.

title: Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Triggered by Mixed Plasmodium spp. and SARS-CoV-2 Coinfection
abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that may be triggered by infectious diseases, including malaria and viral infections. A case of mixed Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum infection concomitant with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in a patient who developed secondary HLH is described in the present study. Malaria was acquired in the endemic state of Mato Grosso, Brazil, but diagnosed in Macaé, Rio de Janeiro, a nonendemic region. The patient presented with high fever, pancytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperferritinemia. Bone marrow aspirate revealed hemophagocytosis. The patient met six of the eight HLH-2004 criteria and had an HScore indicating a high probability of secondary HLH. Recovery was achieved after the initiation of antimalarial and corticosteroid therapies. This case suggests that parasitic and viral infections may synergistically trigger immunologic “second hits,” promoting macrophage hyperactivation. Recognition of overlapping infections, particularly outside endemic areas, may facilitate earlier diagnosis and timely management of secondary HLH.
journal: The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

title: Assessment of the Association between Myocarditis (New-onset Heart Failure) and COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination
abstract: Introduction: Myocarditis is a rare but significant cardiovascular complication that may occur after receiving COVID-19 vaccines, particularly in younger individuals. The majority of cases have been reported after receiving mRNA-based vaccines, while inactivated and viral vector-based vaccines have been associated with fewer occurrences. Despite this, myocarditis is much more common and results in a poorer prognosis following COVID-19 infection. However, the relationship between myocarditis post-vaccination and its potential mechanisms remains unclear due to limited information. Methods: This study investigated patients with myocarditis (new-onset heart failure) who had received the COVID-19 vaccine and those who had been infected with COVID-19 between March 2021 and March 2023 in Farshchian Cardiovascular Hospital in Hamedan. The data was analyzed using Stata version 14 software and Python. Results: Among 146 myocarditis patients, unvaccinated individuals had higher rates of hypertension, diabetes, obstructive pulmonary disease, and substance abuse, and exhibited more severe cardiac issues like mitral regurgitation and ventricular dysfunction. Vaccinated patients had better lab results and fewer severe symptoms. A model identified advanced age and cardiovascular dysfunction as key mortality risks, suggesting vaccination may mitigate severe cardiac complications and improve outcomes. Conclusion: The findings of this study show that although there is a risk of myocarditis as a side effect following the COVID-19 vaccination, its severity is far less than the occurrence following the COVID-19 infection, with fewer complications and a better prognosis. However, more studies are still necessary to complete the existing findings and clarify their unknown aspects.

title: Reducing Poverty and Income Inequality Through Zakat Redistribution During the COVID-19 Crisis
abstract: Poverty and income inequality remain persistent development challenges across many countries, including those with established zakat management systems. Although zakat is widely recognized as an Islamic social finance instrument capable of improving social welfare, empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of zakat redistribution across different economic conditions, particularly before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic, remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining whether zakat redistribution effectively reduces poverty and income inequality and whether its effectiveness is state-dependent across crisis and recovery regimes. This study employs the Pooled Mean Group Autoregressive Distributed Lag (PMG-ARDL) approach using quarterly panel data from eight countries covering the 2016-2025 period. Quarterly observations were generated through quadratic match-average interpolation. Two empirical models, poverty and income inequality, were estimated while controlling for GDP per capita, inflation, and the Human Development Index. The findings reveal that zakat redistribution exerts a significant negative effect on poverty in both the short and long run, with the strongest long-run impact occurring during the COVID-19 period. Regarding income inequality, zakat redistribution produces a significant long-run negative effect, whereas the short-run effect is significant only for the full-sample estimation. Robustness tests using Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) and Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS) confirm the consistency of the PMG-ARDL estimates. These findings underscore the importance of strengthening zakat governance, collection, redistribution, and digitalization to enhance poverty alleviation and inequality reduction, particularly during future economic crises.

title: Pneumonia incidence, hospitalizations and mortality before and during the COVID-19 pandemic in Peru: An observational study
abstract: Background Pneumonia is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children and older adults. COVID-19 related disruptions in healthcare and surveillance may have altered incidence, hospitalizations, and deaths. We assessed pneumonia incidence, hospitalizations, and mortality rates in children under five and adults older than 60 years in Peru during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020–22) versus the pre-pandemic period (2015–19). Methods We conducted a retrospective population-based time series study using nationwide surveillance system data on reported pneumonia cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in Peru from 2015 to 2022. Age- and region-specific incidence rates (IRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% confidence intervals were estimated for pneumonia cases, hospitalizations, and deaths by comparing the pandemic period (2020–22) with the pooled pre-pandemic period (2015–19). Results Between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2022, 170,558 pneumonia cases were reported among children younger than 5 years and 163,938 among adults aged >60 years in Peru. During the same period, 56,680 and 68,476 hospitalizations and 1,563 and 16,485 deaths occurred in these age groups, respectively. Compared with the pre-pandemic period (2015–2019), pneumonia incidence among children younger than 5 years declined markedly during the pandemic, decreasing by 71% in 2020 (IRR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.28–0.30), 63% in 2021 (IRR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.36–0.38), and 12% in 2022 (IRR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.87–0.90). Hospitalizations and mortality in this group also decreased. In contrast, adults aged >60 years experienced increased hospitalization and mortality rates, particularly in 2021 (hospitalizations: IRR, 2.04; 95% CI, 1.97–2.09; mortality: IRR, 4.28; 95% CI, 4.01–4.57). Substantial regional heterogeneity was observed across Peru. Conclusions During the COVID-19 pandemic, pneumonia epidemiology in Peru showed contrasting patterns by age, with sustained declines in incidence, hospitalizations, and mortality among children younger than 5 years, but increased hospitalizations and mortality among adults aged >60 years, underscoring the need to strengthen surveillance, access to timely care, and vaccination programs.

title: Makroökonomische Maßnahmen zur Stabilisierung der Wirtschaft während der COVID-19-Pandemie
abstract: Zusammenfassung Die COVID-19-Pandemie stellte die Wirtschaftspolitik vor außergewöhnliche Herausforderungen, da Nachfrage-, Angebots- und Unsicherheitsschocks gleichzeitig auftraten. In diesem Beitrag erörtert Rüdiger Bachmann wesentliche makroökonomische Stabilisierungsmaßnahmen in Deutschland und bewertet ihre Wirksamkeit anhand aktueller empirischer Forschung. Im Mittelpunkt stehen der Kinderbonus und die temporäre Mehrwertsteuersenkung von 2020. Die Evidenz zeigt, dass Transfers insbesondere in liquiditätsbeschränkten Haushalten den Konsum erhöhten, während die Mehrwertsteuersenkung vor allem Käufe langlebiger Konsumgüter vorzog und die gesamtwirtschaftliche Nachfrage stabilisierte. Wichtige Fragen zu den Wirkungen der Unternehmenshilfen sowie der Ausweitung des Kurzarbeitergeldes hingegen bleiben offen. Der Autor betont die Bedeutung einer besseren Forschungsdateninfrastruktur für künftiges Krisenmanagement und insgesamt für eine zielgenauere Ausgestaltung fiskalischer Stabilisierungsmaßnahmen.
