title: Comparative Evaluation of the Inactivation of SARS-CoV-2 and Human Coronavirus 229E against Sodium Hypochlorite
abstract: Introduction: Surface disinfection is one of the important non-pharmaceutical intervention measures that help prevent the spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Disinfectants with an efficacy claim against Human Coronavirus strain 229E (HCoV-229E) have been used for the disinfection of SARS-CoV-2; however, the comparative susceptibility of these two viruses to chemical disinfection has not been well defined. To address this, laboratory data were generated to compare the level of inactivation of human coronaviruses HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to a common antimicrobial agent, sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), on a hard non-porous surface. Methods: A hard surface-based Quantitative Method (QM) was used to evaluate the viral inactivation efficacy by three treatments of NaOCl against HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2. For each treatment, viral inoculum containing soil load was applied onto a stainless steel carrier and dried. The inoculated carrier was exposed to NaOCl or a control fluid and held for five minutes. Following the exposure time, a neutralizer was added, and the sample was serially diluted and inoculated onto host cells to determine the number of infective units. The resulting Log10 of the density for control and treated carriers was used to generate Log10 reduction (LR) values for comparative statistical evaluation. Results: The mean LR ± standard error (SE) for HCoV-229E was 0.96 ± 0.09 (n=10) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 2.41 ± 0.15 (n=10) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.54 ± 0.13 (n=10) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. The mean LR ± SE for SARS-CoV-2 was 0.91 ± 0.24 (n=4) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 1.96 ± 0.26 (n=4) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.23 ± 0.16 (n=4) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. Both viruses were significantly responsive to the increasing concentrations of NaOCl. HCoV-229E had slightly higher mean LRs compared to SARS-CoV-2 at each NaOCl concentration; however, these differences were not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.067). Regression analysis using a linear mixed effects model (LMM) also indicates that the susceptibility of HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to NaOCl is comparable. Discussion: Understanding the antimicrobial tolerance of viruses can enhance public health response to viral infections. By determining the tolerance, the most appropriate antimicrobial agent can be chosen to disinfect surfaces contaminated with viral particles. Disinfection of highcontact surfaces can reduce the amount of fomite transmission and limit outbreaks. Conclusion: The data suggest that HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 are statistically comparable in their susceptibility to NaOCl treatments.

title: Assessing COVID-19 transmission patterns and government responses in India
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic initiated its effects in India, the nation with the second-most populous population worldwide, on January 30, 2020. As of December 5, 2021, the cumulative number of confirmed cases of the coronavirus in India stood at 34,633,255. These incidents have arisen as a result of people&s;s lack of awareness regarding the coronavirus. A succession of government directives about the coronavirus was disregarded. As a consequence of the prevailing conditions, India has been struck by two consecutive outbreaks of the coronavirus. The government responded by instituting a nationwide curfew and offering free vaccinations to the general populace. The obstruction engenders a multitude of advantageous and detrimental ramifications for the economic landscape of India, the environment, and the means of subsistence of individuals. This research aims to determine the transmission patterns of COVID-19 across India, assess the economic and ecological consequences, and examine the responses taken by the Indian government.

title: Socio-economic Impacts of COVID-19 on Employment, Income Loss, Food Security, and Social Protection in Pakistan: Evidence from National Survey Data
abstract: This COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted livelihoods, labour markets, and food security worldwide, with particularly adverse consequences for developing countries. This study examines the socio-economic impacts of COVID-19 on people’s well-being in Pakistan by analysing nationally representative secondary data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics’ Special Survey for Evaluating the Socio-economic Impact of COVID-19 on People’s Well-being (2020). Using a two-stage stratified random sample of 31,022 households, the study employs descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis to investigate the effects of job loss due to migration, household coping strategies, and social protection programs on unemployment, income loss, and food insecurity. The findings reveal that job loss and coping strategies significantly increased unemployment, income loss, and food insecurity during the pandemic. Social protection programs, primarily cash transfer schemes, showed limited effectiveness in mitigating these socio-economic hardships, reflecting structural weaknesses in coverage, targeting, and support for informal-sector workers. The study concludes that short-term cash assistance alone is insufficient to address large-scale socio-economic crises and emphasises the need for comprehensive labour-market interventions, targeted welfare reforms, and inclusive social protection systems. These findings provide important policy insights for strengthening crisis governance and socio-economic resilience in Pakistan and similar developing economies.

title: Модель прогноза отсутствия постковидных гастроинтестинальных нарушений у детей, перенесших инфекцию COVID-19
abstract: Введение.После выздоровления от COVID-19 у многих пациентов наблюдаются долгосрочные последствия, известные как постковидный синдром. Растущий интерес вызывает роль изменений микробиоты кишечника, особенно в связи с желудочно-кишечными симптомами после COVID-19, хотя данные об этих изменениях в постковидный период остаются противоречивыми.Цель— на основании клинико-анамнестических, молекулярно-биологических и иммунологических методов выявить основные предикторы отсутствия гастроинтестинальных симптомов в постковидный период у детей.Материалы и методы.Создана база данных, которая включала более 400 признаков, характеризующих общие сведения, клиническую картину, лабораторные данные, в том числе уровень прокальцитонина и C-реактивного белка, 16S секвенирование микробиоты, определение зонулина, ПЦР кала на вирус SARS-Co V-2, анализ назначения антибиотиков и синбиотика. Анализ проводился в двух группах пациентов. Группа 1 — 24 ребенка, у которых через месяц после выздоровления появились желудочно-кишечные симптомы, группа 2 состояла из 23 пациентов, не имевших никаких гастроэнтерологических симптомов.Результаты.С помощью нейронной сети выделены пять признаков, сопровождающих отсутствие постковидных гастроинтестинальных симптомов у детей через месяц после выздоровления от новой коронавирусной инфекции. Чувствительность нейронной сети составила 95,0%, специфичность — 87,5%, точность — 91,0%.Заключение.Основные предикторы отсутствия гастроинтестинальных симптомов в постковидный период у детей — это относительная доляActinobacteriotaменее 0,24 в стуле методом 16S секвенирования через месяц после выздоровления, наличие видаА ctinobacteriaменее 0,1 в стуле методом 16S секвенирования через месяц после выздоровления, лечение синбиотиком в течение 30 дней, нормальный уровень зонулина в стуле, отсутствие пищевой аллергии в анамнезе. Introduction.After recovery from COVID-19, many patients experience long-term sequelae known as post-COVID syndrome. The role of changes in the gut microbiota, particularly in relation to gastrointestinal symptoms following COVID-19, is of growing interest, although data on these changes in the post-COVID period remain controversial.Aim— to identify the main predictors of the absence of gastrointestinal symptoms in the post-COVID period in children using clinical, anamnestic, molecular biological, and immunological methods.Materials and methods. A database was created that included over 400 characteristics characterizing general information, clinical presentation, laboratory data, including procalcitonin and CRP levels, 16S microbiota sequencing, zonulin determination, stool PCR for SARS-Co V-2, and analysis of antibiotic and synbiotic prescriptions. The analysis was conducted in two groups of patients. Group 1 included 24 children who developed gastrointestinal symptoms one month after recovery, while Group 2 consisted of 23 patients who had no gastrointestinal symptoms.Results.Using a neural network, five features were identified that predict the absence of post-COVID gastrointestinal symptoms in children one month after recovery from novel coronavirus infection. The sensitivity of the neural network was 95.0%, specificity 87.5%, and accuracy 91.0%.Conclusion.The main predictors of the absence of gastrointestinal symptoms in the post-COVID period in children are the relative proportion of Actinobacteriota less than 0.24 in stool by 16S sequencing one month after recovery, the presence of Actinobacteria species less than 0.1 in stool by 16S sequencing one month after recovery, treatment with a synbiotic for 30 days, normal zonulin levels in stool, and the absence of a history of food allergies.

title: Party capacity, state capacity, and pandemic governance: a fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis of COVID-19 prevention and control outcomes in 52 African countries during the early stage
abstract: During the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic in Africa, from March to May 2020, significant variations emerged among countries regarding the implementation of containment policies. During this period, viewed strictly from a public health perspective, social distancing and lockdowns were considered critical for curbing transmission. However, epidemic control outcomes varied considerably across countries. This variation raises questions about the independent and interactive influence of socioeconomic conditions on these outcomes, and about how political factors, including state capacity and party politics, moderate or mediate these influences, especially in resource-constrained contexts. This article employs fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) with 52 African countries as case studies to investigate the combination of conditions for COVID-19 containment success. The analysis reveals three equifinal configurations: a party-led high-risk response pathway, an administrative compensation pathway, and a coercive compensation pathway. Party capacity is not a generally applicable determinant; its role is contingent upon the specific governance context. Under the structural constraint of healthcare deficiency, distinct dimensions of state capacity operate through differentiated compensatory mechanisms. The paper makes two theoretical contributions: conceptualizing party capacity as a crisis-contingent rather than a generalized governance asset, and disaggregating state capacity into administrative and coercive dimensions with distinct compensatory functions. It also makes a methodological contribution by adopting a configurational approach that examines combinations of conditions rather than the net effects of individual factors.

title: COVID-19 patent publications in WIPO PATENTSCOPE: A bibliometric analysis
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has driven innovation activities around the world. This study investigated COVID-19-related patents from the WIPO PATENTSCOPE database between December 2019 and September 2025, focusing on publication trends, technology focus, applicant characteristics, and geographic distribution. The bibliometric indicators of the study included International Patent Classification (IPC) codes and word frequency analysis of patent titles and abstracts. 14,834 COVID-19-related patent publications were retrieved. The results showed a peak in publications in 2021, followed by a decline. China (5,131) and the United States (1,624) had the highest number of national patent publications, while published PCT applications reached 4215 publications. Academic and public research institutions were also major applicants. The IPC analysis revealed that most patent publications focused on pharmaceutical, therapeutic, and molecular biology technologies. The top IPC codes were A61K (7,180), A61P (5,996), and C12N (3,440). Healthcare informatics (G16H) had the lowest share among the top ten IPC codes. The findings reveal a geographically concentrated pattern of COVID-19-related patent publications and the dominance of pharmaceutical and biomedical technologies during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Leadership behavior, employee engagement, and retention: lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic in the hospitality industry
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in organizational workforce structures, particularly in the hospitality industry, where unemployment peaked at 39.3% in April 2020 before a turbulent recovery. As organizations worked to rebuild their workforces, questions about which leadership behaviors sustain employee engagement and promote retention became strategically urgent. This study examines how leadership behavior influences employee engagement and, in turn, employee retention in the hospitality context, reflecting on lessons from the pandemic experience. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from N = 223 employed participants across 13 countries via social media recruitment. Leadership behavior was measured using the 48-item Managerial Practices Survey, employee engagement using the 17-item Utrecht Work Engagement Scale, and retention using a three-item intention-to-remain scale. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) assessed construct validity. Mediation and moderated mediation analyses tested the indirect effect of leadership on retention through engagement, with industry (hospitality vs. non-hospitality) and employee age as moderators. CFA supported construct validity, with the proposed three-factor model providing the best fit among the models tested (RMSEA [90% CI] = 0.042 [0.026, 0.056], CFI = 0.982, TLI = 0.979, SRMR = 0.031). Leadership behavior significantly predicted employee engagement (β = 0.562) and retention (β = 0.205), and engagement mediated the leadership-retention relationship. Decomposing the leadership composite showed task-oriented behavior was the only significant predictor of engagement. The indirect effect of task-oriented leadership on retention through engagement was significant in both hospitality [IE = 0.421, 95% CI (0.269, 0.605)] and non-hospitality contexts [IE = 0.211, 95% CI (0.119, 0.344)], and was stronger in the hospitality industry, according to the significant index of moderated mediation [IMM_IE = 0.209, 95% CI (0.076, 0.392)]. The direct effect of leadership on retention was significantly stronger for older employees, while the indirect effect through engagement was significant across all age groups and somewhat larger for younger workers, though the formal moderation test did not reach significance. Dedication emerged as the primary engagement dimension through which leadership was associated with retention. Task-oriented leadership appears to support retention primarily by sustaining employee dedication, an effect amplified in hospitality settings. These findings offer guidance for post-pandemic leadership development and retention strategy in high-turnover industries.

title: Cardio-pulmonary vascular deficits and progression to overt ischemic syndromes in ambulant long-COVID population
abstract: Predilection and progression of perfusion defects to overt ischemic syndromes including sudden deaths, two years post COVID illness, was evaluated prospectively among 133 ambulant participants, using nuclide imaging to visualize the cardio-pulmonary vasculature. A tiered or graded cost-effective diagnostic approach for resource optimization was used. At enrollment, any myocardial perfusion defect in the nuclide imaging was detected among 22/61 (36.06%) and 30/72 (41.66%) in the non-severe and severe COVID-19 participants respectively, ( p = 0.51); spontaneously resolving in 32/52 (61.5%). Five participants with pre-existing comorbidities required intervention, with one among them succumbing. Risk factors for occurrence of myocardial perfusion defects in the multivariate regression {adjusted relative risk (95% CI} were persisting breathlessness: 1.17 (1.04, 1.32), Cardiac Ejection fraction: 23 kg/m 2 : 1.29 (1.1, 1.51) and new-onset comorbidities post-COVID-19: 1.16 (1.02, 1.32). Two participants in the severe group had pulmonary vascular defects with intact myocardial perfusion. We conclude that cardio-pulmonary vascular defects, visualized in advanced imaging, progressing to major cardiac events de-novo, due to COVID-19 per se, two years post COVID-19 illness, was uncommon. Perfusion defects resolved over time without any active intervention in a majority, unless driven by pre-existing comorbidity or unattended cardiac injury sustained during acute illness.

title: Conformational dynamics and energetic landscape of the SARS-CoV-2 nsp12 with and without accessory proteins: new insights on this potential therapeutic target against COVID-19
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 replication-transcription complex (RTC) represents a key antiviral target, yet the conformational dynamics underlying its function remain insufficiently characterised. While cryo-EM structures resolve the architecture of the nsp12 polymerase and its nsp7/nsp8 cofactors, they do not capture the motions governing catalysis and RNA engagement. In this study, independent triplicate 300 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations (nine trajectories, 2.7 μs aggregate) were conducted for nsp12 in three assembly states: isolated nsp12-RNA, the central RTC and the nsp13-containing mini-RTC. Across replicas, cofactors consistently reduced nsp12 flexibility, particularly in the interface domain and thumb subdomain, while maintaining catalytic-site geometry. MM/GBSA analysis identified electrostatic interactions as the primary determinants of RNA recognition and delineated a reproducible set of RNA-contact hotspots. When the receptor was fixed as nsp12, cofactors produced only a modest increase in nsp12-RNA interaction strength, within the range of replica-to-replica variability. Thus, their principal influence appears to be on the dynamics rather than on static binding energetics. The simulations also consistently predicted R914 as a persistent favourable contact with the product-RNA strand, a feature not highlighted in prior static analyses. This observation is presented as a hypothesis for experimental validation and structure-based antiviral design.

title: Livelihood vulnerabilities among women in the bushmeat trade in Ghana during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The bushmeat trade is a significant source of employment for women in Ghana; providing income-generating opportunities and supporting household livelihoods. However, there is a paucity of research on how the COVID-19 affected these women. Using qualitative data, this paper examines the livelihood vulnerabilities of women bushmeat traders during the COVID-19 pandemic. Drawing on their lived experiences, the study highlights interrelated factors shaping their vulnerability, including the association of the commodities with zoonotic diseases, the perishable nature of the commodity, limited economic resources, and weak protection systems. Despite these challenges, the women demonstrated resilience and agency in sustaining their livelihoods. The paper recommends that policy makers incorporate the needs of women bushmeat traders into interventions aimed at reducing vulnerability and sustaining their livelihoods.

abstract: La pandemia de COVID-19 generó un impacto profundo en la salud bucal infantil debido al confinamiento, alteraciones en la dieta y la disminución de la higiene bucodental (Tervonen et al., 2022). Este estudio tiene como objetivo general: evidenciar el impacto de la pandemia de COVID-19 en el desarrollo y progresión de la caries dental en la población infantil (Machiulskiene et al., 2020). Los objetivos específicos são: analizar cómo las alteraciones dietéticas adoptadas durante el confinamiento agravaron el deterioro del sistema estomatognático (Encalada-Torres & Castro-Sipán, 2023). Asimismo, la presente revisión narrativa evidencia cómo el estrés psicosocial, la hiperactivación del eje hipotalámico-hipofisario-adrenal y el cierre de consultorios crearon un ecosistema oral altamente cariogénico (Scorca et al., 2021). Asimismo, se analiza la sinergia de microorganismos pospandemia, tales como Candida albicans, Streptococcus mutans y Scardovia wiggsiae, los cuales han exacerbado la progresión de la caries (Francis et al., 2025; Tanner, 2024). Las estadísticas locales muestran un incremento alarmante de esta enfermedad en la población infantil ecuatoriana (Ministerio de Salud Pública, 2024).

title: Impacto da pandemia de Covid-19 na saúde mental de profissionais de enfermagem: revisão narrativa da literatura Impacto de la pandemia de Covid-19 en la salud mental de los profesionales de enfermería: una revisión narrativa de la literatura Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mental health of nursing professionals: a narrative literature review
abstract: Este artigo tem como objetivo identificar, na literatura, o impacto da pandemia na saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem durante a pandemia do Covid-19. Para tanto, desenvolveu-se uma revisão narrativa da literatura nas bases de dados do Portal Unique, no período de 2020 a 2023, a partir dos descritores “saúde mental” AND “qualidade de vida” AND “profissionais de saúde” AND “pandemia Covid-19”. Posteriormente, foram aplicados os filtros: “texto completo”, idioma “português”. Na última etapa da análise foram aplicados os filtros “enfermagem” “enfermeiros” e “técnicos de enfermagem”. Após a avaliação dos materiais foram identificados 5 artigos que atendiam aos objetivos. A análise dos estudos selecionados identificou três categorias de análise: Sobrecarga de trabalho e esgotamento profissional; Ansiedade, depressão, estresse e sofrimento psíquico; Condições de trabalho e fatores institucionais. Os resultados indicam que a pandemia impactou na saúde mental dos profissionais de enfermagem, sendo necessárias novas pesquisas para investigar a persistência ou reversibilidade dos impactos psicológicos e ocupacionais no período pós-pandêmico.
authors: Maria João Sousa Pinto dos Santos

title: Competing Risk Prediction of COVID-19 Hospital Mortality with Model Diagnostics and Exploratory Evaluation in Mexico
abstract: Background/Objectives: We evaluated six-predictor cause-specific models for 45-day in-hospital COVID-19 mortality, including departures from proportional hazards and linearity and transport to Mexican data. Methods: The oxygenation-expanded Barcelona cohort included 1622 adults. Recorded arterial PaO2/FiO2 (P/F) was preferred; otherwise P/F was derived from documented saturation and inspired oxygen using the Rice relationship at SpO2 ≤ 97%. Linear cause-specific Cox models for death and discharge served as a reference. Quadratic and time-varying extensions were assessed by three repetitions of five-fold cross-validation. Frozen Barcelona models were evaluated in a separate Mexican workbook using reconstructed day-45 outcomes and minimum-oxygenation proxies. Historical supplied scores for 634 patients were analysed separately. Results: Barcelona included 325 day-45 deaths. The reference model had apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.822 and bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.820. Proportional hazards (PH) departures persisted within 45 days. Combining quadratic terms and predictor-by-log(1 + time) interactions improved cross-validated AUC from 0.819 to 0.831 and Brier score from 0.12343 to 0.11974, while calibration slope decreased from 0.945 to 0.830. In 171 Mexican records with 12 reconstructed deaths, AUC was 0.967 for the expanded linear model and 0.857 for the combined extension. Excluding one extreme lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) record yielded 170 patients, 11 deaths, and AUCs of 0.964 and 0.935, respectively. The combined model predicted 17.8% mortality against 6.5% observed in that subset. Conclusions: Flexible effects improved some internal metrics but did not establish an adequate replacement model. Residual misspecification, extrapolation and incompatible predictor timing limit transportability. The calculator implements the linear reference model; definitive admission-time external validation remains necessary.

title: Prescribing Appropriateness and Clinical Outcomes in Hospitalized Adults with COVID-19 in Jazan, Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic required repeated revision of national treatment protocols; evaluating prescribing against the guidance then in force is central to stewardship. Objective: To characterize clinical outcomes of adults hospitalized with COVID-19 in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, and to assess prescribing appropriateness using the Medication Appropriateness Index (MAI) benchmarked against contemporaneous Ministry of Health (MOH) guidance. Methods: Single-center retrospective cohort study of all adults (aged 18 years or over) admitted with COVID-19 between 1 March 2020 and 28 February 2021. Two trained clinical pharmacists independently applied the MAI to 1018 prescriptions. All associations were examined in univariable, unadjusted analyses. Results: Hypertension (44.1%), diabetes (38.7%), end-stage renal disease (13.7%), and cardiac disease (12.4%) were prevalent. In-hospital mortality was 26.8% (121/451 patients with a determinate outcome). Diabetes (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.32–3.08), hypertension (OR 1.92, 95% CI 1.26–2.93), and cardiac disease (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.15–3.64) were each associated with higher unadjusted odds of death; patients who died were on average 15.8 years older (p < 0.0001). Overall, 936 of 1018 prescriptions (91.9%) were appropriate; rates ranged from 99.4% (311/313) for enoxaparin to 42.9% (6/14) for hydroxychloroquine, the latter based on a small number of prescriptions. Inappropriate prescriptions were flagged mainly in the duration (82.9%) and indication (70.7%) domains, and receipt of at least one inappropriate prescription was not associated with mortality (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.31–1.12; p = 0.10). Conclusions: Anticoagulants and corticosteroids were largely prescribed in line with contemporaneous MOH guidance; several repurposed agents were not. These findings support an MAI-based audit against the guideline version in force as a tool for quality control.

title: Longitudinal analysis of Covid-19 vaccine hesitancy and its determinants in Poland
abstract: Introduction and Objective. Vaccine hesitancy is dynamic, with longitudinal evidence beyond two waves scarce. The aim of the study is to characterise, across a four-wave Polish panel (2021–2025), how stated vaccination intentions translate into actual vaccination, and to identify modifiable determinants of persistent non-vaccination versus delayed conversion. Materials and Method. 4,205 wave records from 2,559 unique Polish adults (Rise or Fall [ROF] panel, 2021/2022/2024/2025) were harmonised. The analytical cohort (n=859, ≥2 waves) was classified into five trajectory classes: Baseline vaccinated, Early convert, Late convert, Persistent unvax willing (PuW), and Persistent unvax hesitant (PuH; reference). Predictors were identified by Multinomial logistic regression and discrete-time hazard models. By 2025, 83.4% of baseline-willing respondents were vaccinated vs. 38.9% of baseline-hesitant – a 44.5-percentage-point gap nearly identical to 2022 (45.7 pp). Persistent non-vaccination tracked higher fear of side-effects (hazard OR=0.63 per point; p<0.001) and conspiracy beliefs (OR=0.79; p<0.001); a Bachelor’s degree raised the conversion hazard 2.6-fold (p<0.001). Low fear emerged as a strong predictor of Baseline vaccinated (OR=6.0) and Early convert (OR=3.0). PuW had the highest mean HLS-Q12 (3.04; omnibus p=0.040), with a borderline multinomial association (OR=1.56; p=0.077); HLS-Q12 robustly predicted lower vaccination hazard (OR=0.58; p=0.001). Vaccine hesitancy in Poland is durable; the willing/hesitant behavioural gap persists. Post-rollout strategy should combine safety-centred dialogue targetting fear of side-effects with structural facilitators for the willing-but-unvaccinated subgroup.
journal: Annals of Agricultural and Environmental Medicine

title: Future Jobs for People with Disabilities Post-COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Technology was the driving force behind future employment for people with disabilities and created opportunities, but it posed challenges regarding the gap between PWD and people without disabilities. Driven largely by the expansion of remote and hybrid work, current employment rates for PWD saw remarkable gains, even outpacing those of nondisabled workers in some sectors. The call of post-pandemic RTO mandates could erode the progress in flexibility of work and technology achieved by PWD in term of progress in the labor market during the pandemic in the United Kingdom and United States. In both countries, the legal framework encourages this kind of flexible working as a potential reasonable accommodation/adjustment, though the United Kingdom had implemented more explicit, universal rights to request it. The second half of the chapter examines the role of AI as a potential to enhance future work opportunities for workers with disabilities in both the United Kingdom and the United States through advanced assistive technologies and flexible work options. However, the realization of this potential could heavily be contingent on proactive policy and regulatory frameworks in each country to address inherent biases in AI-powered hiring tools and government systems. The post-pandemic labor market offered some potential for positive change, largely driven by technological shifts. However, despite the opportunities, the economic situation in many LMICs stayed the same or even worsened. In many of these countries the lack of robust, disability-inclusive policies and social safety nets would make individuals with disabilities vulnerable to economic shocks.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Employment for Persons with Disabilities in the Twenty-First Century Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Prior to the pandemic, both the United Kingdom and United States saw increasing employment rates for people with disabilities, driven by policy shifts, strong economies, and rising self-reporting of disabilities. However, significant employment gaps persisted, and workers with disabilities often faced inequality in pay, opportunities, and workplace accommodations. There was a steady increase in the number of people with disabilities who worked in the United Kingdom between 2013 and 2019. However, the gap between disabled and nondisabled people narrowed, but a substantial disparity remained. Despite improvements, workers with disabilities still faced notable inequalities. They were more likely to be in part-time work and lower-skilled occupations. Prior to the pandemic, employees with disabilities were more likely to face discrimination, leading to lower wages, fewer opportunities for advancement, and a lack of necessary accommodation. Employment for people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States had seen significant shifts in the twenty-first century, particularly shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic. While pre-pandemic efforts showed some progress, the pandemic temporarily reversed trends before accelerating new opportunities, most notably the expansion of remote work. For workers with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), the COVID-19 pandemic amplified preexisting systemic disadvantages. While the pandemic caused widespread job loss, workers with disabilities, who were already disproportionately in the informal sector, suffered more severe economic impacts. Post-pandemic, recovery has been uneven, with some progress seen through remote work, but the employment gap persists.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: IMPACT OF COVID-19 ON THE PRICE OF PORK FOR THE PRODUCER IN MEXICO: AN INTERVENTION ANALYSIS MODEL
abstract: Pork (Sus scrofa domesticus) is a source of protein and minerals in the Mexican diet, with significant national production and high demand. Following the declaration of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020, the aim of this research was to quantify its impact on the average monthly price paid to producers for pork carcasses in Mexico. The hypothesis suggested the existence of a structural change in the price paid to pork carcass producers, resulting in a negative effect on producers in this sector. Statistical analysis was performed using Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and intervention models to detect structural changes and atypical values, or outliers. The results showed a structural change in April 2020 caused by the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. The model that best represented the behavior of the analyzed time series was an intervention model that included structural changes and atypical values. This model estimated the behavior of prices in the absence of the pandemic. Pork carcass producers experienced an estimated loss of MXN 12,428.78 million during the pandemic, demonstrating its direct economic impact on the pork sector. title: The Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Children and Adolescents
abstract: Chapter 2 addresses the situation of children and adolescents during the pandemic. It documents children’s and adolescents’ rates of illness and shows that in contrast with some other respiratory epidemics young people did not have high rates of morbidity or mortality during the COVID-19 epidemic. However, children and adolescents were deeply harmed in other ways. The impact of the pandemic on children’s and adolescents’ mental and emotional well-being was severe and likely long-term. The pandemic led to a higher rate of children being orphaned and increased the loss of caregivers. Pandemic school closures in the United States and elsewhere in the world along with the inadequacies of remote learning also set students back significantly in their educational progress. Particularly problematic, schools often remained closed longer in low-income communities resulting in widened inequalities that left students in poor communities at a greater relative disadvantage than they were before the pandemic.

title: Psychotropic prescribing trends in a Peruvian General Hospital during and after the COVID-19 pandemic: an interrupted time-series analysis
abstract: To evaluate trends in psychotropic prescription rates (PRs) in a Peruvian general hospital during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. We conducted an interrupted time-series (ITS) study using routinely collected clinical data from hospitalized patients with psychiatric diagnoses between September 2020 and December 2024. Psychotropic PRs, defined as the number of weekly psychotropic prescriptions per 1,000 psychiatric consultations, were calculated overall and by subclass: antidepressants (N06A), antipsychotics (N05A), anxiolytics (N05B), and mood stabilizers (N05AN01/N03A). For ITS analysis, the study period was divided into six predefined phases (two waves, three relaxation phases, and one post-pandemic phase) based on COVID-19 mortality and transmission trends in Peru. Segmented regression models were applied to estimate phase-specific level and slope changes. A total of 6,151 patients were included. The overall psychotropic PR was higher during the post-pandemic period compared with the pandemic period (1,308 vs. ITS analyses showed a significant downward trend in overall psychotropic prescribing during phase 1 (post-first wave stabilization, β = −25.53; 95% CI = −43.82 to −7.01; p = 0.007), followed by a structural break in phase 2 (second pandemic wave) with an abrupt level increase (β = 295.53; 95% CI = 60.48 to 530.57; p = 0.014) and slope reversal (β = 23.79; 95% CI = 3.33 to 44.26; p = 0.016), after which prescribing stabilized. A similar temporal pattern was observed for antidepressant PR. Anxiolytic PR displayed a transient upward slope change in phase 2 (β = 14.15; 95% CI = 1.80 to 26.50; p = 0.01), whereas antipsychotic and mood stabilizer prescribing remained stable across phases. Overall psychotropic prescribing showed phase-specific disruption followed by structural rebound and subsequent stabilization across the COVID-19 and post-pandemic periods. These findings provide real-world evidence and underscore the need to monitor psychiatric prescribing and mental health service adaptation in middle-income settings.

title: Maternal COVID-19 During Pregnancy and Offspring Neurodevelopmental Disorders
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) during pregnancy was common during the pandemic. However, its potential risks for clinically diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorders in offspring, including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID), remain uncertain in Asian populations. We examined the association between maternal COVID-19 during pregnancy and diagnoses of neurodevelopmental disorders in offspring. METHODS: This nationwide birth cohort study included 108,148 singleton children, contributing 224,965 person-years, using a nationwide administrative claims database from 2020 to 2024. We investigated the association between maternal COVID-19 during pregnancy and offspring neurodevelopmental outcomes, including ADHD, ASD, ID and a composite outcome, using Cox proportional hazards models, with primary analyses based on time-dependent propensity score (PS) matching. The robustness of the primary findings was evaluated through adjusted models, sibling comparison, trimester-specific analyses and sensitivity analyses for outcome misclassification. RESULTS: Among 108,148 children, 7797 (7.2%) were exposed to maternal COVID-19 during pregnancy; PS matching yielded 7679 matched pairs contributing 22,360 person-years with well-balanced covariates. In PS-matched analyses, maternal COVID-19 was not associated with composite neurodevelopmental outcomes (hazard ratio [HR], 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-1.66), ADHD (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.32-1.78), ASD (HR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.40-1.55), or ID (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.55-2.01). Adjusted models, sibling comparisons, trimester-specific analyses and sensitivity analyses addressing outcome misclassification yielded similar null findings. CONCLUSIONS: We found no evidence of an increased risk of offspring neurodevelopmental disorders following maternal COVID-19 during pregnancy during the available follow-up period.

title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. Findings: Sustainability performance (ESG scores) significantly enhanced stock resilience during the pandemic. However, this protective effect dissipated post-pandemic. Results confirm a statistically significant improvement in overall resilience following the crisis, as investors redirected their focus toward traditional financial fundamentals such as profitability and leverage. Conclusion: Sustainability performance acts as situational crisis insurance. Its risk-mitigation value is highly salient during systemic uncertainty but diminishes under stable market conditions. Novelty/Originality of this article: Unlike prior single-phase studies in developed economies, this research provides longitudinal evidence on the dynamic, state-dependent nature of sustainability performance across crisis and recovery phases within Southeast Asia’s early-stage ESG landscape.

title: An unusual trigger for a rare hemolytic anemia: paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria after shingles and COVID-19
abstract: Paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria (PCH) is a rare autoimmune hemolytic anemia that commonly presents as a transient, post-infectious disease mediated by biphasic Donath-Landsteiner antibodies, which bind to red blood cells at cold temperatures but cause hemolysis at core body temperature. PCH is less common in adults but can be a complication of infection or hematologic malignancy. One viral trigger of PCH that has rarely been described is that of primary varicella-zoster virus (VZV). Here, we report the case of a 69-year-old man who developed severe PCH following an episode of shingles, raising the possibility of a temporal relationship between PCH and VZV reactivation. Erythrophagocytosis and rosetting of red blood cells around neutrophils, smear findings commonly seen in PCH, were observed on the patient’s blood smear and aided in our diagnosis. Initial hemolysis testing demonstrated complement component 3-positive, immunoglobulin G-negative direct antiglobulin testing. Donath-Landsteiner testing confirmed a diagnosis of PCH. The patient had a complicated 38-day hospital course that required mechanical ventilation, renal replacement therapy, and extensive transfusions. Notably, the patient was also diagnosed with COVID-19 shortly before the onset of hemolysis, representing a potential alternative trigger or co-trigger to his PCH. Although the clinical timeline is compatible with VZV reactivation triggering PCH, the specific infectious trigger cannot be definitively established. Nevertheless, to our knowledge, this is the first reported case of PCH occurring in temporal association with VZV reactivation rather than primary VZV infection.

title: ‘Pushing the crisis button’? Temporal space and institutional synchronization in Finland's COVID-19 governance
abstract: The article examines how the temporal space of a crisis is constructed, synchronized and contested within crisis governance. Drawing on conceptual history and recent scholarship on crisis temporalities, we introduce the concept of ‘institutional synchronization’ to capture the active, precarious work of aligning diverse governance actors into a shared temporal framework. Through an in-depth case study of the Finnish COVID-19 response, utilizing situational reports, government policies and parliamentary debates, we map how this synchronization was achieved across expert, governmental and parliamentary domains. Our analysis identifies two core mechanisms of temporal alignment: ‘situational temporal framing’ (operationalized via the metaphor of epidemic waves) and ‘data-driven presentism’, which anchored decision-making in a continuously updated ‘now’. While these mechanisms effectively forged a synchronized present at the outset of the pandemic, they inherently marginalized long-term societal timescapes. As the crisis prolonged and its scope widened beyond a narrow epidemiological emergency, this temporal friction resulted in political contestation and the ultimate fracturing of the synchronized order. By demonstrating that crisis synchronization is not an automatic societal alignment but a linguistically mediated and highly fragile institutional effort, this article contributes to our understanding of chronopolitics and the limits of crisis governance in an era of polycrisis.

title: Nuanced Preemption: A Case Study of State and Local Government Behavior During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: This study reconceptualizes state preemption as a multidimensional policy design choice that actively reshapes state-local authority. We examine gubernatorial treatment of local governments through executive orders issued during the COVID-19 pandemic to capture the complexity of state-local interactions. Utilizing the Institutional Grammar Tool, we code executive orders to develop a novel measure that considers both the direction (authorization versus prohibition) and scope (narrow versus broad) of state intervention in local autonomy. This approach reveals variation in how states simultaneously constrain and empower local governments, demonstrating patterns that are obscured by conventional measures that treat preemption solely as a prohibitive instrument. The findings highlight the importance of nuanced measurement strategies for understanding intergovernmental dynamics, particularly in crisis contexts that are characterized by rapid policy change.

title: The Pharmacokinetics, Biodistribution and Therapeutic Efficacy of a Trimeric Nanobody Against SARS-CoV-2 in the Golden Syrian Hamster COVID-19 Model
abstract: Nanobodies are promising medical countermeasures against respiratory viruses, but their local pharmacokinetics and therapeutic window remain incompletely defined. We evaluated the pharmacokinetics, biodistribution and efficacy of a SARS-CoV-2-neutralising trimeric nanobody (A8) in golden Syrian hamsters. Following intranasal administration, A8 concentrations were quantified in nasal wash, bronchoalveolar lavage, lung and serum, and tissue distribution was assessed immunohistologically. Therapeutic efficacy was examined after intranasal treatment before or following challenge with SARS-CoV-2 B.1.351. Intranasal administration of A8 produced sustained respiratory exposure with minimal systemic absorption, whereas intraperitoneal dosing generated transient serum exposure and limited pulmonary delivery. A8 was detected within airway lining material, respiratory epithelial cells, type II pneumocytes and alveolar macrophages. Prophylactic administration 2 h before infection prevented weight loss, while treatment 24 h post-infection accelerated recovery and reduced viral subgenomic RNA in respiratory tissues. Doses as low as 0.1 mg/kg were effective when administered at 24 h post-infection, with no clear dose–response relationship. Treatment delayed until 48 h post-infection was less effective. These findings demonstrate that intranasal A8 achieves favourable compartmentalised exposure and that therapeutic efficacy depends principally on early respiratory delivery rather than dose magnitude, supporting further development of inhaled nanobody therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.

title: Real-World Outcomes of Ambulatory Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis Management During the COVID-19 Pandemic in Romania
abstract: Background: Romania continues to experience one of the highest tuberculosis (TB) burdens in the European Union/European Economic Area. During the COVID-19 pandemic, reduced inpatient capacity accelerated the use of ambulatory care for patients with drug-susceptible tuberculosis (DS-TB). This study evaluated treatment outcomes, outcome ascertainment, hospitalization requirements, and factors associated with unfavorable outcomes among patients managed through ambulatory TB services. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of adults with pulmonary or extrapulmonary DS-TB managed through ambulatory tuberculosis dispensaries affiliated with the “Marius Nasta” Institute of Pneumophthisiology, Bucharest, Romania, between January 2020 and December 2022. Treatment outcomes were defined according to World Health Organization criteria. Factors associated with unfavorable outcome were assessed using Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression. Hospitalization during treatment was analyzed as a secondary outcome. Results: The final cohort comprised 545 patients with DS-TB, with a mean age of 44.8 years and 56.1% being male. Overall, 281 of 545 patients achieved treatment success, corresponding to a WHO-defined treatment-success rate of 51.6%. The high proportion of not-evaluated patients represents an important programmatic weakness and limits conclusions regarding the effectiveness of the ambulatory model. Improved outcome ascertainment and continuity of follow-up are essential components of decentralized TB care.

title: Maternal Characteristics and Adverse Neonatal Outcomes During the COVID-19 Pandemic and Maternal Characteristics During the Three-Child Policy: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, studies showed a significant decrease in fertility rate among Chinese women of reproductive age. The Chinese government implemented the three-child policy in an attempt to change the sustained low birth rate under the dual threat of population development and the pandemic. To separately evaluate the changes in maternal characteristics after the outbreak of the epidemic and the adjustment of fertility policies, as well as the relationship between the COVID-19 pandemic and adverse neonate outcomes, a retrospective study was conducted at one hospital. We collected data on birthing women from medical record databases from January 1, 2017, to December 31, 2022. Records for a total of 93,547 neonates and a corresponding 88,857 maternal medical records were analyzed using SPSS software version 26. The differences in maternal and gestational characteristics between subgroups during the two periods were analyzed using Pearson's chi-square test. We used univariate and multivariate analyses to assess the relationship between the COVID-19 pandemic and neonatal outcomes. We found that during the epidemic, the proportion of pregnant women of advanced age (20.3% vs. 24.5%), mothers who gave birth ≥ 2 times (27.0% vs. 42.1%), and non-IVF pregnant women (86.2% vs. After the implementation of the three-child policy, the proportion of mothers who gave birth once (74.8% vs. 72.8%) increased significantly, while the proportion of mothers who gave birth ≥ 2 times (25.2% vs. In addition, the results of multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that the risk of cesarean birth (CB) in newborns increased (aOR 1.062, 95% CI 1.032-1.093, p < 0.001), but the risk of premature birth (PTB) (aOR 0.809, 95% CI 0.775-0.844, p < 0.001), low birth weight (LBW) (aOR 0.903, 95% CI 0.861-0.947, p < 0.001), macrosomia (aOR 0.890, 95% CI 0.824-0.960, p = 0.003), small for gestational age (SGA) (aOR 0.921, 95% CI 0.887-0.956, p < 0.001), and large for gestational age (LGA) (aOR 0.924, 95% CI 0.887-0.962, p < 0.001) were all reduced after the outbreak of the epidemic. In summary, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the proportion of pregnant women under 35 years old, women without previous delivery history and women undergoing fertility therapy increased in this hospital. The incidence of adverse outcomes in newborns, including PTB, LBW, macrosomia, SGA, and LGA, was reduced. After the implementation of the three-child policy, the proportion of multiparous women has decreased. This suggests that the threat of the pandemic has led to significant changes in fertility preferences in the area, but the incidence of adverse outcomes, except for cesarean birth, has decreased. However, exposure to COVID-19 alone cannot be assumed as a significant impact on the neonatal outcomes; we need to pay more attention to the future development of these children and the impact of public events and policies on them.

title: Changes in Antimicrobial Resistance in Bloodstream Infections During the COVID-19 Pandemic—A Retrospective Study from a Tertiary Care Hospital
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to major repurposing of healthcare settings, especially Infectious Diseases hospitals, by redirecting care towards SARS-CoV-2-infected patients. However, frequent bacterial infections overlapping the viral background led to changes in antimicrobial resistance profiling among patients. This study aims to assess isolates from invasive infections and their antimicrobial susceptibility patterns in pre-pandemic and pandemic periods. Positive blood cultures from patients hospitalized in our Institute between January 2019 and September 2022 were assessed in terms of antimicrobial susceptibility, following sample processing as per laboratory protocol, with the use of the automated Bactalert®3D system, MALDI-TOF® MS and microscopy for bacterial identification. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the Vitek2Compact® and Micronaut-S® systems. Phenotypic enzyme production testing was assessed using the Resist-5 OKNVI kits. All data were subsequently digitalized, and statistical analysis was performed. A total of 932 non-duplicated bacterial and fungal strains were analyzed, with the most commonly isolated organisms being Staphylococcus aureus (n = 173), followed by Escherichia coli(n = 156), Acinetobacter baumannii (n = 95), and Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 89). Resistance rates to multiple antimicrobials increased substantially amongst Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates followed a national decrease trend during the pandemic period; however, an increasingly resistant profile to macrolides may be attributable to the excessive and often unjustified use of Azithromycin during the pandemic period. The COVID-19 pandemic was accompanied by a shift in bacterial profile of invasive infections amongst our cohort, illustrating the dynamic nature of antimicrobial resistance in an Infectious Diseases hospital during those times, underscoring the complex interplay between the COVID-19 pandemic and antibiotic resistance patterns, and highlighting the need for ongoing surveillance and tailored antimicrobial stewardship efforts in clinical practice.

title: UMA PERSPECTIVA DE REDE DOS SINTOMAS DE BURNOUT EM PROFISSIONAIS DE SAÚDE NA PANDEMIA DA COVID-19 A NETWORK PERSPECTIVE ON BURNOUT SYMPTOMS AMONG HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC UNA PERSPECTIVA DE RED SOBRE LOS SÍNTOMAS DE AGOTAMIENTO ENTRE LOS PROFESIONALES SANITARIOS DURANTE LA PANDEMIA DE COVID-19
abstract: A área da saúde apresenta a maior prevalência de Síndrome de Burnout (SB) entre seus profissionais. Dado o contexto da pandemia de COVID-19, esses sintomas podem ter apresentado aumento significativo nesse grupo, o que torna necessário reconhecer sobre quais manifestações da SB devem-se desenvolver trabalhos preventivos e interventivos. Este estudo teve como objetivo compreender a relação entre os sintomas de Burnout, fatores sociodemográficos, condições de saúde e estilo de vida de profissionais de saúde na pandemia da COVID-19. 104 participantes (Midade = 35, DP = 8,9) responderam aos questionários desta pesquisa de maneira remota (on-line). Pelo fato da SB se tratar de um fenômeno multideterminado, empregou-se a análise em perspectiva de rede. A rede apresentada mostrou fortes ligações entre os sintomas de Burnout, além da maior influência esperada dentro do modelo gerado. Os resultados mostram sobre quais manifestações da SB devem-se focar em medidas de cuidado para este grupo. O tamanho da amostra e o fato de ter sido composta por profissionais de um único local constituem as principais limitações à generalização dos resultados.

title: COVID-19 is associated with lupus flare and persistent disease activity: longitudinal data from the ReumaCov-Brazil Register study
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate flares in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients over a period of six months after COVID-19. A multicenter, observational, and prospective cohort study was performed. SLE adult patients with COVID-19 (case group) were compared to SLE patients without COVID-19 (control group). Assessments were performed at baseline (V0), immediately after COVID-19 (V1), and three and six months after infection (V2 and V3). Disease activity was evaluated using the patient global assessment (PGA) and the modified SLE Disease Activity Index 2000 (mSLEDAI-2 K). Flare was defined as an increase in the mSLEDAI-2 K score of greater than three, and persistent disease activity was defined as mSLEDAI-2 K score greater than three over two consecutive visits. A total of 715 patients were included, 363 in the case group and 352 in the control group. Patients in the case group were slightly older than controls [mean age 41.0 (SD 12.38) vs. 38.8 (SD 12.07) years; p = 0.017]. Longitudinal analyses showed differences in disease activity trajectories between groups, particularly for PGA. Flare and/or persistent disease activity occurred more frequently in the case group [74 (18.5%) vs. 33 (10.5%); p = 0.001], and COVID-19 during follow-up was associated with this outcome [OR 1.70 (95% CI 1.06–2.74); p = 0.029]. However, in the sensitivity analysis restricted to laboratory-confirmed COVID-19, the difference in the categorical outcome was not statistically significant. New SLE manifestations were also more frequent following COVID-19. The findings suggest a possible association between COVID-19 and subsequent SLE disease activity.

title: The Impact of COVID-19 on Regional Tourism and Its Statistical Modeling: A Provincial Case Study of Morocco’s Oriental Region (2019–2025)
abstract: Tourism is a key driver of development for emerging economies but is vulnerable to shocks. The subnational level remains understudied relative to national or global assessments, despite the 190,000 annual tourist arrivals recorded before the crisis in the five provinces studied here. We describe the change in tourism demand associated with the pandemic period in Morocco’s oriental region using a panel of five provinces (2019–2025, 35 observations) and four models: a log-linear regression, a negative binomial regression, a fixed-effects panel model, and a multivariate PLS2 regression on two jointly modeled responses, arrivals and overnight stays. All four models show a pandemic-phase decline of 41–64% depending on the model; the primary year-by-year specification shows a drop of approximately 55% in 2020 and 33% in 2021, and regional arrivals recovered to about 122% of their 2019 level by 2025. No significant province-level heterogeneity was detected, though test power is limited; accommodation capacity shows the strongest cross-sectional association with demand in the exploratory PLS2 model but is not a within-province determinant; and average length of stay shortened during the crisis. These results point to a pandemic shock of substantial magnitude and a recovery that is quantitative rather than qualitative—consistent with, though not proof of, a largely region-wide shock.

title: Changes in Healthcare-Associated Infections Before and After COVID-19–Related Intensive Care Unit Reorganization: A Long- Term Comparative Surveillance Study
abstract: Objective: The COVID-19 pandemic led to substantial structural changes in intensive care unit (ICU) organization worldwide. However, data on long-term changes in healthcare-associated infection (HAI) epidemiology after COVID-19–related ICU reorganization remain limited. This study compared HAI epidemiology before and after COVID-19–related ICU reorganization while excluding the pandemic transition period. Methods: This retrospective surveillance study included HAI episodes among adult patients admitted to level II and III ICUs of a 600-bed tertiary teaching and research hospital between January 2015 and June 2025. Healthcare-associated infection episodes diagnosed during the pandemic transition period (March 2020-June 2021) were excluded. The pre-COVID period (January 2015-March 2020) was compared with the post-reorganization period (July 2021-June 2025). Healthcare-associated infections were identified using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/National Healthcare Safety Network surveillance definitions applicable during each surveillance year. Patient-level characteristics, episode-level infection types and microbiological findings, device-associated infection rates, and in-hospital mortality were compared. Results: A total of 3015 HAI episodes occurring in 2351 patients were included: 1062 episodes in 828 patients during the pre-COVID period and 1953 episodes in 1523 patients during the post-reorganization period. The overall HAI rate increased significantly from 5.64% to 6.42% (rate ratio [RR], 1.14; 95% CI, 1.06-1.23; P < .001). Device-associated infection rates also increased significantly, including catheter-associated urinary tract infection (RR, 1.31; P = .011), ventilator-associated pneumonia (RR, 3.03; P < .001), and central line-associated bloodstream infection (RR, 1.52; P < .001). The post-reorganization period showed higher proportions of ventilator-associated pneumonia and non-ventilator-associated pneumonia, predominance of gram-negative pathogens, increased frequencies of Acinetobacter spp. and Pseudomonas spp., emergence of Candida auris, and higher in-hospital mortality (69.1% vs. Conclusion: Healthcare-associated infection epidemiology differed substantially between the pre-COVID and post-reorganization periods. Increased device-associated infection rates, shifts in pathogen distribution, emergence of Candida auris, and higher in-hospital mortality highlight the need for sustained infection prevention and control efforts beyond the pandemic period. title: Secondary stroke prevention during the first Swiss COVID-19 lockdown: a single-centre cohort study
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic necessitated lockdowns, potentially affecting stroke care. We evaluated changes in acute stroke treatment, diagnostic work-up, and secondary prevention during the first Swiss COVID-19 lockdown primarily by comparing the lockdown and post-lockdown periods; the 2015 cohort was used as historical context for secular changes. We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Bernese Stroke Registry, including consecutive patients with acute ischaemic stroke receiving reperfusion therapy in 2015 ( n = 319), during lockdown (March 16-April 26/2020; n = 66), and post-lockdown 2020 ( n = 236). Baseline characteristics, treatment metrics, diagnostic work-up, secondary prevention and 3-month outcomes were compared. Analyses were unadjusted and exploratory, and no correction for multiple comparisons was applied. The centre treated 11.0 patients/week during lockdown and 25.4 patients/week post-lockdown (rate ratio 0.43, 95%CI 0.33–0.57, p < 0.001). Baseline characteristics, treatment metrics and functional outcome were similar between lockdown and post-lockdown patients. title: Newly Diagnosed Anxiety, Mood, and Trauma-Related Disorders Following COVID-19 Infection Among U.S. Military Beneficiaries
abstract: The long-term neuropsychiatric effects of COVID-19 are still unclear. Various mental health conditions are known to be influenced by biopsychosocial factors. We sought to investigate whether COVID-19 infection increases the risk for newly diagnosed anxiety, mood, or trauma and stressor-related disorders in individuals ages 12–64 years. We performed a retrospective cohort study using data from the Military Health System database (2018–2022). A propensity score match pairing each person with a COVID-19 diagnosis to two uninfected individuals was implemented, balancing matches across 1852 different variables representing medical records of procedures, diagnoses, and prescriptions in the year prior to COVID-19 infection. Exact matching was performed on sex, age in years, beneficiary type and month of entry into the cohort. We calculated the hazard ratios (HR) and Bonferroni-corrected confidence intervals (BoCI) for new mental health diagnoses using the Cox proportional hazards models. The initial matched cohort included 788,185 individuals. COVID-19 significantly increased the risk for newly diagnosed mental health conditions. The effect was strongest for trauma and stressor-related disorders (HR, 1.29; BoCI, 1.22–1.37), followed by mood disorders (HR, 1.22; BoCI, 1.15–1.30) and anxiety disorders (HR, 1.16; BoCI, 1.12–1.21). COVID-19 infection is associated with the subsequent diagnosis of a new mental health condition, including depressive, trauma and stressor-related, mood, and anxiety disorders. Our findings suggest that screening for mental health conditions should be a key part of post-COVID-19 care, and more work is needed to understand the biological reasons for this connection and consider the role of vaccines for prevention.

title: “This Too Shall Pass”—Resilience Factors of Parental Divorce During COVID-19 Pandemic for Adolescents
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic had detrimental effects on the well-being of individuals across the world. For adolescent girls experiencing parental divorce during the COVID-19 pandemic, the effect was exacerbated, as they had to grapple with the adversities associated with both the pandemic and divorce. Nonetheless, many of them have fared well and shown resilience despite adversities. The resilience of adolescents in the face of parental divorce during COVID-19 has been largely understudied, especially in South Africa. The present study aimed to explore the factors that enable the resilience of adolescent girls from divorced households during the COVID-19 pandemic. In alignment with qualitative research, the study employed a phenomenological research design. Purposive sampling was used to recruit five female adolescents in Johannesburg, South Africa. Data were collected using semi-structured interviews and a focus group. Braun and Clarke’s six steps of data analysis were used to analyse data thematically. The findings of the study grouped resilience into individual attributes (coping mechanisms, viewing divorce as a good resolution, perseverance, optimism and spirituality), relational factors (relationships with mothers, extended family, friends and partners) and contextual factors (access to mental health support and teacher support). These findings underscore that a combination of individual and social-ecological factors should anchor interventions aimed at promoting the resilience of adolescent girls whose parents divorced during pandemics.
journal: Journal of Child and Family Studies

title: Voices from the classroom: Exploring COVID-19 vaccine perceptions among teachers and adolescent learners in the Western Cape, South Africa.
abstract: This study explored COVID-19 vaccine perceptions among secondary-school teachers and late-adolescent learners in the Western Cape, South Africa. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 teachers (mean age = 43.4 years) and 23 learners (mean age = 18.6 years) from seven public schools. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Vaccine perceptions emerged as dynamic, often contradictory, and shaped by fear, mistrust, faith, mandates, social influence and the evolving pandemic context. Although teachers and learners described many shared influences, occupational role, developmental stage and changing pandemic conditions shaped how these influences were experienced. Interpreted through the 5C model of vaccine hesitancy, the findings demonstrate that vaccine perceptions were negotiated within relational and institutional contexts, distinguishing vaccine uptake from vaccine acceptance. These findings contextualise the application of the 5C model within South African secondary schools and highlight the importance of contextually grounded, developmentally sensitive approaches to school-based vaccine communication.

title: Not only correcting lies. Analysis of interventionist strategies in news articles dealing with misinformation during the COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands
abstract: During crises, when falsehoods often spread faster than facts, journalists face the challenge of deciding how to fight misinformation without amplifying its reach. This study focuses on Dutch journalists who addressed pandemic-related misinformation during the COVID-19 crisis (January 2020–May 2023), distinguishing between actively interventionist strategies (correction and prebunking) and more detached approaches. Drawing on a content analysis of 698 news articles, it investigates the use of actively interventionist strategies, and their variation across pandemic phases and in their use of expert sources. Findings show that 14.2% of articles adopted actively interventionist roles, with corrections being more common than prebunking. Such strategies were more frequent during the initial uncertain phase of the pandemic and during vaccine rollouts. Articles using these strategies relied on a greater number and diversity of sources, especially academic, governmental, and health-related. The results highlight a cautious engagement by journalists in actively countering misinformation, favoring a more detached reporting. Overall, the study advances the understanding of journalistic role performance in health crises and the interplay between journalism practice and misinformation management.

title: Staying attached: short-time work and worker retention during COVID-19
abstract: Purpose This paper estimates how workers retained through short-time work (STW) during the COVID-19 pandemic would have fared had STW not been available. Design/methodology/approach Using Austrian matched employer-employee administrative data, we compare workers who became unemployed during the initial nationwide lockdown with observationally similar workers who entered STW instead. To strengthen the credibility of the comparison, we focus on jobs plausibly at risk of dismissal, exclude likely non-crisis unemployment using a machine-learning prediction model trained on pre-crisis labour market histories, and exploit quasi-experimental variation in firms' early adjustment strategies while conditioning on rich worker-, firm- and shock-related characteristics. Findings Although many unemployment entrants returned quickly to employment, unemployment had persistent adverse effects relative to STW. Three years later, unemployment entrants were less likely to be employed, much less likely to remain with their pre-crisis employer, and accumulated substantially lower labour income than comparable STW participants. Practical implications These findings suggest that STW can substantially reduce medium-run employment and earnings losses following sudden and unexpected demand shocks. They support the use of well-targeted job-retention schemes in response to future large-scale economic shocks. Originality/value The paper provides novel individual-level counterfactual evidence on unemployment relative to job retention through STW during the COVID-19 pandemic. By focussing on workers whose jobs were plausibly at risk of dismissal and comparing unemployment entrants with observationally similar STW participants rather than workers who remained continuously employed without STW, it provides a more credible assessment of the worker-level effects of STW.

title: Pencil or a Keyboard: Teacher Implications Pre and Post COVID-19
abstract: This chapter examines how handwriting and typing shape early literacy instruction and how the COVID- 19 pandemic accelerated shifts in writing modalities. Drawing on cognitive science, neuroscience, and literacy research, it argues that handwriting remains essential for developing phonological processing, orthographic mapping, spelling, and writing fluency, while typing supports efficiency and digital participation. The pandemic highlighted gaps in teacher preparation, as preservice teachers received limited training in handwriting pedagogy and defaulted to digital tools during remote learning. The chapter proposes a dual- modality approach in which teacher preparation programs intentionally integrate handwriting and typing, preparing educators to make research- aligned instructional decisions that support reading, spelling, and written expression in post- COVID classrooms.

title: Higher Education Responses to the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: This chapter describes a qualitative research project led by Professor Jitendra Singh which analyzed university responses to the COVID-19 pandemic. Chris J Shannon and Stephen Yorkstone describe how data collected through a co-designed instrument was subjected to thematic analysis to explore how faculty and administrators from educational institutions across the world prepared for and responded to the challenges caused by the pandemic, and also explore how these challenges changed and evolved over time through the subsequent waves of COVID-19 variants and prolonged lockdowns. The five themes identified in the data (institutional responses, teaching continuity, technological limitations, staff and student experiences, and socio-political environments) are then explored. The authors revisit Yorkstone&s;s 2017 model of university functions, outputs, and destinations to consider how crises impact on universities within their societal contexts.

title: ‘Who do we not save?’: Biolegitimacy, the right to health and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the well-being of frontline workers in the United Kingdom
abstract: This article examines the experiences of frontline workers in the United Kingdom to understand how they navigated changes to services during COVID-19 and the impact this had on their well-being. It uses qualitative data from semi-structured interviews with frontline workers from various sectors, including health and social care, criminal justice, education, and community-led organisations. It examines some of the challenges they faced and uses Fassin’s concept of biolegitimacy (the sacredness assigned to biological life) to understand the tensions and contradictions in the United Kingdom’s response to the pandemic, which emphasised saving lives but, at the same time, did not value all lives equally. The article highlights how the primacy afforded to the National Health Service and COVID-related care created hierarchies of frontline work; considers workers’ experiences of vicarious suffering; and workers’ subjugation of their own needs to continue providing care to individuals they considered disadvantaged by the public health response to COVID-19. The article further argues there is a gendered dimension to these experiences, as women in the research bore the brunt of ill-considered, generic policy responses which failed to account for their specific needs. By using the concept of biolegitimacy to understand workers’ experiences, the article connects the micro-level experiences of frontline workers to wider value systems to consider how lives are evaluated in periods of crisis, providing an understanding of workers’ experiences that goes beyond the organisational level.

title: Reach and engagement in the ECAIL trial targeting socially disadvantaged families across the COVID-19 pandemic and cost-of-living crisis: A mixed-methods implementation study
abstract: Background The ECAIL trial, launched in 2017, was designed to evaluate a multicomponent intervention for childhood obesity prevention among hard-to-reach families. At a maternity hospital in Lille, France, healthcare providers screened pregnant women experiencing social vulnerability, and dietitians delivered a home-based intervention until age 2. The COVID-19 pandemic led to a six-month suspension in 2020. This study compared eligibility and participation before the pandemic and after resumption, and examined how implementation and reach evolved across the pandemic and subsequent cost-of-living crisis. Methods Using a convergent mixed-methods design, we analyzed 5,744 eligibility questionnaires distributed at the maternity ward and conducted a focus group with six dieticians delivering the intervention to triangulate quantitative implementation indicators with qualitative implementation data. Inclusion criteria included ≥1 indicator of social vulnerability (e.g., socioeconomic disadvantage, precarious housing, or social isolation). The focus group was recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically focusing on reach, acceptability, and adaptation. Results Eligibility increased from 29.7% (n = 955) pre-pandemic to 33.6% (n = 849) after resumption, while the distribution of vulnerability criteria remained similar across periods: 78.3% received social/medical benefits; employment was not the main source of household income for 58.7%; 24.4% experienced financial hardship; 14.7% reported social isolation; 6.0% lived in precarious housing; and 19.0% had three or more vulnerabilities. Participation among eligible women remained stable (24.6%; n = 443). Qualitative findings indicated dietitians’ satisfaction and participants’ enthusiasm for the resumption of home visits, particularly in addressing social isolation. After resumption, the introduction of a pre-visit COVID-19 questionnaire was associated with fewer failed home visits. Integration of quantitative and qualitative findings indicated sustained, and in some cases strengthened, provider engagement despite pandemic-related strain on hospital services. Conclusions This study suggests that a complex intervention can maintain reach and acceptability through adaptive implementation under major contextual disruptions. The rapid resumption of home-based services emerged as a promising implementation strategy for engaging and retaining socially disadvantaged families, highlighting the importance of flexible, context-sensitive approaches during social and economic crises. Trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov NCT03003117; registration date: 21/12/2016; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03003117.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Based Framework for Automated Research Gap Identification in COVID-19 Literature
abstract: The surge in COVID-19 scientific publications has complicated the process of identifying research gaps through traditional literature reviews, necessitating automated analysis methods. This study presents a framework to identify and classify these gaps using BERTopic and large language models (LLMs). From the CORD-19 dataset, 84,964 abstracts indicating potential literature gaps were filtered for analysis. The text-processing pipeline vectorized abstracts with SBERT, performed dimensionality reduction with UMAP, and clustered the data with HDBSCAN.
