title: Exposure to residential greenness and subsequent risk of common mental disorders among individuals with COVID-19 in South Korea: A nationwide cohort study
abstract: Background Residential greenness is considered protective for mental health, but its impact on clinically diagnosed psychiatric disorders following COVID-19 remains unclear. This study investigated the association between residential greenness and risk of common mental disorders after COVID-19, and whether this relationship differed by population subgroup. Methods We conducted a nationwide cohort study of 3,097,179 adults aged ≥19 years with confirmed COVID-19 in South Korea between 2018 and 2023 using the K-COV-N cohort, which integrates administrative and clinical data from the National Health Insurance Service and COVID-19 data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency. Residential greenness was assessed using the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and categorized as low (0.2– < 0.4), moderate (0.4– < 0.6), or high (≥0.6). The primary outcome was first diagnosis of anxiety disorder, depression, insomnia, or bipolar disorder ≥30 days post-infection. Weighted Cox proportional hazards models with inverse probability of treatment weighting were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs). Results Compared to low NDVI, moderate NDVI was associated with reduced risk of any common mental disorder (aHR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96–0.98), with the strongest effect for bipolar disorder (0.84; 0.79–0.88). High NDVI showed no overall benefit (1.00; 0.99–1.01) and was associated with increased anxiety risk (1.04; 1.03–1.06), especially in older adults and those with comorbidities. Younger individuals experienced the greatest benefit from moderate greenness. Conclusion Moderate residential greenness was linked to lower risk of mental disorders following COVID-19, while high greenness conferred limited benefit and potential risk. Greening strategies should be paired with strengthened health and social infrastructure to reduce disparities.

title: Evolution of symptoms, quality of life, and objective breathing markers in a prospective case series of patients with post-COVID-19 dysfunctional breathing
abstract: Dysfunctional breathing (DB) was described after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and can contribute to persistent dyspnoea and other associated symptoms but the evolution of DB after COVID-19 is poorly described. Individuals with persistent symptoms after COVID-19 were evaluated and those diagnosed with DB were included. DB was diagnosed by identifying an abnormal breathing pattern during cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) associated with compatible symptoms after ruling out cardiopulmonary conditions that could account for the symptoms. All included patients were prospectively followed and systematically assessed 6–9 months after their diagnosis. Given the multiplicity of analyses and the absence of a pre-specified primary analysis, all findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Forty-eight patients were included and 45 patients were successfully reassessed at 6–9 months. Forty-two received specific respiratory physiotherapy targeting DB. The proportion of individuals with a Nijmegen score ≥ 23 decreased from 30 (68%) at baseline to 19 (43%) at follow-up ( p = 0.02). Dyspnea improved at 6–9 months, with 0%, 11%, 44%, 35%, and 11% of patients presenting mMRC grades 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 at baseline, compared with 20%, 39%, 37%, 4%, and 0% at follow-up ( p < 0.001). Improvements in quality of life and functional status were observed. However, 21 patients (47%) continued to experience significant functional limitations, defined as a post-COVID-19 functional status (PCFS) scale score ≥ 2. Objective markers of DB during CPET improved, with reductions in hyperventilation, dispersion of breathing parameters, and the number of sighs. In most patients diagnosed with DB after COVID-19, improvements in symptoms, QoL, functional status and objective markers of DB were observed at 6–9 months. A substantial proportion of patients remained disabled.

title: Effect of Fluvoxamine and Metformin for Fatigue in Patients With Long COVID : An Adaptive Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Postacute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (long COVID) presents a therapeutic challenge, with fatigue being a common, debilitating symptom. OBJECTIVE To assess the efficacy of fluvoxamine and metformin to treat long COVID fatigue. DESIGN Randomized, placebo-controlled, adaptive trial. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06128967). SETTING Outpatient sites in Brazil. PARTICIPANTS 399 adults with fatigue 90 days to 24 months after confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. INTERVENTION Participants were randomly assigned to fluvoxamine (100 mg twice daily [BID]), extended-release metformin (750 mg BID [n = 71] from October 2023 to April 2024; reduced to 500 mg BID [n = 40] in May 2024 after a protocol amendment until the group was stopped for futility in September 2024), or a matching placebo, each for 60 days with follow-up to day 90. MEASUREMENTS Change in Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) score. RESULTS Median baseline FSS scores ranged from 5.6 to 5.9 across all study groups. The treatment effect on FSS score for fluvoxamine versus placebo showed a mean difference of -0.43 at day 60 and -0.58 at day 90; both had a posterior probability of superiority of 99%. Fluvoxamine also improved quality-of-life scores with a high posterior probability of superiority. Findings for metformin were inconclusive. Incidence of adverse events was lower for fluvoxamine (24.0%) than for metformin, 750 mg BID (45.1%); metformin, 500 mg BID (42.5%); and placebo (35.5%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events were rare (≤2.7%), with no treatment-related deaths. LIMITATIONS The results were inconclusive for metformin because of a dose change recommended by the data safety and monitoring committee due to adverse effects causing study withdrawal and early termination. The benefit of fluvoxamine after 90 days is unknown. The trial did not address other long COVID symptoms. CONCLUSION Fluvoxamine shows potential for improving long COVID-associated fatigue and quality of life. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE The Latona Foundation.

title: A CXCL10-enriched hepatic-risk phenotype reveals a cell-count paradox in severe COVID-19.
abstract: BACKGROUND Cell-count-derived inflammatory indices, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), are widely used to assess COVID-19 severity, but hepatic dysfunction and thrombocytopenia may alter their prognostic meaning. We tested whether FIB-4-defined hepatic risk modifies the interpretation of cell-count inflammation and whether this discordance has a cytokine or chemokine correlate. METHODS We applied an a priori 2 × 2 framework to 575 hospitalized adults with COVID-19 undergoing CT pulmonary angiography, classified by cardiometabolic burden and FIB-4-defined hepatic risk. Associations with oxygen requirement, ICU admission, in-hospital death, composite ICU/death and prolonged hospitalization were analyzed. A separate non-overlapping cytokine cohort of 90 patients was used for cytokine/chemokine profiling. RESULTS Hepatic-risk phenotypes had higher adjusted odds of adverse outcomes but paradoxically lower NLR, PLR, SII and derived NLR. Significant index × hepatic-risk interactions showed that NLR, SII and dNLR retained their expected risk gradients in non-hepatic-risk patients but were attenuated or absent in hepatic-risk patients. In the cytokine cohort, the cellular pattern was reproduced, CXCL10/IP-10 and IL-8/CXCL8 were selectively elevated, and hepatic-risk patients were enriched in the NLR-low/CXCL10-high quadrant. Cell-normalized CXCL10 metrics and a CXCL10-NLR discordance score supported disproportionate chemokine enrichment relative to suppressed peripheral cell-count readouts. CONCLUSION FIB-4-defined hepatic-risk COVID-19 identifies a CXCL10/IP-10-enriched, peripherally cell-count-suppressed inflammatory phenotype. Conventional NLR-, PLR-, SII- and dNLR-based risk interpretation may underestimate clinical risk when hepatic risk is present.

title: Trends in long COVID and post-viral fatigue in children in primary care in England.
abstract: BACKGROUND Post-viral sequelae following the COVID-19 pandemic attention to post-viral fatigue and long COVID, but the impact on children and young people's (CYP) primary care use is unknown. AIM To examine temporal, seasonal, and sociodemographic patterns in primary care consultations for long COVID and PVFS in CYP DESIGN AND SETTINGS: We conducted a retrospective, population-based dynamic cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum data for CYP aged <18 years in England, between 1st January 2006 and 31st December 2022 (from 1st March 2020 for long COVID); a period covering the influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and COVID-19 pandemics. METHOD Consultation rates per 100 000 child-years were calculated for long COVID and post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS) by calendar year, month, and sociodemographic characteristics. Trends, seasonal patterns, and differences between pandemic and non-pandemic periods (for PVFS) were described. Negative binomial regression was used to estimate associations with sociodemographic characteristics. RESULTS The cohort included 7,442,572 CYP (3 624 692 registered in primary care during the COVID-19 pandemic). There were 6700 long COVID and 20,440 PVFS consultations. Long COVID consultation rates were highest in 2022 (140.3 per 100,00 child-years). PVFS consultation rates peaked in 2009 and 2022 (during H1N1 and COVID pandemics) with rates of 57.1 and 56.9 per 100 000 child-years, respectively. Consultation rates were highest among older CYP, girls, and those from least deprived areas. CONCLUSION Long COVID consultations were highest in 2022, and PVFS consultation rates peaked during 2009 and 2022. Our findings that rates were highest in less deprived areas and girls need further investigation.

title: Organized communities as pre-existing infrastructures of care during the COVID-19 pandemic: A transnational dialogue
abstract: This article draws from a community-engaged study of how ordinary people's social justice mobilization during the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil, Canada, Germany, and Peru placed demands on local and national governments for equitable social policies. It challenges celebratory narratives of resilience that assume that made-marginalized peoples and communities can repeatedly and indefinitely absorb negative shocks while continuing to thrive/survive. Instead, we emphasize the value of understanding these communities as producers of care infrastructures, while recognizing that this care work is often done through their volunteer labor under difficult circumstances. These practices reveal the long-standing normalization of structural abandonment under neoliberal governance and, from an Urban Political Ecology (UPE) perspective, the uneven socio-ecological conditions through which the impacts of crisis are produced and lived. Across diverse contexts, pandemic care infrastructures emerged precisely where public health systems, housing policies, labor protections, and social safety nets failed to protect made-marginalized populations. We argue that infrastructures of care do not/should not replace claims on the state for just and equitable access to comprehensive social protections and rights, but rather indicate community recognition and creation of what could and should exist as an integrated (state-community) infrastructure of care that is a truly community-informed and -engaged approach to social well-being.

title: Heterogeneous Crime Disruption in the COVID-19 Era: Structural Break Evidence From Aotearoa New Zealand Monthly Victimisation Data
abstract: This study examines whether the COVID-19 period coincides with structural breaks in Aotearoa New Zealand recorded crime and whether break timing differs across offence categories. Monthly report-date victimisation counts from the Aotearoa New Zealand Police Recorded Crime Victim Statistics are analysed from July 2014 to January 2025 across nine offence groupings. Log-transformed series are modelled with seasonal controls and long-run trend terms. Structural change is assessed with the Bai-Perron endogenous break test, which searches all candidate months for the dates at which the level or trend of a series changes, using wild-bootstrap inference and information-criterion selection of multiple breaks; corroborating stability diagnostics are reported as sensitivity analyses. Magnitudes are characterised through a centred pre–post regime comparison with heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation-consistent inference, and a decomposition separates persistent change from recovery after the restriction period. The results indicate widespread but non-universal instability and reveal three timing pathways: near-onset breaks for opportunity-sensitive property offences, pre-pandemic breaks for selected violence-related categories consistent with shifting baselines, and delayed breaks in late 2021 to mid-2022 that are consistent with, though not uniquely attributable to, adaptation and digitalisation. Overall, the findings support a multi-phase interpretation of pandemic-era crime change and underscore the importance of aligning inference about disruption mechanisms with offence-specific opportunity structures and measurement conditions in recorded crime.

title: Racial, Socioeconomic, and Structural Determinants of Age-adjusted Excess COVID-19 Mortality Across U.S. Counties.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To examine racial, socioeconomic, and structural disparities in age-adjusted excess COVID-19 mortality across U.S. counties and identify contextual factors associated with disproportionate mortality. METHODS County-level data from all 3,142 U.S. counties and the District of Columbia were assembled from ten national datasets. Age-adjusted excess COVID-19 mortality was calculated using national age-specific COVID-19 mortality rates. Data-driven variable selection was performed using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, followed by population-weighted linear regression with state-clustered standard errors. RESULTS Excess mortality varied substantially across counties (mean 29.2 per 100,000; range - 593.4 to 879). Counties with larger Black populations, greater racial segregation, higher socioeconomic disadvantage, lower educational attainment, and higher uninsured prevalence experienced significantly greater excess mortality. Percentage of female-headed family households with no husband present (β = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.34-0.41) and Republican vote share (β = 0.22, 95% CI: 0.19-0.24) were positively associated with mortality, whereas remote work prevalence was inversely associated. CONCLUSIONS Racial and structural inequities remain strongly associated with unequal mortality across U.S. Addressing persistent inequities in education, healthcare access, neighborhood disadvantage, and economic opportunity may improve resilience to future pandemics and other population health threats.

title: Prescription of inhaled corticosteroid in children before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic: time trends and regional differences in Norway
abstract: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICSs) are the basic treatment for asthma, but prescription rates are markedly higher in preschool children than older children, a pattern not explained by asthma prevalence. This study examined time trends in ICSs prescription rates in Norwegian children before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Annual data (2013–2025) on children with at least one dispensed ICSs prescription were obtained from the Norwegian Prescribed Drug Registry (NorPD), stratified by age group (0–4, 5–9, 10–14 years), sex, and county. For 2019–2022 we obtained monthly data. Rates per 1000 children were estimated using Poisson regression. Among children aged 0–4 years, prescription rates declined slightly before the Covid-19 pandemic, declined a further 19% in 2020, rose above pre-pandemic levels by 2022, then declined again through 2025. Rates in 5–9-year-olds were stable through the pandemic but rose significantly from 2021 to 2024. Rates in 10–14-year-olds remained stable, with a moderate increase from 2022. Monthly data showed a sharp pandemic-onset rise in March 2020 followed by markedly low rates in young children, then pronounced winter peaks in subsequent seasons. Regional variation was substantial, greatest in the youngest group (> 3-fold between counties), the variations were largely consistent over time. ICS prescription rates in Norwegian children vary substantially by age, season, year, and region, particularly in children 0–4 years. These patterns suggest ICS may be overprescribed for infection-related respiratory symptoms in young children, while recent trends may also reflect improved guideline adherence.

Regional variation was substantial, greatest in the youngest group (> 3-fold between counties), the variations were largely consistent over time. ICS prescription rates in Norwegian children vary substantially by age, season, year, and region, particularly in children 0–4 years. These patterns suggest ICS may be overprescribed for infection-related respiratory symptoms in young children, while recent trends may also reflect improved guideline adherence.

title: Developing Drawing Skills Among Unemployed Youth through WhatsApp-based Creative Learning During COVID-19 in a Rural Western Cape Town: An Arts-based Study
abstract: This paper examines how drawing skills can be taught to unemployed youth in under-resourced contexts to support the expression of their lived experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic. Framed within a vocational education and training (VET) skills ecosystem orientation, the study positions creative skills development as part of broader human development and livelihood sustainability initiatives in informal settings. The paper aims to explore the potential of arts-based research (ABR) as a pedagogical and methodological approach for developing 21st-century skills, with a specific focus on drawing as a tool for communication and reflection during a crisis. We employed a qualitative arts-based research design that combined creative workshops, visual artefacts, and participant reflections. Due to pandemic-related restrictions, the research design was adapted to a digital environment, with WhatsApp used as the primary platform for skills instruction, interaction, and data collection. The dataset comprised visual drawings produced by unemployed youth participants, reflective narratives, and facilitator observations generated during a series of online creative workshops. The qualitative and visual data were analysed thematically, resulting in six key themes that captured participants’ experiences of unemployment, uncertainty, resilience, identity, and the challenges of learning creative skills in a digitally mediated, resource-constrained context. The main findings demonstrate that (i) drawing skills can be effectively taught using low-cost digital platforms, even in under-resourced settings; (ii) creative processes enable unemployed youth to articulate and reflect on their lived experiences during a pandemic; and (iii) a VET-oriented skills ecosystem provides a useful framework for situating arts-based skills development within broader livelihood and social support structures. Despite a small sample size, the study contributes practical insights into conducting arts-based research during crises and offers guidance for integrating creative skills development into informal youth skills ecosystems.

title: COVID-19 infection and Hong Kong elementary children's Chinese and English reading proficiencies: Parent-reported proficiency versus performance-based reading tests.
abstract: Previous studies investigated the effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on children's language development. This study explored the association between different COVID-19 infection statuses (children with no history of infection, children with a history of infection, and children with long COVID symptoms) and Hong Kong elementary children's Chinese and English reading performance. Participants were 195 dyads of parents and elementary children from Grades 1-6 (Mage = 8;8, SDage = 1;7, 89 boys and 106 girls) in 2022-2023. We adopted a 3 x 3 between-participant design. The two independent variables were COVID-19 status and grade levels. The dependent variables were parents' ratings of reading proficiencies, reading proficiencies in Chinese and English, and the differences between the parents' ratings and reading proficiencies. All measures (the language experience and proficiency questionnaire for parents' ratings, Chinese word reading battery, and the Wechsler Individual Achievement Test - Third Edition) were adapted from published works and showed high reliability in our sample. Using Multivariate Analysis of Covariates (MANCOVA) and Analyses of covariance (ANCOVA), we examined the links of infection with covariates, including parents' education level, number of children in the family, and monthly household income. We found that long COVID status was associated with lower parent-rated Chinese reading in the upper grades and lower Chinese spelling performance. Grade-specific differences in parent-performance discrepancy scores were also observed. These findings highlight the need for further longitudinal investigations and needs-based monitoring using both caregiver reports and performance-based assessments for children experiencing persistent health and learning difficulties.

title: An Investigation of Personal and Social-Contextual Resources as Mediators of the Influence of Duration of COVID-19 Pandemic Exposure and Mentoring Program Participation on the Mental Health and Well-Being of Adolescents
abstract: Although a sizable body of research indicates deterioration in the mental health of adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic, the mediating processes accounting for these effects as well as the potential for community-based prevention programs to offset and/or buffer declines in mental health during this period have received limited investigation. The present study addressed these gaps using data from a randomized controlled trial of the Big Brothers Big Sisters of America Community-based Mentoring Program in which there was naturally occurring variation in the extent to which the 18-month window between baseline and an initial follow-up assessment overlapped with the pandemic. Structural equation modeling analyses revealed support for hypothesized indirect associations of pandemic exposure with negative change in mental health and well-being via co-occurring declines in levels of personal and social-contextual resources, as well as a partially offsetting indirect association of mentoring program participation with improved mental health via an increase in personal resources. Mentoring program participation did not interact with pandemic exposure, and model pathways generally did not vary significantly by gender. Findings suggest that declines in adolescent mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic were linked to disruptions in their personal and social-contextual resources and that community-based mentoring interventions may at least partially offset pandemic-related declines in mental health.

title: Multifractality and time-varying market dynamics across sectors: Evidence from Brazil during the global financial crisis and COVID-19
abstract: This study examines the multifractal properties and time-varying scaling of four Brazilian sectoral indices during the Global Financial Crisis (GFC) and the COVID-19 pandemic. Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (MF-DFA) is combined with shuffled and phase-randomized series, formal moving-block bootstrap comparisons, rank Gaussianization, finite-sample simulations, matched fractional Gaussian noise (fGn), parameter sensitivity checks, and rolling windows. Point estimates of multifractal intensity are generally larger during the GFC, particularly for the financial sector, but none of the cross-crisis or cross-sector differences is statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment. The transformed-series diagnostics indicate substantial sensitivity to heavy-tailed marginal distributions, especially during the GFC. Relative to matched finite-sample fGn, all four GFC series retain excess spectrum width, whereas during COVID-19 only the real estate sector does so at the 5% level under the \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$q\in [-4,4]$$\end{document} validation. Rolling estimates vary over time but overlapping 250-day windows generate frequent false excursions under monofractal simulations; they are therefore interpreted as exploratory regime indicators rather than formal break tests. The evidence supports multifractal scaling in Brazilian sectoral returns while showing that finite-sample effects, marginal tails, and statistical uncertainty preclude universal claims of genuine multifractality or statistically established sector and crisis rankings.

title: CURRÍCULO, TECNOLOGIA E INOVAÇÃO NO ENSINO DA EDUCAÇÃO FÍSICA ESCOLAR DURANTE A PANDEMIA COVID-19
abstract: O presente artigo analisa as inter-relações entre inovações curriculares, mediação tecnológica e o ensino da Educação Física Escolar no contexto do Ensino Remoto Emergencial (ERE) decorrente da pandemia de Covid-19. A investigação caracteriza-se como uma pesquisa qualitativa, de caráter exploratório e analítico, delineada sob os preceitos da revisão integrativa da literatura, a partir de buscas sistematizadas nas bases SciELO, Portal de Periódicos da CAPES, Google Acadêmico e normativas da Base Nacional Comum Curricular (BNCC). O fechamento das escolas impôs o desafio ontológico de tematizar a cultura corporal de movimento mediada por telas e ambientes virtuais, ressignificando o papel docente para além da reprodução de exercícios mecânicos ou fitness doméstico. Constata-se que o uso de plataformas digitais, aplicativos de mensagens instantâneas e recursos audiovisuais viabilizou práticas híbridas e apropriações conceituais relevantes, embora tenha descortinado severas assimetrias socioeconômicas e exclusão digital. Conclui-se que as tecnologias digitais não anulam a dimensão corporal da disciplina, mas consolidam-se como ferramentas estruturantes para a flexibilização curricular, personalização do ensino e diversificação das linguagens pedagógicas no cenário pós-pandêmico.

title: eHealth-Guided Exercise Improves Peak Oxygen Uptake and Health-Related Quality of Life After COVID-19: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE Physical activity (PA) levels declined during the COVID-19 pandemic, contributing to reduced fitness and quality of life. eHealth tools may help increase PA. In a six-month randomized controlled trial, we evaluated Activity Quotient (AQ), an innovative eHealth tool designed to promote PA and improve peak oxygen uptake (V̇O2peak), compared with standard advice on national PA recommendations in physically inactive adults recovering from COVID-19. METHODS Seventy-seven participants with previous COVID-19 infection were randomized 1:1 to either receive: 1) an eHealth-guided exercise intervention (n=38), using AQ to motivate for a PA dose that led to >100 weekly AQs, or 2) a control group (n=39) advised to follow standard PA recommendations. V̇O2peak scaled for fat-free mass (FFM) was the primary outcome, assessed in a subsample of participants who completed clinical assessment (n=33; eHealth group n=16, control n=17), while secondary outcomes included physical and mental scores of health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze the effects of the intervention. RESULTS Participants (79% women) were 41.4±10.0 years and had a BMI of 28.8±5.9 kg/m2. Among 33 participants who completed clinical assessment, V̇O2peak increased 4.9 mL•kgFFM -1•min -1 (95%CI 1.2 to 8.7, p=0.0134) more in the eHealth group compared with controls. Mental HRQoL increased by 9.8 points (95% CI 2.5 to 17.0, p=0.009) more in the eHealth group compared with controls. No between-group difference was observed in physical score of HRQoL. CONCLUSIONS A six-month eHealth-guided exercise intervention using AQ was more effective than standard PA advice in improving V̇O2peak and mental HRQoL among physically inactive adults recovering from COVID-19. These findings highlight the potential of AQ as an effective and feasible approach for post-COVID rehabilitation.

title: Sustained increases in ADHD medication use after the COVID-19 pandemic: A nationwide register-based study.
abstract: Aims: To examine population-level trends in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) medication use in Norway before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic, and to identify age and sex groups with particularly pronounced changes, using interrupted time series analysis to test for a shift in trend from 2020. Methods: Using nationwide Norwegian prescription registry and population data (2009-2024), we calculated annual prevalence of dispensed ADHD medications (ATC code N06BA) across age and sex strata. Interrupted time-series quasi-Poisson regression models were fitted to quantify changes in trends associated with the pandemic period. Results: The analytical sample included 63,737,063 person-years. ADHD medication use was relatively stable until 2020, followed by a sharp, sustained acceleration across all groups. The largest increases occurred among females aged 15-24 years, where annual growth rates rose by 19 percentage points after 2020 (from 5.2% to 24.4% annually). Males aged 15-24 showed the strongest acceleration among men (+9.0 percentage points, from 2.7% to 11.7% annually). Conclusions: The pandemic period coincided with a durable shift in ADHD pharmacotherapy rather than a transient disruption, with particularly pronounced changes in groups historically considered underdiagnosed. Further research is warranted to determine whether this acceleration reflects improved detection or potential overuse.

title: Occupational risk of incident COVID-19 related hospital admissions in two Nordic countries with relaxed and rigorous lockdown.
abstract: AIMS To compare COVID-19 related hospital admissions among employees in two Nordic countries that applied a relaxed (Skåne, Sweden) and a rigorous (Denmark) lockdown during the pandemic. METHODS We did a register-based follow-up study of the incidence of first-time COVID-19 related hospital admission among all employees aged 20-69 years in Skåne and Denmark. Analyses were performed separately at each site, but according to a uniform study protocol. Adjusted incidence rate ratios (IRRs) during follow-up, 2020 and 2021, for 30 selected occupations were computed by Poisson regression using a reference population of mainly office workers. RESULTS The incidence of COVID-19 related hospital admission was 2.02/1000 person-years in Skåne (2443 admissions among 607,179 individuals) and 1.01/1000 person-years in Denmark (4416 admissions among 2,451,542 individuals). The relative risk of COVID-19 related hospital admission was increased among healthcare and transportation workers in both countries (Skåne: IRR 1.38 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.18-1.60) and 1.33 (95% CI 1.08-1.78), respectively; Denmark: IRR 1.56 (95% CI 1.39-1.75) and 1.48 (95% CI 1.23-1.78), respectively). The relative risk for occupations within education, retail sales, and a broad group of service occupations were, with few exceptions, not increased in either country. There was no indication of higher relative risks in Skåne compared with Denmark-if anything the opposite. CONCLUSIONS The relative risk of COVID-19 in at-risk occupations was not higher in a country with relaxed lockdown compared with a country applying rigorous legal lockdown. However, higher absolute risk of infection in Skåne, Sweden might have attenuated occupational differences in hospital admissions.

title: The development finance regime complex and crisis response: a comparative perspective of multilateral development banks’ response to COVID-19
abstract: This article explains variation in multilateral development banks’ (MDBs) crisis-response policies during the COVID-19 crisis. Drawing on a focused, structured comparison of 22 MDBs, this study analyzes five crisis-response policies: investment scale-ups and resource repurposing; institutional restructuring; fast-track facilities and procedures; policy and scope expansions; and inter-institutional collaboration and orchestration. It argues that MDBs’ crisis responses were shaped not only by institutional capacity but also by competitive pressures and hierarchical positioning within the development finance regime complex. MDBs occupying higher positions in the hierarchy demonstrated greater flexibility and were more likely to scale up lending, introduce expedited procedures, and expand operational scope, while lower-positioned MDBs adopted more cautious strategies and relied more heavily on cooperation with established MDBs. The analysis shows that some of this variation takes the form of patterned convergence in policy choices within hierarchical tiers and benchmarking practices across them, suggesting that hierarchy conditions both competition and coordination among MDBs during fast-moving crises and helps explain variation in countercyclical responses.
journal: Journal of International Relations and Development

title: The Influence of Crisis and Risk Communication Best Practices on COVID-19 Communication: A Content Analysis of Lessons Learned and Recommendations.
abstract: Despite the availability of crisis and risk communication best practices, scholars have analyzed and described the global COVID-19 pandemic communication failures that led to mass confusion about disease dynamics and appropriate protective behaviors. In this study, we sought to understand the alignment of crisis and risk communication best practices with national and international organizational lessons learned from COVID-19 pandemic responses. Our study design was a summative content analysis of a purposeful sample of COVID-19 lessons learned and recommendations reports published by US or international organizations between March 2020 and June 2024. Forty-four organizations published 61 reports, with 331 recommendations (24%) aligned with communication strategies, practices, behaviors, or actions. We identified 612 full or partial statements that aligned with at least 1 of 12 crisis and risk communication best practices. Alignment between the 12 crisis and risk communication best practices and report recommendations varied by best practice. "Take a process approach" was the best practice that aligned most frequently with recommendations and "explain risk in plain language" and show "an ethic of care" were the least frequently aligned with recommendations. Word cloud analyses showed alignment between best practice definitions and report recommendations. Our findings indicate that despite the critical nature of the work to inform the public, there is little international consensus on the use of 12 crisis and risk communication best practices that represent consolidated evidence about what works. Organizations' own reports and our analysis provide the blueprint for future robust crisis and risk communication emergency responses, if the organizations heed their own advice. We recommend that in advance of the next pandemic, organizations at all levels prioritize building awareness of and planning with these 12 best practices so they are prepared to fully listen to and respond to public's information needs.

title: Leadership, resilience and safety outcomes: A study of Indian construction workers post-COVID-19
abstract: Worker safety remains a serious concern for the Indian construction industry, where unsafe worker behaviour is a key contributor to workplace accidents, and leadership has a strong impact on safety behaviour. Construction industry researchers have largely focused on how leadership styles and safety climate affect employees' overall satisfaction. Prior research suggests that the quality of the association between leaders and followers may relate to followers' resilience. Leader–member exchange (LMX) captures this relationship quality, defined by trust, mutual respect, support and role clarity between supervisors and workers. While earlier studies have generally treated LMX as a single, uniform construct, this study advances the literature by unpacking its four distinct sub-dimensions to better understand how each uniquely contributes to worker outcomes. By linking these sub-dimensions to resilience and safety behaviour amongst Indian construction workers in the post-coronavirus disease 2019 environment, this study offers a richer theoretical explanation and contextually relevant insights for strengthening leadership practices and safety management in high-risk settings. To reduce unsafe behaviour amongst construction workers, this study examined how the four sub-dimensions of LMX relate to employee resilience and safety behaviour. Hypothesised relationships were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling, with data collected from 139 construction workers across various construction companies in the Delhi/National Capital Region using purposive sampling. Results show a positive association between all four LMX dimensions: affect, contribution, loyalty and professional respect, and employee resilience. Additionally, employees' capability to cope with adverse situations enhances their safety behaviour, indicating that despite pandemic-related challenges, leaders' support, emotional connection, mutual goal setting and inspirational motivation helped employees overcome adversity, fostering intrinsic motivation to abide by safety norms and engage actively in safety behaviour.

title: How personality traits shape susceptibility to mental distress in times of crisis: Evidence from the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Empirical evidence indicates that societal crises and adverse conditions can negatively impact population mental health. The Big Five personality traits – neuroticism, extraversion, openness, agreeableness, and conscientiousness –significantly influence stress responses. In this article, we examine how personality traits were associated with mental distress during and in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on data from the Understanding America Study, we find that, since the pandemic began, individuals with high levels of neuroticism were more likely to experience mental distress. By contrast, the remaining personality traits exhibited weaker, inconsistent, or statistically insignificant associations with mental health trajectories. Further analyses indicate that the heightened vulnerability among individuals high in neuroticism was accompanied by elevated risk perceptions, differential adoption of protective behaviors, and less adaptive coping patterns. Taken together, these findings suggest that personality-linked differences, particularly driven by the level of neuroticism, help explain heterogeneity in mental health responses to large-scale societal stressors. Our findings point to the relevance of personality traits (particularly neuroticism) for identifying individuals who may benefit from targeted mental health support during future crises.

title: Dinamika Pertumbuhan Ekonomi, Inflasi, dan Suku Bunga Riil Sebelum dan Selama Pandemi COVID-19
abstract: Pandemi COVID-19 mengguncang pertumbuhan ekonomi, inflasi, dan suku bunga riil secara bersamaan, tetapi kajian yang menempatkan ketiganya dalam satu sistem dinamis pada data bulanan masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis dinamika dan keterkaitan ketiga variabel tersebut sebelum dan selama pandemi. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif dengan data sekunder bulanan periode Januari 2016 sampai Desember 2020 sebanyak 60 observasi. Pengolahan data dilakukan dengan perangkat lunak EViews. Analisis mencakup uji akar unit, penentuan lag optimum, uji stabilitas model, uji kausalitas Granger, uji kointegrasi Johansen, estimasi Vector Error Correction Model, fungsi respons impuls, dekomposisi varians, dan uji diagnostik residual. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ketiga variabel stasioner pada diferensiasi pertama, lag optimum berada pada lag dua, dan model memenuhi syarat stabilitas. Kausalitas Granger hanya ditemukan dari pertumbuhan ekonomi ke inflasi. Uji Johansen mengindikasikan hubungan keseimbangan jangka panjang, dan koefisien koreksi kesalahan signifikan pada persamaan inflasi serta suku bunga riil, tetapi tidak pada persamaan pertumbuhan ekonomi. Residual bebas dari autokorelasi dan heteroskedastisitas, tetapi tidak berdistribusi normal akibat pencilan ekstrem. Dekomposisi varians memperlihatkan bahwa guncangan pertumbuhan ekonomi menjadi sumber utama variasi inflasi. Implikasinya, pembuat kebijakan perlu memantau ketiga indikator secara bersamaan ketika terjadi guncangan besar. Temuan ini perlu ditafsirkan secara hati-hati karena sampel yang pendek dan pelanggaran asumsi normalitas.

title: Breastfeeding Cessation Across Gestational Ages Among First-Time U.S. Mothers before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic, 2016-2021.
abstract: BACKGROUND The early COVID-19 pandemic period, with contact restrictions that affected in-hospital supports, provides a unique opportunity to examine changes in population-based breastfeeding cessation rates across the full spectrum of gestational age (GA) among first-time U.S. METHODS Using serial cross-sectional data from the Pregnancy Risk and Assessment Monitoring System (2016-2021), we included women from 19 U.S. jurisdictions who reported ever breastfeeding and cessation reasons (weighted N = 1,724,352). Weighted multivariable Cox regression compared cessation rates by GA between pre-COVID (2016-2019) and during-COVID (2020-2021) periods. Cessation reasons were assessed by prematurity using weighted Chi-square analysis (weighted N = 689,756). RESULTS During pre-COVID years, cessation rates among mothers of extremely preterm (EP) infants were 31% lower (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 0.69, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.53-0.89) compared to term mothers; very or moderately preterm (VMP) and late preterm (LP) mothers had higher cessation rates compared to term and EP mothers. Between periods, a 47% increase was observed among EP mothers (aHR: 1.47, 95% CI: 0.97-2.27). Only LP mothers had higher cessation rates relative to term mothers during COVID (aHR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.06-1.46). Compared to mothers of EP (9.8%) and term (11.8%) infants, more mothers of VMP (16.2%) and LP (16.6%) infants reported too many household duties (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION This study found that first-time U.S. mothers of VMP and LP infants breastfed for a shorter duration than their EP and term counterparts before COVID-19. The first two pandemic years were the most disruptive for EP mothers, highlighting the importance of in-hospital breastfeeding support.

title: Left Behind Places and Regional Resilience to COVID-19 Shock in Europe
abstract: Current turbulent times pose challenges not only for countries, but also-and above all-for regions within them. However, economic resilience of left behind places is still underexplored, especially in the light of entrenched regional disparities. The aim of this paper is to investigate the nexus between regional development and economic resilience across 898 European NUTS 3 regions during the COVID-19 pandemic. To go beyond the GDP-based approach, we construct a multidimensional "left behindness" index. Our findings show that left-behind places, as identified through this multidimensional approach, were relatively more successful in resisting the immediate pandemic shock, while more developed regions demonstrated a stronger recovery capacity. The analysis also highlights that international trade, industrial specialization and the share of public employment acted as determinants of these divergent resilience trajectories. The results suggest that policymakers should adopt a differentiated strategy by strengthening the resistance of more advanced regions and enhancing the recovery capacity of left behind places to reduce persistent regional disparities.

title: Impacts of COVID-19 on well-being during deployment and the role of leadership
abstract: Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic created new challenges, adding or compounding the effects of many existing stressors that military personnel face during deployment. While these stressors can negatively impact individual and organizational outcomes by worsening well-being and performance, research suggests that subordinates’ trust in leadership may help improve these outcomes and mitigate the negative effects of these stressors. Methods: The present study examined the effects of COVID-19-, deployment-, and family-related concerns on the morale, psychological distress, occupational performance, and levels of job stress experienced by Canadian Armed Forces personnel deployed on international operations (n = 256) and the moderating role of trust in leadership in these relationships. Results: Moderated linear and logistic regressions revealed that deployment-related concerns emerged as the primary driver of poor outcomes (higher levels of job stress and psychological distress, lower morale), although none of the concerns were related to greater self-perceived occupational impairment. By contrast, greater trust in leadership was associated with better well-being outcomes and a lower likelihood of occupational impairment. However, trust in leadership did not moderate the association between concerns and outcomes. Discussion: These findings highlight that deployment-related concerns are a salient driver of diminished well-being. Further, while trust in leadership did not moderate these relationships, it directly predicted all well-being and performance outcomes, highlighting its critical role in supporting well-being independent of reported level of concerns.
journal: Journal of Military Veteran and Family Health

title: Integrating in vitro and in silico correlation of thiazole-based carboxamide derivatives as promising SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease inhibitors: a versatile approach for COVID-19 therapy
abstract: Abstract A new series of thiazole-based carboxamide derivatives (5–12) was designed, synthesized with structural elucidation performed using standard spectroscopic techniques including NMR and HRMS. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) and compared with the reference inhibitor GRL0617 (IC50 = 2.73 ± 2.20 μM). Among the tested compounds, compounds (8) (IC50 = 1.94 ± 1.50 μM) and (6) (IC50 = 2.53 ± 1.90 μM) exhibited the most potent inhibitory activity, outperforming or matching the reference inhibitor, while the remaining compounds showed moderate to good PLpro inhibition. Structure–activity relationship analysis was supported by molecular docking studies, which demonstrated that compound 8 possessed the strongest binding affinity (−7.875 kcal/mol), forming key hydrogen bonds with Gly163 and Gly271. Compound (6) also showed favorable binding (−7.426 kcal/mol), establishing similar hydrogen bonding interactions together with additional hydrophobic contacts within the active site. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provided insights into the electronic properties underlying molecular reactivity and stability, whereas in silico ADME analysis predicted favorable pharmacokinetic characteristics and drug-likeness. Collectively, these experimental and computational findings identify thiazole-based carboxamide derivatives, particularly compounds (8) and (6), as promising candidates for the development of potent SARS-CoV-2 PLpro inhibitors.
journal: Zeitschrift für Naturforschung C - A Journal of Biosciences

title: Management of Disputes in the Construction Industry during COVID-19: Contractors’ Takeaways for Future Pandemics
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic intensified construction disputes. While dispute management has been widely studied, limited research has examined pandemic-induced disputes globally, especially within the Sri Lankan construction context. Hence, this study aims to investigate how to manage the disputes due to COVID-19 in the Sri Lankan construction industry, considering the contractors’ perspective. The study adopts an interpretivist philosophy and employs a qualitative Delphi technique involving two iterative rounds of semistructured interviews, thereby making a methodological contribution. The data were analyzed through manual content analysis. The findings reveal six positive impacts and 12 negative impacts of COVID-19 on the construction industry, along with suitable preventive measures to manage the 12 important causes of disputes arising from the pandemic. This is positioned as one of the limited studies identifying both positive and negative impacts and suitable preventive measures in managing the identified causes. The findings can be applied for developing contexts of a similar nature, particularly in managing disputes during future pandemics.
journal: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction

title: IMPACTOS ECONÔMICO-FINANCEIROS AOS ALUNOS DO CURSO DE ADMINISTRAÇÃO NA UNIVERSIDADE FEDERAL DE PELOTAS DECORRENTES DA COVID-19
abstract: A economia financeira é um tema que possui relevância na vida de todos, mas principalmente aos alunos do curso de administração. Quando se trata sobre impactos financeiros aos alunos do curso de Administração da Universidade Federal de pelotas questiona-se como estes se saíram financeiramente em uma crise global inimaginável como a da COVID-19. O presente artigo busca compreender e dar respostas a essa questão, avaliando qual o grau de endividamento dos alunos do curso baseando-se em questionários socioeconômicos e questões baseadas em hábitos econômicos financeiros além de compreender se os alunos dos semestres do curso de Administração entendem a importância da educação financeira e da reserva de emergência para situações como a que o mundo tem vivenciado nos últimos dois anos com a pandemia. title: DIAGNÓSTICO DIFERENCIAL DE OPACIDADES EM VIDRO FOSCO: DA COVID-19 RESIDUAL A LESÕES PRÉ-MALIGNAS
abstract: A opacidade em vidro fosco (OVF) é um achado frequente e desafiador na tomografia computadorizada (TC) de tórax, cuja relevância cresceu com o aumento de exames realizados durante e após a pandemia de COVID-19 e com a consolidação do rastreamento do câncer de pulmão por TC de baixa dose. Na prática, o radiologista precisa diferenciar OVF residuais de natureza infecciosa/inflamatória, que tendem à resolução espontânea, daquelas pertencentes ao espectro pré-invasivo e invasivo do adenocarcinoma pulmonar. O objetivo deste estudo foi sistematizar os principais critérios de imagem que auxiliam nessa diferenciação. Trata-se de uma revisão narrativa da literatura, com busca nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase e LILACS/BVS, priorizando publicações dos últimos dez anos, além de diretrizes e consensos de sociedades. Os achados foram organizados por eixo etiológico e comparados quanto a distribuição, margens, densidade interna, componente sólido, sinais associados e evolução temporal, incluindo as recomendações da Fleischner Society e do Lung-RADS v2022. Conclui-se que nenhum critério morfológico isolado permite essa diferenciação com segurança absoluta e que a avaliação temporal seriada permanece como a ferramenta mais robusta, cabendo ao radiologista adotar vigilância criteriosa e comunicar com clareza o plano de seguimento.

title: Challenges and Opportunities in Building a Post-Covid-19 Small and Medium Enterprise Entrepreneurship Ecosystem in Bali
abstract: One of the biggest challenges for Small and Medium Enterprises (SME’s) post-COVID-19 is establishing an entrepreneurial ecosystem that is both holistic and resilient. The challenge is relates to two main perspectives: expanding digital transformation and strengthening an integrated entrepreneurial ecosystem. This article argues that one of the main challenges, as well as an opportunity for SME’s development, is establishing a community-based entrepreneurial ecosystem based on the needs of the SME’s themselves. Various empowerment programs and the creation of entrepreneurial ecosystems that have been implemented so far have been top-down, focused on government interests and dependent on government policies. Furthermore, entrepreneurial ecosystem programs targeting SME’s are not a priority in these villages. This article demonstrates that the biggest challenge in building an integrated entrepreneurial ecosystem is that it touches on the ability to identify self-potential, social capital, and the independence of SME’s entrepreneurs, whose characteristic.

title: Biye And Getage: Community Health Resilience During COVID-19 in Indonesia's Geographically Isolated Ulu Ogan Community.
abstract: Geographically isolated rural communities face compounding structural barriers to formal healthcare, yet their capacity to organize health governance through culturally embedded frameworks remains undertheorized in health communication scholarship. Using the culture-centered approach (CCA) as theoretical framework and analytical lens, this qualitative study examined how the Ogan Malay community of Ulu Ogan, South Sumatra, Indonesia, mobilized cultural practices to sustain health resilience during COVID-19 amid structural marginalization. Through in-depth interviews with 17 informants, we analyzed the dynamic interplay between cultural agency, structural constraints, and geographical isolation. Findings document two indigenous governance frameworks-biye (institutionalized mutual aid) and getage (collective crisis preparedness)-through which the community organized health action without adequate state support. Rather than passively receiving official directives, communities demonstrated sophisticated hybrid governance: selectively adapting formal health protocols through local moral logics, mobilizing ecological health literacy rooted in agrarian embodied knowledge, and developing culturally grounded pandemic responses that formal health systems failed to provide. Critically, traditional and religious leaders were formally listed in governance structures but systematically excluded from substantive authority-constituting what this study theorizes as performative inclusion, a distinct modality of epistemic violence that manufactures the appearance of participatory governance while preserving centralized biomedical control. These findings advance CCA scholarship by reframing subaltern agency as organizational capacity, theorizing hybrid governance as dialectical co-production, and introducing performative inclusion as a new analytic concept for health communication. Implications call for health governance models that move beyond nominal community participation toward genuine redistribution of epistemic authority and decision-making power.

title: Assessing microbial safety and food safety knowledge and practices among representative fast-food restaurants in the United Arab Emirates during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: To date, no studies have examined the status of food safety knowledge and practices among representative fast-food restaurants and vendors in Abu Dhabi (Al Ain City). The primary objective of this study was to assess awareness of food safety practices and attitudes and to examine their effects on consumer health in representative fast-food restaurants. The research was conducted at 6 fast-food vendors across various locations in Al Ain City, Abu Dhabi. A desirable practice scored one, whereas an undesirable practice received no score, as determined by a standardized questionnaire applied to all food establishments. We used this scoring system to see how each operation's percentage score compared with the maximum possible score for that operation. To test for significant differences among the attributes analyzed across food outlets and suppliers, an analysis of variance was conducted (significance level: p<0.05). The study demonstrated significant differences among various vendors regarding the production area (78-94%), production safety (61-100%), and physical facilities ranging between 38% and 88%. Product-related aspects range from 29% to 88%. Food handlers' and personal hygiene practices ranged from 47% to 83%. Finally, knowledge of food safety and equipment availability ranged from 50% to 78%. The total count did not exceed the standard values, and the TVC ranged from 2 to 4 log CFU/mL. The coliform count exceeded the standard levels in some places. The study's findings indicate inadequate hygiene practices among food workers in food-preparation areas. In conclusion, further efforts are necessary to ensure safe food handling and production. This research will contribute to the development of educational programs to enhance food safety.

title: PREVALENSI DAN DETERMINAN INTENSI UNTUK BERHENTI MEROKOK SELAMA COVID-19 DI ACEH
abstract: Merokok masih menjadi salah satu masalah kesehatan masyarakat yang berkontribusi terhadap meningkatnya risiko penyakit kronis dan kematian yang dapat dicegah. Intensi berhenti merokok merupakan tahap penting dalam perubahan perilaku karena menjadi dasar seseorang untuk melakukan upaya penghentian merokok. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui prevalensi dan determinan yang berhubungan dengan intensi berhenti merokok pada masyarakat perokok aktif di Aceh selama pandemi COVID-19. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan desain cross-sectional. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 593 responden yang dipilih menggunakan random sampling. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji chi-square dan analisis multivariat. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sebanyak 367 responden (61,89%) memiliki intensi berhenti merokok. Analisis bivariat menunjukkan bahwa pengetahuan, sikap, lingkungan, dukungan keluarga, dan media informasi berhubungan signifikan dengan intensi berhenti merokok. Hasil analisis multivariat menunjukkan bahwa sikap merupakan faktor paling dominan dengan AOR 6,21 (95% CI: 3,97–9,70; p=0,000), diikuti oleh dukungan keluarga dengan AOR 5,13 (95% CI: 3,28–8,02; p=0,000). Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa perubahan sikap positif dan penguatan dukungan keluarga menjadi aspek penting dalam meningkatkan intensi berhenti merokok pada masyarakat.

title: Exposure Records Preserved by Two Users of Japan's COVID-19 Contact-Confirming Application During the Seventh Wave: A Descriptive Study
abstract: Introduction: Japan's COVID-19 Contact-Confirming Application (COCOA) stopped functioning in November 2022, and the records held on users' devices were lost with it. We describe the exposure records preserved by two users during the seventh wave of COVID-19 in Japan and the changes around the revision of full mandatory case reporting on September 26, 2022. Methods: We analyzed exposure windows (date, duration, and minimum attenuation) contained in files exported from the app. Observer 1 worked at a hospital in Tokyo and commuted almost exclusively by private car; Observer 2 lived in Kyoto Prefecture and spent most of the time at home. Seven-day rolling sums of exposure windows were compared descriptively with daily new case counts in each prefecture. Results: During the common pre-revision period (April 3 to September 25, 2022; 176 days), Observer 1 recorded 358 exposure windows and Observer 2 recorded 261. The rolling sums rose in July and fell in September, as did new case counts (r-squared = 0.807 and 0.397), but week-on-week changes corresponded weakly (r-squared = 0.183 and 0.002). Of the windows in this period, 97.2% and 93.1% had a minimum attenuation of 65 dB or more, the bucket given the lowest weight in the notification decision. After the revision, Observer 1 recorded three windows in 27 days (45 in the preceding 27 days), and Observer 2 recorded none in 23 days (25 in the preceding 27 days). Conclusions: The exposure-window records of two users rose and fell with the seventh wave, although the correspondence of week-to-week changes was limited. Recorded windows decreased after the revision, but the effects of the policy change, the supply of diagnosis keys, app usage, and operating-system updates cannot be separated. This descriptive report does not evaluate the preventive effectiveness of COCOA. It shows that indicator definitions, retrieval dates, and the history of software and policy changes are essential when records left on users' devices are analyzed after the fact.

title: Coronavirus nucleocapsid proteins differentially antagonize RIG-I-like receptor signaling to shape pathogenicity
abstract: Coronaviruses cause human infections with divergent clinical outcomes. Viral proteins likely play important roles in the severity of human diseases but are poorly defined. In this study, we discovered that viral nucleocapsid (N) proteins from various human coronaviruses have distinct abilities to antagonize human innate immune responses. N proteins from more pathogenic coronaviruses, such as SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2, have more potent activities specifically against human RIG-I-like receptor (RLR) activation than less pathogenic coronaviruses including OC43 and HKU1. Mechanistically, the SARS-CoV-2 N protein interacts with RLR pathway viral RNA sensors MDA5 and RIG-I and inhibits their interaction with MAVS. The CTD of SARS-CoV-2 N protein is an important region for RLR antagonism. Consequently, N proteins from more pathogenic coronaviruses promote viral replication more effectively than N proteins from less pathogenic coronaviruses. Blocking N protein function may be a promising antiviral strategy.

title: Multiple Sclerosis and Viruses: « Liaisons Dangereuses ».
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a complex, multifactorial neurodegenerative disease with an aetiology that is still partially elusive. Several risk factors are associated with MS development including genetic predisposition and various environmental stressors; however, recently, viral infections have gained significant attention as a crucial environmental trigger. Despite the well-established link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and MS susceptibility, a single-pathogen model fails to clearly characterise the molecular cascades driving the disease, suggesting that the transition from infection to autoimmune response involves more than one viral agent. In this review we examine the speculation that the interactions among different neurotropic viruses could serve a collective causative role in MS, which is under-researched in the literature at present. We summarise contradictory evidence on the role of different viral agents, including the Herpesviridae family (Human Cytomegalovirus, EBV, Herpes Simplex Viruses HSV-1 and HSV-2, and Varicella Zoster Virus), Paramyxoviridae family (Measles Virus and Rubella Virus), Influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs). Through interplay within shared molecular pathways, immune modulation, and activation of latent infections, these viruses may collectively influence the inflammatory and demyelinating processes that characterise MS. This review evaluates the etiological role of viral interplay in MS through the cumulative and interactive effects of these pathogens. The available epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data converge on the concept that viral co-exposures act synergistically to shape MS susceptibility in genetically predisposed individuals. Characterising these viral interactions presents a new research direction for the identification of novel biomarkers and the development of preventative strategies through the targeted control of viral networks.

Several risk factors are associated with MS development including genetic predisposition and various environmental stressors; however, recently, viral infections have gained significant attention as a crucial environmental trigger. Despite the well-established link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and MS susceptibility, a single-pathogen model fails to clearly characterise the molecular cascades driving the disease, suggesting that the transition from infection to autoimmune response involves more than one viral agent. In this review we examine the speculation that the interactions among different neurotropic viruses could serve a collective causative role in MS, which is under-researched in the literature at present. We summarise contradictory evidence on the role of different viral agents, including the Herpesviridae family (Human Cytomegalovirus, EBV, Herpes Simplex Viruses HSV-1 and HSV-2, and Varicella Zoster Virus), Paramyxoviridae family (Measles Virus and Rubella Virus), Influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs). Through interplay within shared molecular pathways, immune modulation, and activation of latent infections, these viruses may collectively influence the inflammatory and demyelinating processes that characterise MS. This review evaluates the etiological role of viral interplay in MS through the cumulative and interactive effects of these pathogens. The available epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data converge on the concept that viral co-exposures act synergistically to shape MS susceptibility in genetically predisposed individuals. Characterising these viral interactions presents a new research direction for the identification of novel biomarkers and the development of preventative strategies through the targeted control of viral networks.

title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.
abstract: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

title: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen identifies host dependency factors and potential viral-induced cell death regulators for porcine deltacoronavirus infection
abstract: Porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV) is a globally circulating coronavirus of swine that causes severe enteric disease and mortality in neonatal piglets. Its broad host range and zoonotic potential raises concerns about continued spillover into human populations. However, the host factors that govern PDCoV infection remain largely unexplored. Identifying host factors involved in virus infection may uncover novel therapeutic targets for antiviral drug development or targets for gene editing to create resistant pigs. Here, we conducted a genome-wide CRISPR knockout (GeCKO) screen to identify host factors contributing to PDCoV infection in swine testicular (ST) cells. Small guide RNAs (sgRNAs) targeting the ANPEP gene, expressing the main receptor porcine aminopeptidase N for PDCoV, were enriched in PDCoV-resistant cells, demonstrating the validity of the screen. Moreover, we identified transmembrane protein 30A (TMEM30A), an accessory β-subunit of the P4-ATPase flippase complex, as a host dependency factor for PDCoV infection along with several potential PDCoV-induced cell death regulators, including DET1, IFNAR1, RFWD2, STAT1 and TP53. We further demonstrated that PDCoV attachment and internalization into cells were significantly impaired in TMEM30A knockout ST cells, suggesting that TMEM30A is important in the early stages of the PDCoV life cycle. Because TMEM30A also contributes to SARS-CoV-2 replication, future studies are warranted to investigate its mechanistic role in the context of coronavirus infection.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Regional Health Information Exchange (HIE)-Based Platform for Population-Level Infectious Disease Surveillance
abstract: Background Health Information Exchanges (HIEs) offer a potential resource for timely, population-level infectious disease surveillance by integrating electronic health record data across healthcare systems. Methods We developed an end-to-end informatics pipeline for near-real-time community-level health surveillance based in a regional HIE serving Southeast Texas. We identified deidentified individual-level COVID-19, influenza, and RSV cases using diagnosis codes and laboratory results and assessed demographic and temporal trends from January 2022 through August 2026. Results We identified 492,242 COVID-19 cases, 343,977 influenza cases, and 33,159 RSV cases during the study period. Surveillance data captured expected seasonal patterns, including recurring winter COVID-19 and influenza peaks and shifting RSV epidemiology, while enabling monitoring of laboratory test positivity metrics and hospitalization trends across age groups. Conclusions HIE-based surveillance provides scalable, near-real-time monitoring of disease targets across large populations. HIE infrastructure can enhance public health situational awareness and complement traditional surveillance systems by harmonizing vital health data across systems and providers and delivering timely, standardized, and representative population health indicators.

title: Control-Polygon Epidemiology: A Bernstein-Bezier Framework for Epidemic Reconstruction, Forecasting, and Control
abstract: Abstract Many data-driven biological systems must be reconstructed from observations, forecast under uncertainty, and steered toward desired outcomes, yet these tasks are often assigned different model representations. In computational epidemiology, this fragmentation obscures parameter meaning and makes model outputs harder to compare and communicate. We introduce 'control-polygon epidemiology', a unified Bernstein-Bezier framework in which an effective reproduction-number trajectory is encoded by a small set of interpretable control points. Historical polygons are estimated by constrained least squares or Bayesian negative-binomial renewal inference; forecasts attach new, smoothly joined Bernstein segments instead of extrapolating the historical polynomial; and inverse control maps a desired epidemic trajectory back to feasible intervention intensity, implementation speed, uncertainty, and cost. The representation yields global convex-hull threshold certificates, finite-difference momentum and curvature, coefficient-level uncertainty propagation, spectral calibration to mechanistic models, and structural lower bounds: C transversal threshold crossings require at least C + 1 control points, while E isolated interior extrema require at least E + 2. Synthetic experiments span renewal, SIR, SEIR, SIRS, vector-borne, age-structured, vaccination, isolation/hospitalization, and overdispersed observation models. In Philippine COVID- 19 rolling-origin tests, a history-only peak-aware continuation improved on the original joined-Bernstein forecast in 87.5% of origin–horizon comparisons and on a constant-Rt baseline in 75%, while stress tests correctly exposed the impossibility of forecasting genuinely unobserved structural shocks from case history alone. The framework provides a low-dimensional bridge between statistical learning, mechanistic transmission models, probabilistic forecasting, and interactive decision science.

title: Privacy-Preserving, Decentralised Inference of Epidemic Transmission Dynamics from Digital Exposure Histories
abstract: BackgroundExposure-history data collected during epidemics or pandemics within digital contact-tracing applications hold immense potential for rapid, scalable epidemiological inference. The sensitivity of these data makes privacy-preserving designs essential to secure public trust and app uptake. However, during the COVID-19 pandemic, such approaches were not yet available at the scale or maturity required for deployment. We present a Bayesian decentralised framework to infer transmission dynamics from exposure-history data while protecting user privacy. MethodsOur approach is based on iterative communication between user devices and a central server, computing log-likelihood gradients on device from exposure-history data and centrally updating parameter values using only aggregated gradients. Applying this framework to synthetic exposure-history data from a hypothetical respiratory pathogen epidemic simulated on dynamic contact networks, we assessed its ability to estimate the underlying transmission parameters, perform infector attribution, and reconstruct serial-interval (SI) distributions. We systematically explored how inference was affected by incomplete exposure-history data arising from partial app adoption, case under-ascertainment, and incomplete exposure logging, and by transmission scenarios. FindingsOur decentralised framework accurately recovered transmission parameters, closely matching estimates derived from centralised data with no systematic bias in posterior means. Parameter recovery remained robust when hazards from unobserved exposures were known as a daily average across the population. Although incomplete exposure-history data and specific transmission scenarios introduced compensatory parameter biases, the inferred host infectiousness profile retained sufficient accuracy, and the weekly SI distributions reconstructed from infector attributions closely resembled the ground-truth distributions. InterpretationOur findings highlight that, beyond its primary role as a control measure, digital contact tracing could help characterise transmission dynamics almost in real time and inform public health interventions while preserving user privacy. FundingOxford Martin School Programme on Digital Pandemic Preparedness; National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Health Protection Research Unit in Emerging and Zoonotic Infections. Evidence before this studyWe searched PubMed for studies published from database inception to Sept 30, 2026, using the keywords ("digital contact tracing" OR "exposure notification" OR "contact tracing app") AND ("federated learning" OR "decentralised" OR "privacy-preserving" OR "statistical inference" OR "Bayesian inference") AND ("transmission" OR "serial interval" OR "infectiousness"). During the COVID-19 pandemic, digital contact-tracing (DCT) apps were deployed at an unprecedented scale: 224 COVID-19 apps were launched across 127 countries, 128 of which supported exposure notification. In England and Wales, the NHS COVID-19 app had 16.5 million regular users (28% of the total population) and averted an estimated 1 million cases and 9,600 deaths in its first year. To protect privacy, however, most apps used decentralised architectures that kept exposure-history data on users devices. This privacy-preserving principle has largely prevented these data from being used for epidemiological inference to understand transmission dynamics, such as estimating the serial-interval (SI) distribution and host infectiousness profile over time. While existing decentralised algorithms estimate each users infection risk, we found no study that developed and evaluated a framework for estimating population-level epidemiological parameters from exposure-history data that remain on users devices. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first such framework. It estimates key quantities required for understanding transmission dynamics, including how an infected individuals infectiousness changes over time relative to their symptom onset date, how much close contacts increase the risk of transmission, and the SI distribution. The framework learns an exposure hazard function from data that never leave users devices, then attributes infections to likely infectors, and reconstructs the SI distribution. We applied the framework to synthetic exposure-history data from epidemics simulated on dynamic contact networks of 166,034 individuals, matching the 2024 population of Oxford, UK. It produced estimates comparable to those from centralised analysis, identified the timing of peak host infectiousness relative to symptom onset to within one day, and reconstructed SI distributions that closely tracked the ground truth. We also systematically assessed how participation levels (app adoption and case ascertainment), technical limitations (incomplete exposure logging), and surveillance (knowledge of the background hazard from unobserved exposures) affected inference, and showed that daily population-level knowledge of the background hazard was sufficient for reliable inference. Implications of all the available evidenceBeyond their role as a control measure, DCT apps could provide timely, population-representative estimates of key transmission parameters, such as the host infectiousness profile and SI distribution. Our findings show that such inference is feasible within the privacy-preserving architectures likely to underpin future DCT systems. Greater app adoption, case ascertainment, and exposure logging would improve inference accuracy. To realise this potential, the framework will need to be embedded in DCT systems, supported by concurrent epidemiological research, real-world validation, and early collaboration with public health authorities and platform providers.
