title: Revenue Models and Funding Dynamics of Healthcare-technology Startups in India: An Empirical and Analytical Study
abstract: India’s healthcare-technology (HealthTech) startup sector has changed into one of the most volatile segments of the Indian startup economy since the COVID-19 pandemic. Due to these recent and rapid changes, it becomes pertinent to analyse the trends prevailing in this sector. This paper focuses on examining the revenue generation and funding behaviour of Indian HealthTech startups. The study collected secondary data from funding-intelligence platforms such as Tracxn, Inc42 Datalabs, Entrackr/TheKredible, regulatory and industry literature, and company financial disclosures from firms such as PharmEasy, Tata 1mg, Practo, Pristyn Care, MediBuddy, Innovaccer, Cult.fit and MFine. The study maps annual funding trends and firm-level cumulative funding raised. Furthermore, it analyses revenue performance through mix of monetisation strategies such as e-pharmacy/marketplace commission, teleconsultation subscription and lead-generation fees, enterprise healthcare SaaS/data-platform subscriptions, elective-procedure marketplace fee-sharing, wellness-subscription-plus-diagnostics-commission models. The pilot survey was conducted with a structured questionnaire administered to practising Chartered Accountants, finance faculty, and healthcare-startup finance professionals to gauge perceived determinants of fundability in the post funding winter environment. The survey data was further examined through correlation, reliability (Cronbach’s alpha), exploratory factor analysis, and OLS regression to identify respondents’ perception and their association with overall fundability. Findings indicate that Indian HealthTech funding has followed a non-linear path surging during the pandemic to ₹7,590 crore in 2022, collapsing by more than half to ₹3,461 crore in 2023, and then rebounding sharply to ₹9,436 crore in 2024. A volatility pattern distinct from the steady decline observed in India’s FinTech sector over the same period. A detailed case study of PharmEasy, whose valuation fell from ₹41,720 crore in October 2021 to ₹3,967 crore in 2025 rights issue (a decline of roughly 90 per cent), illustrates the sector’s acute correction in capital intensive e-pharmacy models, while more capital efficient, recurring revenue models (enterprise SaaS, elective-procedure marketplaces) have shown comparative resilience. The paper argues that regulatory uncertainty (e-pharmacy rules, telemedicine guidelines, data-privacy compliance) functions as a distinctive risk factor for Indian HealthTech relative to other startup categories. Revenue-model diversification and a credible path to profitability are now weighted more heavily by both investors and practitioners than growth alone. The study also observed that funding is increasingly concentrated among a small set of category leaders and diagnostics/enterprise-SaaS niches. The study concludes with suggestions for founders, investors, regulators and accounting academics, and identifies avenues for further empirical and longitudinal research.

title: Bridging the intention‒behavior gap in herpes zoster vaccination: A nationwide survey in a self-payment setting.
abstract: Herpes zoster (HZ) causes substantial morbidity, yet global uptake remains suboptimal where the vaccine is excluded from universal coverage. Taiwan exemplifies such a self-payment setting, with the HZ vaccine self-financed and local government subsidies restricted to limited eligible groups. This study analyzed data from a nationwide, web-based cross-sectional survey of adults aged ≥18y fielded in 2025, examining factors associated with HZ vaccination behavior, intention, and willingness to pay (WTP). Of 1690 respondents, 281 (16.6%) were vaccinated; among 1409 unvaccinated, 1140 (80.9%) were willing to vaccinate. title: Respiratory Viruses and Pulmonary Diseases: Mechanisms, Therapies, and Metabolic Reprogramming.
abstract: Respiratory viral infections constitute a substantial global health challenge, extending their impact beyond acute inflammation to encompass long-term pulmonary sequelae. Recent evidence highlights that respiratory viruses such as influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 reprogram host metabolism to facilitate their replication, with significant alterations in glucose metabolism playing a critical role. This metabolic reprogramming augments glucose metabolism via activation of core signaling pathways including PI3K/Akt/mTOR, HIF-1α, and c-Myc. Beyond facilitating viral proliferation, these metabolic changes crosstalk with oncogenic signaling. By triggering chronic inflammation, oxidative stress and genomic damage, they disrupt the pulmonary immune microenvironment and ultimately promote the pathogenesis of lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The pathogenesis of these symptoms is multifactorial and is influenced by genetic susceptibility, environmental exposure, and key interactions between persistent viral infection and the host's immune system. In this review, we synthesize recent advancements on the molecular mechanisms linking virus-induced metabolic alterations to the progression of pulmonary diseases. Furthermore, we discuss novel therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting these metabolic vulnerabilities to mitigate the long-term risks associated with respiratory infections.

title: Respiratory Pathogen Spectrum Among 12,220 Testing Episodes for Clinically Suspected Acute Respiratory Infection in Predominantly Hospitalized Patients at a Tertiary Hospital in Wuhan, China, 2025: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) impose a substantial global disease burden, yet the post-pandemic pathogen spectrum in central China remains incompletely characterized. This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 12,220 consecutive testing episodes in which a 12-pathogen multiplex PCR panel was ordered for selected patients with clinically suspected ARI at Wuhan No. 1 Hospital in 2025; 99.7% occurred during hospitalization. Overall pathogen detection was 30.3% (3705/12,220). Human rhinovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen (8.84%), followed by influenza A virus (5.29%), respiratory syncytial virus (4.75%), SARS-CoV-2 (4.13%), and human coronavirus (3.77%). Detection rates varied by age (children 60.4% vs. adults 23.3% and elderly 24.6%) and season (autumn 34.1%, winter 33.1%, spring 29.2%, summer 25.4%), with a monthly peak in November (39.3%) and trough in August (21.5%). Co-detection of two or more pathogens occurred in 343 positive episodes (9.26%), with HRV plus RSV being the most common pairing (12.8%). In multivariable analysis, clinical department (pediatrics aOR 5.84, 95% CI 3.69–9.49; hematology aOR 2.19, 95% CI 1.76–2.74) and season (autumn aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.39–1.77) were independently associated with pathogen detection, whereas sex was not. The strong pediatric age association (aOR 4.99, 95% CI 4.42–5.65) was attenuated to non-significance after adjustment for department (aOR 1.30, 95% CI 0.82–2.00), reflecting near-complete overlap between young age and pediatric attendance, which precludes separation of the two effects; within childhood, detection nevertheless decreased with increasing age (p for trend < 0.0001). These findings characterize pathogen detection among predominantly hospitalized patients with clinically suspected ARI at a single tertiary center and may inform local diagnostic stewardship and infection-control practice.

title: Healthcare-associated infections and antimicrobial use in a Greek tertiary hospital: two cross-sectional point-prevalence surveys in 2012 and 2022
abstract: Abstract Objective: To describe and cautiously compare two cross-sectional snapshots of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and antimicrobial use (AU) at the same Greek tertiary hospital in 2012 and 2022. Design: Secondary analysis of two cross-sectional point-prevalence surveys using European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control protocol versions 4.3 and 6.1. Setting: A public tertiary-care university referral hospital in northwestern Greece. Patients: Eligible inpatients present in participating wards before 08:00; 276 patients were included in 2012 and 391 in 2022. Methods: Patient-level HAI prevalence was the primary comparison, and AU prevalence was secondary. Infection site, microbiological, susceptibility, antimicrobial indication, and prophylaxis findings were analyzed descriptively because only aggregate outputs were available. Results: HAI prevalence was 23/276 (8.3%) in 2012 and 48/391 (12.3%) in 2022 (prevalence ratio [PR], 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.92–2.36; P = .126). AU prevalence was 147/276 (53.3%) and 206/391 (52.7%), respectively (PR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.86–1.14; P = .937). Pneumonia was the most frequently recorded infection-site category in both surveys. Surgical prophylaxis exceeded 1 day in 51/58 (87.9%) courses in 2012 and 47/48 (97.9%) in 2022. Protocol-year carbapenem non-susceptibility markers were frequent among small numbers of tested isolates. Conclusions: Both snapshots showed substantial HAI and AU burdens. The observed HAI difference cannot be separated from changes in patient mix, season, the COVID-19 pandemic, surveillance practices, and protocol definitions. Prolonged surgical prophylaxis was highly prevalent at both survey dates and represents a clear stewardship target.

title: Association between air sampling for viral respiratory pathogens and acute respiratory tract infection cases in the emergency department
abstract: Abstract The emergency department (ED) is a common site for respiratory viral surveillance, but air sampling has not been thoroughly explored in this setting. In this study, we observed a significant association between COVID-19, influenza A, and RSV detection via air sampling in an ED waiting room and clinical viral testing.

title: Introduction
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly changed the employment landscape for people with disabilities (PWD) in the Western world and in a few LMICs. This introduction is an important road map clarifying the rest of the book. Chapter 2 discusses employment for PWD in the twenty-first century, including before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic, primarily in the United Kingdom and United States, and in LMICs. Chapter 3 discusses the experiences of workers with disabilities during the pandemic in the United Kingdom and United States, as well as in LMICs, where employees with disabilities faced disproportionate job losses, reduced hours, and increased health risks during the pandemic due to preexisting inequalities. Chapter 4 introduces a comparison between UK and US policies regarding employees with disabilities during and post-pandemic and reviews the policies in a few LMICs. Chapter 5 reviews and discusses the benefits and challenges of PWD in the United Kingdom and United States regarding working from home in the post-pandemic era. Chapter 6 estimates which future jobs would be available for PWD post-pandemic in the United Kingdom and United States. A central part of the chapter is artificial intelligence (AI), which can offer a significant potential to enhance future work opportunities for PWD in both the United Kingdom and United States through advanced assistive technologies (AT) and flexible work options. In the concluding remarks there is a discussion of five themes regarding the benefits and disadvantages of the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the employment of PWD.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Is Wastewater Surveillance Predictive during the Endemic Phase of Respiratory Disease? An Analysis Based on Clinical, Wastewater, and Digital Search Data in Detroit, Michigan
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has emerged as a major public health innovation catalyzed by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, its potential remains underexplored during and after COVID-19’s transition to endemicity. This study evaluates WBE’s potential to identify the COVID-19 pandemic-to-endemic transition and to provide early warnings across multiple surveillance systems for influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in the postpandemic era. We monitored SARS-CoV-2 N1 concentrations in wastewater from April 8, 2020, and July 31, 2025, generating the earliest and longest-running wastewater dataset in Detroit, MI. A peak identification method was implemented to identify the pandemic-to-endemic transition by comparing the frequency of N1 concentration peaks between phases. During the endemic phase, from October 1, 2022, and March 31, 2025, we monitored RSV, IAV, IBV, and SARS-CoV-2 in Detroit’s wastewater. Pearson correlations were implemented to quantify the associations between wastewater concentrations and clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological data. Time-lagged cross-correlation (TLCC) was used to examine temporal dynamics among these datasets and identify the earliest emerging data for each disease and time lags. Extensive literature studies were conducted to elucidate the time-lag mechanisms for each disease, embracing the TLCC results. Random forest models were established to predict clinical cases based on WBE datasets. This was among the first studies using WBE-based approaches to identify pandemic-to-endemic transition of SARS-CoV-2. The relationships of wastewater data to traditional clinical, syndromic, and digital epidemiological surveillance data were systematically analyzed during the endemic phase of these respiratory diseases. This study demonstrates the predictive value of WBE during the endemic phase, providing early warnings and predictions for seasonal respiratory diseases, including COVID-19, influenza, and flu-like disease.

title: Handgrip strength parameters as predictors of post-COVID syndrome severity and muscle weakness in an observational study
abstract: Abstract Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) presents with persistent symptoms such as fatigue, muscle weakness, and cognitive impairments, which often impact quality of life. This study determines handgrip strength (HGS) using a digital hand dynamometer as an objective measure of muscle function in PCS, aiming to assess its utility in symptom quantification and explore its relationship with endothelial dysfunction (ED) and inflammatory markers. In a cohort of 102 patients with PCS (77 women and 25 men), 62 of 101 classified patients (61.4%) fulfilled criteria for myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). HGS parameters, including mean HGS, fatigability, and recovery, were assessed. Patients with ME/CFS exhibited lower mean HGS ( p = 0.031), greater fatigability ( p = 0.042), and poorer recovery ( p = 0.048) compared with patients without ME/CFS. Furthermore, HGS parameters were significantly correlated with PCS severity and patient-reported outcome measures (including COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale, PCS Severity Score and Fatigue Severity Scale). A gender-specific analysis revealed associations between HGS and ferritin in males (r = 0.42, p = 0.036) and thrombocyte levels inversely related to muscle recovery (r = − 0.43, p = 0.030), potentially indicating microvascular compromise. Elevated intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) levels were observed in patients with reduced recovery and VEGF was inversely correlated with fatigability in ME/CFS patients (r = − 0.26, p = 0.044), suggesting that ED is involved in PCS-related muscle dysfunction. Anti-S1 IgG titers correlated negatively with HGS in females (r = − 0.24, p = 0.040), suggesting a potential role of viral persistence in muscle impairment. These findings underscore the role of HGS in PCS assessment, revealing phenotype- and gender-specific impairments and highlighting the need for further research into ED pathways and targeted rehabilitation strategies to enhance PCS management.

Elevated intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) levels were observed in patients with reduced recovery and VEGF was inversely correlated with fatigability in ME/CFS patients (r = − 0.26, p = 0.044), suggesting that ED is involved in PCS-related muscle dysfunction. Anti-S1 IgG titers correlated negatively with HGS in females (r = − 0.24, p = 0.040), suggesting a potential role of viral persistence in muscle impairment. These findings underscore the role of HGS in PCS assessment, revealing phenotype- and gender-specific impairments and highlighting the need for further research into ED pathways and targeted rehabilitation strategies to enhance PCS management.

media_mentions.content: Abstract Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) presents with persistent symptoms such as fatigue, muscle weakness, and cognitive impairments, which often impact quality of life. This study determines handgrip strength (HGS) using a digital hand dynamometer as an objective measure of muscle function in PCS, aiming to assess its utility in symptom quantification and explore its relationship with endothelial dysfunction (ED) and inflammatory markers. In a cohort of 102 patients with PCS (77 women and 25 men), 62 of 101 classified patients (61.4%) fulfilled criteria for myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). HGS parameters, including mean HGS, fatigability, and recovery, were assessed. Patients with ME/CFS exhibited lower mean HGS (p = 0.031), greater fatigability (p = 0.042), and poorer recovery (p = 0.048) compared with patients without ME/CFS. Furthermore, HGS parameters were significantly correlated with PCS severity and patient-reported outcome measures (including COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale, PCS Severity Score and Fatigue Severity Scale). A gender-specific analysis revealed associations between HGS and ferritin in males (r = 0.42, p = 0.036) and thrombocyte levels inversely related to muscle recovery (r = − 0.43, p = 0.030), potentially indicating microvascular compromise. Elevated intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) levels were observed in patients with reduced recovery and VEGF was inversely correlated with fatigability in ME/CFS patients (r = − 0.26, p = 0.044), suggesting that ED is involved in PCS-related muscle dysfunction. Anti-S1 IgG titers correlated negatively with HGS in females (r = − 0.24, p = 0.040), suggesting a potential role of viral persistence in muscle impairment. These findings underscore the role of HGS in PCS assessment, revealing phenotype- and gender-specific impairments and highlighting the need for further research into ED pathways and targeted rehabilitation strategies to enhance PCS management. Similar content being viewed by others Introduction In the aftermath of COVID-19, a considerable cohort of individuals continue to struggle with a complex array of symptoms, extending beyond the acute phase of the infection. This condition is recognized as Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS) or Long COVID1,2. PCS is defined by the World Health Organization (WHO) as symptoms persisting for a minimum of two months within three months following a SARS-CoV-2 infection; these symptoms must affect daily functioning and cannot be explained by an alternative diagnosis3. With an estimated incidence of 10–20% and more than 651 million documented SARS-CoV-2 cases worldwide, PCS presents immense challenges to healthcare systems worldwide4,5,6,7. PCS is characterized by symptoms such as fatigue, myalgia, exertional intolerance, postexertional malaise (PEM), cognitive and autonomic dysfunction, and headaches1,8. Within this spectrum, a large subset of patients meets the diagnostic criteria for postinfectious myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS)9,10. The prevalence of postinfectious ME/CFS was substantial even before the COVID-19 pandemic, affecting approximately 3 million individuals on the European continent. With the increased incidence of COVID-19, the emergence of ME/CFS after infection poses a considerable challenge for healthcare and society11. Endothelial dysfunction (ED) and persistent inflammation are increasingly recognized as critical factors in the long-term complications of COVID-19 and ME/CFS12,13. Adhesion molecules such as ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 play central roles by mediating leukocyte adhesion and migration, contributing to endothelial inflammation in patients and leading to impaired lung function and vascular damage in PCS14,15,16,17,18. ED may lead to muscle weakness by reducing microvascular blood flow, thereby limiting oxygen and nutrient delivery to muscle tissues and causing muscle fatigue and decreased strength. This suggests that ED could be a contributing factor to persistent symptoms such as muscle weakness and fatigue in PCS19. Given the potential role of ED in PCS-related functional impairment, objective measures of muscle performance are of particular interest. Handgrip strength (HGS) is an objective measure of muscle strength widely studied in sarcopenia as a predictor of mortality and morbidity20,21,22,23,24,25. Given the role of muscle weakness in PCS, HGS is increasingly relevant and is associated with poorer functional outcomes26,27. Accordingly, patients with PCS are expected to exhibit reduced handgrip strength, with impairments extending beyond normal age- and gender-related differences in muscle function. While sarcopenia denotes age-related muscle loss, the term dynapenia refers to reduced muscle strength and power and is preferred in the context of PCS28. While previous studies have examined the associations between functional outcomes and handgrip strength (HGS) in patients with PCS, an in-depth characterization of patient-reported outcomes (PROMs), which capture patients’ subjective symptom burden, functional limitations, and quality of life through validated questionnaires, and their specific relationships with HGS is still needed. Therefore, the primary aim of this study was to characterize handgrip strength (HGS) parameters, with a particular focus on muscle recovery, as objective measures of muscle function in patients with PCS and to relate these to clinical phenotypes, including ME/CFS. A comprehensive set of PROMs was collected, and two distinct questionnaires were employed to assess PCS severity. As a secondary aim, we investigated associations between HGS parameters and biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction and inflammation, to better understand potential mechanisms contributing to muscle weakness in PCS. Materials and methods Study design and cohort This study is part of the "All Eyes on PCS" study, a prospective, observational single-center study focused on examining the retinal microvasculature of PCS patients and providing a comprehensive clinical characterization. A detailed description of patient recruitment and clinical characterization can be found in the study protocol published previously29. Patients were eligible if they had a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection (PCR or antibody test ≥ 3 months prior) and persistent PCS-typical symptoms lasting ≥ 2 months without an alternative explanation. Exclusion criteria comprised missing consent, age < 18 years, pregnancy, malignancy, conditions markedly reducing life expectancy, rheumatological autoimmune disease, and ocular or neurological disorders (cataract, glaucoma, epilepsy). Between October 2022 and September 2023, 105 patients were recruited via social media (76/105) and from the PCS outpatient department (29/105). Three patients were excluded from the data analysis (one due to a lack of proof of infection, one due to a lack of temporal association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the onset of PCS symptoms, and one because they no longer exhibited PCS-typical symptoms on the day of recruitment). Data were collected at TU Munich (Departments of Nephrology, Neurology, and Ophthalmology) by experienced examiners who were aware of the study context but not involved in hypothesis formulation or statistical analyses. The study protocol received approval from the local ethics committee (Ethics Committee of the Technical University of Munich, School of Medicine, Klinikum rechts der Isar; Approval number: 2022-317-S-SR) and was registered in advance (https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT05635552). All procedures were conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and relevant institutional guidelines and regulations. Written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The final analysis cohort comprised 102 patients with PCS. Median age was 41.5 years (IQR 32.0–52.0), and 77 participants (75.5%) were female and 25 (24.5%) male. Median symptom duration at the time of assessment was 404 days (IQR 291.0–566.0). Most patients had experienced a mild to moderate acute infection not requiring hospitalization (59.8% severity grade 2), and 62 of 101 classified patients (61.4%) fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for ME/CFS. Baseline characteristics of the full cohort are provided in supplementary Table 1. Sample size The present work is a secondary analysis of the prospective "All Eyes on PCS" study. The sample size of this study has been calculated for the primary outcome concerning retinal vessel analysis29. This study was designed as a case–control study comparing patients with PCS to recovered individuals without persistent symptoms, and a target of 100 participants per group was derived from published normative data and expected between-group differences in retinal vessel parameters, allowing for potential dropouts. The present analysis includes the PCS group only (n = 102). No a priori sample size calculation was performed for HGS. Handgrip strength measurement The handgrip strength (HGS) of the dominant hand was assessed via a digital hand dynamometer (Jamar) across two separate sessions. Each session was separated by a 60-min rest period during which participants engaged in no strenuous physical activity. The Jamar dynamometer is widely regarded as the gold standard for HGS assessment, with excellent validity and high test–retest and inter-rater reliability in both clinical and research settings20. To minimize learning effects and motivational bias, participants were familiarized with the device and measurement procedure prior to testing. During each session, participants were seated upright with elbows at 90° flexion and forearms fully supinated. All measurements were conducted under standardized conditions by trained examiners, who provided identical verbal instructions and standardized verbal encouragement to ensure consistent maximal effort. Each contraction lasted three seconds, followed by a five-second rest, repeated ten times per session. The device automatically recorded the peak value of each contraction (kg). To estimate strength, fatigability, and recovery, we analyzed various parameters and ratios as previously described30, as outlined in Table 1. Normative values for Fmax were adjusted for age and gender31. Patient-related outcome measures COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRS) The C19-YRS has 22 items, each rated on an 11-point scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 10 (extremely severe). It is divided into four subscales: symptom severity (0–100), functional disability (0–50), additional symptoms (0–60), and overall health (0–10)32. PCS Severity Score Twelve typical PCS symptoms are assessed and multiplied by a predetermined coefficient. This results in a total score ranging from 0 to 59 points. The higher the score is, the greater the PCS severity. The classification is divided into three groups: none/mild PCS (≤ 10.75), moderate PCS (> 10.75 and ≤ 26.25), and severe PCS (> 26.25)33. Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) This questionnaire covers nine signs and symptoms of fatigue, scored from 1 to 7. Therefore, a score of 9–64 points can be given; the higher the score is, the more severe the symptoms are34. 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) Recommended by many international guidelines, the PHQ-9 is a very reliable screening tool for depression. Nine symptoms of depression within the past two weeks were queried35. EuroQol 5-Dimensions 5-Levels questionnaire (EQ-5D-5L) Health-related quality of life was assessed via the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire, which evaluates five dimensions: mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression, each rated on a five-level scale36. Laboratory values Standard laboratory measurements were conducted in an ISO-certified laboratory. The serum levels of IL-6, IL-8, CXCL10, Rantes, ICAM, VCAM, VEGF, and MCP-1 were determined following previously described methods13. For the detection of von Willebrand factor (vWF) antigen (Ag) in human samples, we utilized the LIAPHEN vWF:Ag kit (HYPHEN BioMed, Neuville-sur-Oise, France), which is an immunoturbidimetric assay. To measure the levels of SARS-CoV-2 spike IgG in plasma samples, we employed an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Specifically, the LEGEND MAX ELISA kit from BioLegend was utilized, following the protocol provided by the manufacturer. Definition of subgroups Four subgrouping variables were used to define exploratory, hypothesis-generating subgroup analyses: Recovery ratio The recovery ratio (Fmean2/Fmean1, see Table 1) reflects the restoration of muscle strength after a 60-min rest and thus corresponds most closely to the delayed recovery after exertion that characterizes PEM30. As a within-patient ratio it is largely independent of age, gender, body composition and absolute strength, and it has an intrinsic physiological reference point close to 1.0 in healthy individuals30, which makes it suitable for dichotomization. As no established threshold for the recovery ratio exists, patients were dichotomized into abnormal (≤ 0.8, n = 23) and normal (> 0.8, n = 79) recovery; this data-driven cutoff approximately corresponds to the lower quartile of our cohort, and sensitivity analyses using 0.75 and 0.85 are reported in supplementary Table 8. ME/CFS ME/CFS was diagnosed according to the Canadian Consensus Criteria37 and patients were grouped by its presence (n = 62) or absence (n = 39). In one patient, the diagnostic criteria were not correctly applied, and the patient was therefore excluded from this classification. Gender Given known gender differences in muscle strength and the female predominance of PCS, correlations with laboratory markers were analyzed separately in male (n = 25) and female (n = 77) patients and tested for effect modification using age-adjusted interaction models. Depression Patients were stratified post hoc by PHQ-9 depression severity into 4 groups (PHQ-9 < 10: no depression, 10–14: mild depression, 15–19: moderate depression, ≥ 20: severe depression) to address whether reduced HGS reflects lack of drive rather than physiological impairment. Statistical analysis The statistical analysis was performed using R (version 4.2.1) and RStudio (version 2024.04.2 + 764) using the packages dplyr, tidyr, purrr, broom, pROC, ggplot2, car, and gt. Normally distributed values are presented as the means ± SDs, whereas nonnormally distributed values are presented as medians and interquartile ranges (IQRs). Categorical variables are presented as counts and percentages. Normality was analyzed via graphical analysis with histogram plotting and boxplotting and with the Shapiro‒Wilk test for normality. For comparisons of baseline characteristics, the Welch two-sample test was used for normally distributed variables, the Wilcoxon rank sum test was used for nonnormally distributed variables, and the chi-square test was used for categorical values. The ggpubr package was used to calculate Spearman ́s and Pearson ́s correlation coefficients to generate scatterplots. All models were specified a priori based on clinical relevance and previous literature. Age and gender were included as covariates in all multivariable models to account for known effects on muscle strength. No automated stepwise selection procedures were applied. For all logistic and linear regression models, standard diagnostic procedures were performed, including inspection of residuals, assessment of influential points (Cook’s distance), and evaluation of model fit (Hosmer–Lemeshow test for logistic models). No major violations of model assumptions were detected. Diagnostic plots for a representative model are shown in supplementary Fig. 1; similar results were observed for the remaining models. To examine the potential discriminatory ability of HGS parameters, receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed via the plotROC and pROC packages. The correlation matrix was created via the corrplot package. These analyses were exploratory in nature and intended to generate hypotheses for future studies rather than provide confirmatory evidence. We used the interaction package to generate the interaction plots; the pinteract was calculated via a multivariate linear regression model. All graphical plots were created using the ggplot2 package. All clinical data were typed by two independent researchers, who checked for mistakes. Results Patient characteristics A total of 102 patients with PCS with a previous history of SARS-CoV-2 infection and ongoing symptoms were recruited (see baseline characteristics of the full cohort in supplementary Table 1). Patients were categorized based on an abnormal recovery ratio, with a cutoff value of 0.8. Among them, 23 patients (mean age 44.1 ± 10.2 years, 82.6% female) had an abnormal recovery ratio, whereas 79 patients (mean age 41.2 ± 11.9 years, 73.4% female) had a normal recovery ratio. Concerning cardiovascular risk factors, PCS patients with abnormal recovery had significantly higher cholesterol levels (p = 0.03). In addition, we observed higher levels of ICAM-1 in PCS patients with abnormal recovery (p = 0.014). There was a tendency toward a history of more severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, this difference was not significant (p = 0.08). Interestingly, there was no significant difference in the duration of PCS. Further detailed demographic and clinical characteristics of the cohort are presented in Table 2, laboratory values of the cohort are shown in Table 3. HGS is correlated with PCS severity, C19-YRS score, and PROMs Figure 1 shows the different measures of HGS and their Pearson correlations with PCS severity scores and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). Patients with lower mean handgrip strength (Fmean) values presented more severe symptoms, as measured by the PCS severity score (r = − 0.31, 95% CI − 0.48 to − 0.12, p = 0.001) and the COVID-19 Yorkshire rehabilitation scale (C19-YRS; r = − 0.30, 95% CI − 0.47 to − 0.11, p = 0.004).…

title: Exposure route, not dose, is the primary driver of infection patterns for a respiratory virus
abstract: Infectious disease severity, shedding, and within-host kinetics can vary substantially with exposure dose, inoculation route, and host factors. However, the relative contributions of these variables to infection heterogeneity remain poorly quantified because small sample sizes in controlled in vivo experiments limit their statistical power and scientific scope. Here, by compiling and jointly analyzing the largest published database of nonhuman primate challenge experiments (107 studies; 721 animals), we show that exposure route drives SARS-CoV-2 infection kinetics more strongly than dose, age, sex, or species. Aerosol inoculation yields kinetics distinct from all other respiratory exposure routes. Route and dose jointly determine which tissues become infected, and 50% infectious doses vary greatly depending on the route of exposure and on the tissue sampled. Our findings underscore the central role of exposure route in pathogenesis and transmission, and highlight the untapped potential for quantitative, cross-study syntheses to extract additional insights from costly animal experiments.

title: Multiplexed Aptamer-Based Proteomic Data Normalization (Adaptive Normalization by Maximum Likelihood) Significantly Influences Results in Critically Ill Patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND Blood-based proteomics are employed in cohorts of patients with critical illness to provide biologic insights and improve diagnosis and risk stratification. Somalogic developed a multiplex aptamer-based platform (Somascan) with thousands of proteins assayed in a single plasma sample. Results are reported in 2 forms: (a) adaptive normalization by maximum likelihood (ANML), which normalizes measurements to a healthy US population and (b) a non-ANML-normalized form. It is unknown how ANML-normalization influences measurements and associations with outcomes. METHODS We correlated ANML and non-ANML protein quantification with 9 immunoassay biomarkers measured in the same patients' blood samples from the COVID-19 Host Response and Clinical Outcomes (CHROME) cohort. We compared the association of log2 relative fluorescent units (RFUs) with hospital mortality with and without ANML-normalization using adjusted (age, sex, body mass index [BMI]) logistic regression. Results report the odds ratio per doubling of each protein's RFU and declared significance at a false discovery rate (FDR) <0.05. RESULTS Among 197 patients the average age was 54 years (±16), 51% had COVID-19, 65% were male and hospital mortality was 26%. All biomarkers had equal or higher Pearson correlation between non-ANML-normalization and immunoassay data compared to ANML-normalization. Thousands of proteins changed directionality and significance for risk of mortality based on whether data was ANML-normalized, with 108 of the associations being significant in both, but opposite directionality. The paired Cohen D agreement between beta estimates was moderate (D = 0.61; 95% CI, 0.58-0.64). CONCLUSIONS In this cohort of critically ill patients, ANML-normalization attenuated correlations with immunoassays and largely changed the distribution and direction of significant mortality-associated proteins compared with non-ANML-normalization.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Kidney Transplantation at the Syzganov National Scientific Center of Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Introduction: Kidney transplantation has been actively developing in Kazakhstan, data on outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate recipient characteristics, patient survival, causes of ESKD, and renal graft function after KT. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 37 consecutive kidney transplant recipients who underwent KT between January 2020 and July 2025. Body mass index (BMI), etiology of ESKD, donor type, pre-transplant hemodialysis, mortality, and renal graft function were evaluated. Renal graft function was assessed using serial serum creatinine measurements during follow-up. Some recipients were lost to follow-up, which limited assessment of long-term graft function in these patients. Results: In the available follow-up data, renal function was generally satisfactory and remained stable in most recipients with observations. Graft survival was 86.5%, with graft loss documented in five recipients: three surviving recipients experienced rejection-associated graft loss, and two patients died following rejection. Among the five deaths, two were associated with confirmed COVID-19 infection, one was attributed to cerebral infarction caused by cerebral arterial thrombosis, and two were related to graft rejection. Among the three recipients with rejection-related complications, all experienced adverse effects associated with immunosuppressive therapy, including significant infectious complications. Discussion: An important consideration is that the study period overlapped with the COVID-19 pandemic. Registry data showed substantially increased infection-related mortality among kidney transplant recipients receiving chronic immunosuppression during 2020, with infection and COVID-19 accounting for a major proportion of excess deaths. Therefore, mortality and survival outcomes should be interpreted in the context of the pandemic, limiting direct comparison with pre-COVID-19 cohorts. Conclusion: Kidney transplantation at our center demonstrated favorable medium-term outcomes, with improvement in renal function and satisfactory outcomes in most recipients. Overall patient survival was 86.5%, and graft survival was also 86.5%. Continued monitoring of immunosuppression-therapy, complications, and long-term follow-up is important for improving patient and graft outcomes.

title: Impact of a national enrolment programme on preventive care uptake in Singapore: a cohort study of 268,315 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND Preventive care uptake in Singapore remains suboptimal despite longstanding national programmes. Healthier SG, launched in July 2023, aims to strengthen primary care through empanelment, continuity, and proactive health planning, but evidence on its effectiveness is limited. AIM To evaluate the association between Healthier SG enrolment and uptake of preventive care services. DESIGN & SETTING Retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from National Healthcare Group Polyclinics. METHOD Adults aged≥40 years with at least two annual visits between January 2018 and September 2024 were included. Outcomes were cervical cancer screening, influenza and pneumococcal vaccination, and cardiovascular risk screening. Quarterly uptake rates were analysed across four periods: pre-COVID-19, COVID-19, post-COVID-19/pre-Healthier SG, and post-Healthier SG. RESULTS Preventive care uptake in Healthier SG enrolees demonstrated more favourable uptake trajectories across all preventive care outcomes. For cervical cancer screening, uptake declined during COVID-19 and recovered thereafter. Following Healthier SG implementation, cervical screening showed a steeper upward trend among enrolees than non-enrolees (quarterly trend change+0.57% versus+0.05%). Although vaccination uptake declined after the post-pandemic peak, reductions were less pronounced among enrolees (influenza: -0.41% versus -2.18%; pneumococcal:+0.07% versus -1.13% per quarter). Cardiovascular risk screening demonstrated a ceiling effect, with a smaller decline among enrolees than non-enrolees (-0.03% vs -0.32%). Among eligible patients, lower enrolment in ethnic minority, single, lower SES housing suggest potential inequities. CONCLUSION HSG enrolment was associated with greater uptake of selected preventive services. As an observational study restricted to regular primary care users, findings may not be generalisable to less-engaged populations. Continued evaluation is needed to assess long-term impact and equity of preventive care uptake.

DESIGN & SETTING Retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from National Healthcare Group Polyclinics. METHOD Adults aged≥40 years with at least two annual visits between January 2018 and September 2024 were included. Outcomes were cervical cancer screening, influenza and pneumococcal vaccination, and cardiovascular risk screening. Quarterly uptake rates were analysed across four periods: pre-COVID-19, COVID-19, post-COVID-19/pre-Healthier SG, and post-Healthier SG. RESULTS Preventive care uptake in Healthier SG enrolees demonstrated more favourable uptake trajectories across all preventive care outcomes. For cervical cancer screening, uptake declined during COVID-19 and recovered thereafter. Following Healthier SG implementation, cervical screening showed a steeper upward trend among enrolees than non-enrolees (quarterly trend change+0.57% versus+0.05%). Although vaccination uptake declined after the post-pandemic peak, reductions were less pronounced among enrolees (influenza: -0.41% versus -2.18%; pneumococcal:+0.07% versus -1.13% per quarter). Cardiovascular risk screening demonstrated a ceiling effect, with a smaller decline among enrolees than non-enrolees (-0.03% vs -0.32%). Among eligible patients, lower enrolment in ethnic minority, single, lower SES housing suggest potential inequities. CONCLUSION HSG enrolment was associated with greater uptake of selected preventive services. As an observational study restricted to regular primary care users, findings may not be generalisable to less-engaged populations. Continued evaluation is needed to assess long-term impact and equity of preventive care uptake.

title: Hierarchical Triboelectric-Plasmonic-Coupled All-Fabric Dual-Mode Platform for Self-Powered Respiratory Monitoring and Electrostatic-Driven In Situ Pseudovirus Detection.
abstract: Respiratory infectious diseases represented by COVID-19 necessitate proactive wearable diagnostic platforms with high integration and sensitivity. In this study, we present a hierarchical, all-fabric dual-mode sensor seamlessly integrating a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for self-powered physiological pre-alert and a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrate for biochemical verification. The core innovation is a rationally engineered bilayer silver (Ag) fabric via secondary Ag plating (Ag nanoparticles: ∼16 nm bottom, ∼92 nm top), forming abundant plasmonic "hot spots" and enabling SERS detection with an LOD down to 10-16 M. Meanwhile, the same fabric serves as a robust TENG electrode paired with high-β-phase PVDF nanofibers (∼70% β-phase), enabling a power density of 461.28 mW m-2 and real-time respiratory monitoring within 99.4% antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. This "monitor-enrich-detect" triboelectric-plasmonic-coupled platform holds promise for early warning and risk mitigation of respiratory infectious disease transmission.

title: Trade policy uncertainty and risk spillovers in global currency markets
abstract: This paper examines how trade policy uncertainty (TPU) affects risk transmission in global foreign exchange markets. Using daily data for 20 major currencies from 2005 to 2025, we combine autoregressive exponential generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity with generalized error distribution (AR-EGARCH-GED) volatility estimates, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator vector autoregression (LASSO-VAR) connectedness measures, and a generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity mixed-data sampling (GARCH-MIDAS) framework that links monthly TPU to daily return and volatility spillovers. The results show that global FX markets are highly interconnected, with average return connectedness of 71.3% and volatility connectedness of 58.46%. Spillovers are time-varying and rise around major stress episodes, including the global financial crisis, Brexit, the USA–China trade war, the COVID-19 pandemic, and renewed trade-policy tensions in 2024–2025. The results also reveal a core-periphery structure: the Singapore dollar and the euro frequently act as important transmitters, while several emerging-market currencies mainly absorb external shocks. The US dollar appears relatively balanced on average, but its large two-way linkages confirm its continuing systemic role, especially during stress periods. This study develops a novel analytical framework that integrates the AR-EGARCH-GED model, LASSO-VAR spillover indices, and the GARCH-MIDAS approach. Using data on 20 major global currencies, we quantify heterogeneous effects of TPU, identify core and vulnerable currencies in the spillover network, and uncover the mechanisms through which TPU transmits across currency markets. The findings provide a theoretical foundation for policymakers seeking to mitigate TPU-related risks and promote financial stability, while also offering practical insights for international investors to optimize portfolio allocation and manage exchange rate exposure.

title: Social Innovation for Digital Equity in Healthcare: A Descriptive Environmental Scan of Selected Digital Initiatives in India
abstract: Digital inequities continue to limit equitable access to healthcare and related services in India, particularly among underserved populations. Social enterprises and nongovernmental organizations increasingly employ digital tools and innovations to support healthcare delivery, communication, and community engagement; however, systematic descriptive evidence regarding such initiatives remains limited. To describe the characteristics, scope, and patterns of digital initiatives implemented by selected social enterprises, nongovernmental organizations, and community-based organizations in India, with particular focus on digital health–related activities, beneficiary populations, and knowledge-exchange engagement. A cross-sectional descriptive environmental scan was conducted from February to July 2025 among 100 purposively selected organizations operating in India. Data were collected from organizational websites, publicly available reports, digital platforms, and direct communication using a structured data extraction tool developed from relevant literature and pilot reviewed before use. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for key proportions. Qualitative organizational descriptions were analyzed thematically to identify recurring domains of digital engagement using an inductive descriptive approach. All organizations reported use of at least one digital platforms for communication or service delivery, and 96% (95% CI: 90.1–98.9) maintained official websites. Common organizational focus areas included women’s empowerment (93%; 95% CI: 86.1–96.8), health-related activities (72%; 95% CI: 62.3–80.1), and education (48%; 95% CI: 38.0–58.2). Among organizations reporting COVID-19–related digital initiatives (n = 96), telehealth services (75%) and online education platforms (50%) were most frequently described. Women/girls and rural populations were the predominant beneficiary groups. Although all organizations perceived their initiatives as having potential for replication or scale-up, these findings were based on organizational self-report and were not independently validated. This environmental scan describes widespread adoption of digital communication and service-delivery tools among selected social innovation organizations in India. Although digitally enabled initiatives frequently targeted underserved populations, the study did not assess effectiveness or direct impact on digital equity outcomes. Further evaluative research is needed to determine the effectiveness and scalability of these initiatives.

title: Динамика смертности от болезней системы кровообращения в Российской Федерации и федеральных округах в 2017—2023 гг.
abstract: Болезни системы кровообращения (БСК) остаются одной из ведущих причин смертности населения Российской Федерации. Особый интерес представляет оценка изменений смертности от ишемической болезни сердца (ИБС) и острого инфаркта миокарда (ОИМ) в период пандемии COVID-19 и последующие годы, а также выявление территориальных различий. Цель исследования — оценить динамику смертности от БСК, ИБС и ОИМ в Российской Федерации в 2017—2023 гг., определить основные изменения показателей после периода пандемии COVID-19 и охарактеризовать межрегиональные различия по федеральным округам. Проведен ретроспективный анализ официальных статистических данных о смертности населения Российской Федерации от БСК, ИБС и ОИМ за 2017—2023 гг. Оценивалась цепная динамика показателей и динамика относительно исходного 2017 г., изменения в период пандемии и последующее восстановление, а также ранговое положение федеральных округов. Анализ выявил выраженную U-образную динамику смертности от БСК и ИБС с повышением показателей в 2020—2021 гг. и последующим их снижением. смертность от БСК и ИБС снизилась (по сравнению с 2017 г.) на 5,27 % и 5,28 %, соответственно. В то же время смертность от ОИМ имела отличную динамику. она превысила исходный уровень на 3,52 %. Была выявлена выраженная межрегиональная неоднородность показателей. При этом сохранение повышенной, относительно 2017 г. Diseases of the circulatory system (DCS) remain one of the leading causes of mortality in the population of the Russian Federation. Of particular interest is the assessment of changes in mortality from ischemic heart disease (IHD) and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) during the COVID-19 pandemic and in subsequent years, as well as the identification of territorial differences. The aim of the study is to assess the dynamics of mortality from DCS, IHD and AMI in the Russian Federation in 2017—2023, to identify the main changes in indicators after the COVID-19 pandemic period, and to characterise interregional differences across federal districts. Materials and methods. A retrospective analysis was conducted of official statistical data on the mortality of the population of the Russian Federation from BSC, IHD, and AMI for 2017—2021. The chain dynamics of the indicators and the dynamics relative to the baseline year 2017 were assessed, as well as changes during the pandemic period and the subsequent recovery, and the ranking position of the federal districts. The analysis revealed a pronounced U-shaped trend in mortality from cardiovascular diseases and ischemic heart disease, with an increase in rates in 2020—2021 followed by a subsequent decline. By 2023, mortality from cardiovascular diseases and ischemic heart disease had decreased (compared to 2017) by 5.27 % and 5.28 %, respectively. At the same time, mortality from acute myocardial infarction showed a different trend. In 2023, it exceeded the initial level by 3.52 %. A pronounced interregional heterogeneity in the indicators was identified. The lowest mortality rates were observed in the North Caucasus Federal District, while the highest were recorded in the Northwestern Federal District. In some federal districts, primarily in the Siberian and Far Eastern ones, unfavorable baseline dynamics persisted for certain indicators. In 2017—2023, the overall dynamics of mortality from CVD and coronary heart disease was characterized by a decrease towards the end of the period, after the pandemic upsurge. At the same time, the persistence of increased mortality from AMI relative to 2017 and pronounced territorial differences testified to the heterogeneity of the epidemiological situation and the need for further study of the factors determining mortality from acute coronary conditions. The interpretation of inter-regional differences required taking into account the age structure of the population and other demographic and socio-medical characteristics.

title: Trends in adolescent suicide attempts requiring pediatric intensive care across pre-COVID, COVID, and post-COVID periods
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic adversely affected adolescent mental health. This study compares pediatric intensive care unit admissions (PICU) due to adolescent suicide attempts across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-COVID periods. This retrospective study included adolescents aged 9–18 years admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit of Mersin City Training and Research Hospital for suicide attempts. Data were classified into pre-COVID (January 2019–March 2020), COVID (April 2020–March 2022), and post-COVID (April 2022–August 2024) periods. Variables included demographics, suicide method, psychiatric history, previous attempts, organ support, and outcomes. Of the 7,074 PICU admissions, 452 (6.4%) were for suicide attempts. Drug ingestion was predominant (95.8%). In the post-COVID period, the proportion of male cases, multiple-drug ingestions, and use of high-lethality methods increased, along with a greater need for intensive organ support. Mortality was observed only in the post-COVID period, with a rate of 1.8%. Logistic regression identified high-lethality methods, psychiatric follow-up, and previous attempts as predictors of severe outcomes in the post-COVID period. Adolescent suicide attempts requiring PICU admission became more severe after COVID-19. Early risk detection and targeted interventions are essential.

title: Lipid Nanoparticle-Formulated Synthetic Messenger RNA Induces Reversible Hematopoietic Bias via Type I Interferon Responses Under Upper-Bound Inflammatory Conditions in Preclinical Animal Models.
abstract: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) formulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) is increasingly used for vaccines and therapeutics, yet the consequences of high-dose systemic exposure for bone marrow hematopoiesis remain poorly defined. We previously reported that intramuscular mRNA/LNP administration transiently alters circulating reticulocytes and bone marrow erythroid cellularity in mice; here, we investigated the mechanistic basis and cross-species generalizability of this hematopoietic bias in murine and non-human primate models. Animals received intramuscular LNP-formulated mRNA encoding SARS-CoV-2 spike protein or firefly luciferase at deliberately supra-clinical, upper-bound doses, and type I interferon signaling was interrogated by interferon-α/β receptor blockade. Bone marrow was assessed by histopathology, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, and trajectory analysis. LNP-formulated mRNA induced reversible erythroid-lineage suppression with concomitant granulocytic expansion, irrespective of the encoded antigen. These effects were absent after naked mRNA and only modestly induced by LNP alone, indicating that formulation of synthetic mRNA within the LNP was required to elicit the full phenotype. Single-cell analysis showed biased hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell differentiation toward granulopoiesis with broad induction of interferon-stimulated genes, and the bias resolved within two weeks. Interferon-α/β receptor blockade mitigated both changes, demonstrating type I interferon dependence. High-dose LNP-formulated synthetic mRNA can therefore drive reversible, type I interferon-dependent hematopoietic lineage bias in preclinical animal models.

title: A bi-objective MILP model for pandemic vaccine allocation and distribution with behavioral adaptation
abstract: The purpose of this study is to develop a comprehensive optimization framework for pandemic vaccine allocation and distribution that minimizes both distribution costs and disease-induced mortality. The work addresses the need for timely, equitable, and logistically feasible vaccine delivery, particularly in settings with constrained resources and infrastructure. A bi-objective, multiproduct, multiperiod mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is formulated to integrate inter- and intra-provincial routing, cold chain requirements, vehicle availability and maintenance and vaccine spoilage. The model incorporates a piecewise linear vaccination rate that dynamically adjusts based on prior public acceptance trends. A context-informed, scenario-based application inspired by the COVID-19 vaccination campaign in Iran is presented to illustrate the model’s structure and policy-relevant insights, along with sensitivity analyses on vehicle capacity and disease spread rate. The model generates distribution and allocation plans that satisfy the modeled cold-chain and fleet constraints and illustrate the tradeoffs between distribution cost, mortality and equity under the assumed epidemiological and behavioral settings. Sensitivity analyses further examine how outcomes vary with transportation capacity and disease spread conditions. The framework can be adapted to different geographic and epidemiological contexts, guiding ministries of health and humanitarian logistics planners in designing responsive and equitable vaccination strategies. This study integrates detailed routing, cold chain compatibility, vehicle management and behavioral adaptation into a single optimization framework – features rarely combined in existing literature. It provides policymakers a decision-support modeling framework that has the potential to support pandemic preparedness and response under the modeled assumptions.

The model generates distribution and allocation plans that satisfy the modeled cold-chain and fleet constraints and illustrate the tradeoffs between distribution cost, mortality and equity under the assumed epidemiological and behavioral settings. Sensitivity analyses further examine how outcomes vary with transportation capacity and disease spread conditions. The framework can be adapted to different geographic and epidemiological contexts, guiding ministries of health and humanitarian logistics planners in designing responsive and equitable vaccination strategies. This study integrates detailed routing, cold chain compatibility, vehicle management and behavioral adaptation into a single optimization framework – features rarely combined in existing literature. It provides policymakers a decision-support modeling framework that has the potential to support pandemic preparedness and response under the modeled assumptions.

title: Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study
abstract: In China, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) persists as a prevalent infectious disease with high transmissibility. Nevertheless, the link between environmental determinants and HFMD incidence has not been fully elucidated. The study assessed associations between air pollution, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence in Shenzhen, China, while also evaluating shifts in these associations before and after the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and during the COVID-19 epidemic. Daily data on HFMD cases, air pollutants (such as PM 2.5 , PM 10 , SO 2 , NO 2 , CO, and O 3 ), and meteorological variables (including mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed) were collected for the period from 2013 to 2022. Associations were assessed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), accounting for immediate and delayed effects. Spearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO2 showing delayed effects. However, SO2 unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. NO2 exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O3 showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM 2.5 and PM 10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature exhibited a dual-peak risk pattern at extremely low and extremely high temperatures, with extreme heat producing sustained effects and extreme cold shorter-lived risk. HFMD risk increased under conditions of extremely high humidity. In general, the risk associated with atmospheric pressure rose as pressure levels increased, and asymmetric lagged effects were observed at both low- and high-concentration extremes. Extremely high wind speed causing short-term harm and extremely low wind speed leading to delayed cumulative risk. Meteorological factors exhibit more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors.

title: Associations Between Digital Attitudes, Digital Inequalities, and Health Care Use Among Recipients of a Community-Based Laptop Distribution Program: Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background Telehealth use expanded rapidly during the COVID-19 pandemic, yet persistent digital inequities continue to shape who benefits from virtual and preventive health services. Although community-based digital inclusion programs aim to reduce barriers to access, less is known about how device reliability, broadband conditions, and perceptions of online health information influence health care use after access is provided. Objective The objective of this study was to investigate associations between digital attitudes and access and health care use, including telehealth use and preventive health care visits, among participants in a community-based laptop distribution program. Methods This study analyzed cross-sectional survey data from 1019 participants in a community-based laptop distribution program. Refurbished laptops were distributed between October 2020 and July 2023, after which approximately 20,000 program recipients were invited by email to complete an online survey in English or Spanish. Ordered logistic regression models assessed predictors of telehealth use and preventive health care use. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, digital access conditions, and attitudes toward online health information. Results Among respondents, 26.95% (218/809) reported increased preventive health care visits since receiving a laptop, and 62% (502/810) reported using telehealth sometimes or often. Having a functioning program laptop was associated with higher odds of increased preventive health care use (odds ratio [OR] 2.13, 95% CI 1.07‐4.27; P=.03), whereas living with a partner was associated with lower odds (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.23‐0.99; P=.048). Participants with both fast internet and affordable broadband had greater odds of increased preventive health care use (OR 8.29, 95% CI 1.03‐66.50; P=.046). Participants who strongly agreed that online information helped them make better health decisions were more likely to report increased preventive health care use (OR 15.03, 95% CI 4.53‐49.82; P<.001). More frequent telehealth use was associated with reporting that online health information often improved health (OR 17.77, 95% CI 6.78‐46.56; P<.001) and with speaking a language other than English as a primary language (OR 5.95, 95% CI 1.73‐20.41; P=.005). Respondents reporting decreased physician visits had lower odds of telehealth use (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.10‐0.46; P<.001). Race, ethnicity, gender, race-by-gender, and ethnicity-by-gender interaction terms were not substantial in adjusted models. Conclusions Digital inclusion efforts may support engagement with preventive and virtual health services, but access alone appears insufficient. Device functionality, broadband quality and affordability, and perceptions of the value of online health information were important predictors of health care use. Digital inclusion initiatives should address both technological infrastructure and digital health engagement to promote equitable access to care.

title: Outcomes and diagnostic yield of paediatric gastrointestinal endoscopy: implications for patient selection, benchmarking and quality standards
abstract: To report updated diagnostic yield in children undergoing first diagnostic gastrointestinal endoscopy, compared with previous periods reflecting earlier routine practice and during COVID-19 pandemic-related service restrictions. Secondary aims were to study clinical and laboratory predictive factors for abnormal paediatric endoscopy and to consider their implications for patient selection, benchmarking and quality standards. Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of all first-diagnostic endoscopies performed in a tertiary paediatric gastroenterology service across three 6-month cohorts: Period 1—historic routine practice; Period 2—during COVID-19 pandemic and Period 3—contemporary routine practice. Assessment of endoscopic findings and preceding clinical and laboratory factors for sensitivity, specificity, negative and positive predictive value. Diagnostic yield defined as the % of patients with histological abnormality confirmed in our weekly histology multidisciplinary team meeting. Macroscopic and histological findings on endoscopy and presenting clinical and laboratory measures. During Period 2, yield reached 89% for oesophagogastroduodenoscopy (OGD) and ileocolonoscopy. In Period 3, there were 194 procedures in 137 children. Period 3 histological abnormality rates were significantly higher than Period 1: 66.4% versus 36% overall; 61.3% versus 28% for OGD; 54.9% versus 16% for OGD alone (in patients with normal anti-transglutaminase IgA antibody); 75% versus 47% for OGD and ileocolonoscopy. Period 3 unexpectedly demonstrated a significant increase in diagnoses of histological gastritis. Refined patient selection can reduce the proportion of normal procedures, with no observed evidence of harm. These data can contribute towards benchmarking and development of quality standards for paediatric diagnostic endoscopy services.

title: The Primary Health Care System and Local-Level Scenarios of Multimorbidity: The Cases of Osorno and Castro in the Los Lagos Region
abstract: La COVID-19, primera pandemia del siglo XXI, se originó en 2019 en Wuhan, China, y tuvo un profundo impacto sanitario, social y económico a nivel global. Aunque la OMS declaró el fin de la emergencia en mayo de 2023, sus secuelas persisten, afectando tanto a sobrevivientes directos como a personas con patologías crónicas no transmisibles. En Chile, la multimorbilidad representa un desafío creciente para el sistema sanitario, frente al cual el Ministerio de Salud implementó la Estrategia de Cuidado Integral Centrado en las Personas (ECICEP). Este estudio mixto, retrospectivo y correlacional se desarrollará en Osorno y Castro, integrando análisis espacial mediante técnicas de clustering para identificar patrones y apoyar la toma de decisiones en salud pública. La muestra incluye datos clínicos de usuarios ECICEP, información censal y entrevistas a profesionales y usuarios, además de la aplicación del MBI-HSS al personal sanitario, con el objetivo de comprender el impacto de la pandemia en la atención de la multimorbilidad. Demostrar los impactos generados por la pandemia por la COVID-19 en la condición de multimorbilidad de los usuarios y de las usuarias pertenecientes al programa ECICEP en las comunas de Osorno y Castro, desde que se inició de la estrategia. Estudio de tipo mixto se relaciona con los objetivos planteados, ello permitió trabajar con datos clínicos, profesionales de la salud y personas inscritas en el programa ECICEP (por medio de grupos focales) tanto de la comuna de Osorno como Castro. Los datos clínicos anonimizados de 7 CESFAM donde 6 fueron de la ciudad de Osorno y uno de Castro. 31.189 pacientes presentaron concurrencia por morbilidad durante el periodo de pandemia. El CESFAM de Lopetegui presentó un 21,3% (n=6.630) y Ovejería con un 8,2% (n=2.546), el CESFAM de Castro con 4.520 pacientes. El grupo etario de adultos entre 27 y 59 años con un 52,4%, seguidos por los grupos etarios de 60 y más años con el 29% (vejez) y de un 12,9% de los jóvenes. El género femenino con atenciones entre los 58,5% hasta 72,2%, sin embargo, en los grupos de vejez y adolescencia, si bien el género femenino se presentó un mayor porcentaje 58,8% y 56,5% el género masculino presento un mayor porcentaje con respecto a los otros grupos etarios. Los grupos etarios que aumentaron la categoría de riesgo fueron del grupo los adultos y de vejez con un 48% y 36,7% respectivamente. Sin embargo, se determinó que en la categoría vejez aumento el porcentaje en el cambio de riesgo de G3G2 73,2% y 62,2% de G3G1 con respecto a las otras categorías. La categoría adulta, se destacó dentro de los grupos que mantuvieron el nivel de riesgo y disminuyeron el nivel del riesgo. En cuanto al número de enfermedades diagnosticadas de en los pacientes, el 52,7% presentaban dos enfermedades, el 15,6% con tres enfermedades. Hay 72 personas que presentaron 12 y más patologías. El género femenino como masculino presentaron la misma tendencia a disminuir los pacientes a medica que aumentaban el número de enfermedades. Se presentaron 3 pacientes con 16 patologías, 2 del género femenino y 1 masculino. Los grupos etarios de adultez y vejez presentaron un mayor número de patologías. El género femenino fue el que solicito un mayor número de prestaciones médicas. Los grupos de adultos y en etapa de vejez, generaron 81,4% de las atenciones en los CESFAM de estudio. El género femenino presentó un mayor riesgo con respecto al masculino, así como los grupos etarios de adultos y de vejez. Los pacientes presentaron entre una a 16 enfermedades, donde el 52,7% presentaron entre una a dos enfermedades. En ambos géneros disminuyo el número de pacientes en relación con el número de patologías diagnosticadas. Los principales factores de riesgo de presentar enfermedades mentales fueron los pacientes del género femenino, encontrarse en la edad joven- adultos y recibir atención en el CESFAM de Castro.

title: National trends in infection-related mortality among US cancer decedents in the immunotherapy era (1999-2023).
abstract: While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have reshaped cancer care, population-level patterns of infection-related involvement at death among cancer decedents remain incompletely characterized. We analyzed >25 million US cancer deaths recorded in Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER; 1999-2023), excluding deaths with COVID-19 as the underlying cause. Infection-related involvement was defined using infection-related multiple-cause-of-death codes among decedents with cancer as the underlying cause. To approximate treatment context at the population level, malignancies were grouped by tumor-site-based likelihood of ICI exposure (a proxy rather than observed receipt), and temporal changes were evaluated using Joinpoint regression and interrupted time-series (ITS) models anchored to 2015, corresponding to the period of broad clinical adoption of ICIs. The proportion of cancer-underlying-cause deaths with infection-related multiple causes increased from 7.98% in 2009-2013 to 8.65% in 2017-2019 (+0.67 percentage points) in the prespecified period comparison. Joinpoint analysis identified a 2015 inflection, shifting from a pre-2015 decline to a sustained post-2015 increase (APC, +1.42% through 2023). Post-2015, cancers in the high-ICI-likelihood group (including melanoma, kidney, lung, and stomach cancers) showed a larger relative increase in infection-related multiple causes than low-ICI-likelihood cancers (+16.2% vs +6.7%), and ITS models supported a steeper post-2015 slope after accounting for the pandemic period. These findings indicate that infection-related conditions listed on death certificates among US cancer decedents have increased since 2015, with larger rises observed in tumor sites more likely to be treated with ICIs. Further work using patient-level treatment data is needed to determine whether these temporal patterns reflect immunotherapy exposure, shifts in case mix, or changes in certification and coding practices.

title: Step-by-step program: mentalization-based intervention for autistic children and their families
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) presents challenges for public health systems due to its heterogeneity and complexity. The Step-by-Step Program was developed as an innovative, community-based mentalization-based intervention for autistic children aged 5–7 and their families. This study aims to evaluate the feasibility of implementing this program within existing systems of care and to examine its preliminary effects. An open trial was conducted with 16 autistic children and their families who participated in the Step-by-Step Program, a two-year intervention integrating weekly group therapy for children with alternating multi-family and parent sessions. Outcome measures included standardized assessments of child emotional and behavioral functioning, autism symptom profiles and parental satisfaction. Data were collected at baseline, midpoint, endpoint and one-year follow-up. Findings indicated high feasibility, treatment adherence and strong family satisfaction ratings. Children demonstrated significant improvements in social communication, symbolic play, flexibility and emotional/behavioral regulation. These gains were not only maintained but further consolidated at the one-year follow-up. Families also reported reduced stress and increased capacity for understanding and supporting their child’s development. This pilot study supports the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of the Step-by-Step program; however, several limitations should be considered. The open, uncontrolled design precludes causal attribution of observed changes to the intervention rather than to time or nonspecific therapeutic effects. This limitation will be addressed in future randomized controlled trials, for which the present findings provide essential pilot data. Additionally, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the final three months of treatment were delivered via telehealth, although outcome assessment and treatment procedures were maintained. Finally, parental perceptions of children’s mentalizing abilities were not assessed. Future studies should include measures of parental reflective functioning, a key treatment target of mentalization-based therapy for children. This is a pilot study that describes the development and implementation of the mentalization-based treatment for autistic children in the context of the community mental health case system in Catalonia, Spain. The Step-by-Step Program appears to be a promising, feasible and effective early intervention model for autistic children and their families. Its integration into community mental health services suggests potential for sustainable, family-centered approaches that enhance social development and well-being. The authors believe that the innovative aspects of this study include the adaptation of mentalization-based therapy for autism, long-term treatment and implementation in the local Catalone system of care.
