Children demonstrated significant improvements in social communication, symbolic play, flexibility and emotional/behavioral regulation. These gains were not only maintained but further consolidated at the one-year follow-up. Families also reported reduced stress and increased capacity for understanding and supporting their child’s development. This pilot study supports the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of the Step-by-Step program; however, several limitations should be considered. The open, uncontrolled design precludes causal attribution of observed changes to the intervention rather than to time or nonspecific therapeutic effects. This limitation will be addressed in future randomized controlled trials, for which the present findings provide essential pilot data. Additionally, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the final three months of treatment were delivered via telehealth, although outcome assessment and treatment procedures were maintained. Finally, parental perceptions of children’s mentalizing abilities were not assessed. Future studies should include measures of parental reflective functioning, a key treatment target of mentalization-based therapy for children. This is a pilot study that describes the development and implementation of the mentalization-based treatment for autistic children in the context of the community mental health case system in Catalonia, Spain. The Step-by-Step Program appears to be a promising, feasible and effective early intervention model for autistic children and their families. Its integration into community mental health services suggests potential for sustainable, family-centered approaches that enhance social development and well-being. The authors believe that the innovative aspects of this study include the adaptation of mentalization-based therapy for autism, long-term treatment and implementation in the local Catalone system of care.

title: ADULT STILL'S DISEASE AS A POST-COVID COMPLICATION: CLINICAL OBSERVATION
abstract: The article describes a clinical case of adult Still's disease that developed in a young woman 10 months after she had been infected with coronavirus disease (COVID-19). It is believed that infection caused by SARS-CoV-2 can induce an exacerbation of an existing immune-inflammatory process or cause the development of a new autoimmune pathology in a patient. Adult Still's disease is a rare disease, the main symptoms of which include fever accompanied by serositis, sore throat, myalgia, arthralgia, and a transient skin rash localized mainly in the proximal parts of the limbs and trunk. The rash may be accompanied by itching and disappear between episodes of fever. Along with the typical manifestations, there are many nonspecific symptoms of the disease that do not allow for its timely detection. As a rule, adult Still's disease is considered an exclusion diagnosis. Infectious, malignant, and autoimmune inflammatory diseases of the connective tissue are primarily excluded. The clinical case described in the article corresponds to the definition and characteristics of adult Still's disease, with a predominance of a prolonged period of low-grade fever and chills, debilitating myalgias, and a cyclical skin rash. One of the features of the presented case is the late onset of joint manifestations. The high level of ferritin with neutrophilic leukocytosis and the absence of antibodies characteristic of other systemic autoimmune and infectious diseases were the main milestones in making the final diagnosis.
journal: Russian Journal of Skin and Venereal Diseases

title: The Unequal Pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately harmed members of already disadvantaged and vulnerable communities. Focusing on five communities in the US with comparative data from other countries – children, older adults, women, people of color, and those who are incarcerated – The Unequal Pandemic explains why. The book points to the inadequacies of the public policies adopted to respond to the pandemic, evaluating their effectiveness and compliance with ethical norms and human rights obligations. By assessing the failures of the responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, the book outlines needed policy changes to rectify current disparities and respond more effectively in future health emergencies.

title: Lyotropic chromonic liquid crystals as hydrophilic signal-transducing media for real-time monitoring and high-sensitivity detection of disease biomarkers
abstract: This study investigates advanced label-free biosensing using the nematic phase of the lyotropic chromonic liquid crystal (LCLC) sunset yellow (SSY) to detect the cancer biomarker CA125 and SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein. Unlike hydrophobic thermotropic LCs, SSY provides a hydrophilic medium that interacts more directly with biomolecules. Formation of antigen–antibody immunocomplexes at the LC–glass interface disrupted SSY orientation and produced measurable optical and dielectric changes. Quantification is achieved through three strategies, including polarizing optical microscopy image analysis, dielectric spectroscopy, and haze measurement. Optical analysis leveraged SSY absorption near 482 nm, while dielectric and haze measurements offered a simpler, more precise alternative to conventional image-based analysis. In addition, SSY enabled real-time monitoring and binding-kinetics analysis of antigen–antibody reactions. Kinetic fitting suggests distinct binding behaviors for CA125 versus SARS-CoV-2 N-protein immunocomplex formation. Together, these results position nematic SSY as a versatile signal-transducing medium for point-of-care screening of cancer and infectious diseases.

title: Association between attachment style and suicide risk in patients receiving online psychotherapy: a cross-sectional study of five psychotherapy services
abstract: Restrictions imposed during the COVID-19 pandemic have raised concern among suicidology and mental health researchers regarding a possible increase in suicide risk, particularly among people already in psychological distress. Attachment style is one relational characteristic that may act as either a vulnerability or a protective factor. To analyze the association between attachment style and suicide risk among patients undergoing online psychotherapy. Additionally, it sought to explore the influence of depression on this relationship and to estimate the prevalence of suicide risk. Cross-sectional analysis of a multi-center sample of patients in online psychotherapy during the COVID-19 pandemic ( n = 94) with complete data on all instruments analyzed. Measures included sociodemographic data, attachment style (Adult Attachment Scale-R, AAS-R), depression (PHQ-9), and suicide risk (PHQ-9-item9). Group comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U test; associations used the chi-square test, and relationships between scores used Spearman correlations. The prevalence of higher suicide risk was 43.6% ( n = 41; 95% CI 34.0–53.7). Patients at higher suicide risk scored higher on anxiety/fear of abandonment (3.53 ± 0.99 vs. 3.03 ± 1.04; p = .018; r = .28) and lower on comfort with intimacy (2.88 ± 0.82 vs. 3.44 ± 0.73; p = .003; r = − .36) and trust in others (2.54 ± 0.76 vs. 2.87 ± 0.68; p = .044; r = − .24). Depression severity fully mediated the effects of comfort with intimacy and trust in others on suicide risk, but not that of anxiety/fear of abandonment. Attachment style was associated with suicide risk in patients receiving online psychotherapy. Much, though not all, of this association operated through depression severity. The findings support the early identification of insecure attachment as a clinically useful component of suicide risk assessment and underline that suicidal ideation is not confined to patients who screen positive for depression.

title: The human gut microbiome primes fever after vaccination
abstract: Fever is a common adverse reaction to vaccination, contributing to vaccine hesitancy and reduced uptake. To understand variation in fever risk, we longitudinally profiled fecal microbiota, oral temperature, and serological markers in 171 healthy adults receiving Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 mRNA vaccines. Fever risk correlated with low-grade intestinal inflammation, increased abundance of flagellated Lachnospiraceae bacteria, and increased flagellin expression prevaccine. Microbiomes from fever-high donors triggered stronger inflammation in human intestinal organoids and drove flagellin-dependent vaccine reactions in gnotobiotic mice. Moreover, microbiome flagellin phenotypes and murine vaccine reactions were modifiable by diet. Consistent with this, human fever risk was associated with self-reported diet and metabolic markers. These findings identify the gut microbiome as a driver of vaccine-induced fever, suggesting that microbiome-targeting strategies could modulate immune tone and improve vaccine side effects.

title: Multiclass Chest X-Ray Classification Using Transfer Learning with Resnet50: Performance Evaluation Across Varying Train-Test Configurations
abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) imaging remains the most widely used diagnostic modality for chest X-ray abnormalities globally, yet its interpretation is heavily dependent on radiologist availability and is prone to inter-observer variability, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where specialist shortages delay diagnosis. While deep learning models have achieved radiologist-level accuracy in classifying chest X-ray abnormalities, many studies report performance on a single, fixed train-test split, leaving open the question of how the proportion of data allocated to training versus testing affects performance under severe class imbalance. This study developed and evaluated a multiclass chest X-ray classification model using transfer learning with ResNet50, and systematically compared its performance across four train-test split configurations. A master dataset of 93,853 chest X-ray images was assembled from four public sources (Chest X-ray Dataset for Tuberculosis Segmentation, Chest X-Ray Images (Pneumonia), NIH Chest X-rays, COVID-19 Radiography Database) and harmonised into eight diagnostic classes: COVID-19, Pneumonia, Tuberculosis, Pleural Effusion, Cardiomegaly, Atelectasis, Pneumothorax, and Normal. Following image preprocessing and class-weighted loss adjustment for dataset imbalance, a ResNet50-based convolutional neural network was trained using transfer learning. Four train-test split configurations (20/80, 40/60, 50/50, and 70/30) were compared, and the 20/80 split yielded the best overall performance, with 71.37% accuracy, 83.59% weighted precision, 71.37% weighted recall, and 75.72% weighted F1-score, alongside a macro-average ROC-AUC of 0.9020. The model performed strongly on Pneumonia and COVID-19 (F1-scores of 93% and 89%, respectively) but showed reduced precision for minority classes such as Atelectasis, Cardiomegaly, and Pneumothorax, largely attributable to systematic misclassification of Normal images rather than confusion among disease classes. These findings show that increasing the proportion of training data does not automatically improve generalisation under severe class imbalance, and highlight class imbalance as a key target for future model refinement.

title: Mapping the genetic landscape of the age at onset and severity of eating disorder symptoms.
abstract: BACKGROUND Eating disorder treatment is most successful when delivered at first onset, underscoring the importance of early intervention. Genetic factors may contribute to earlier onset, but molecular genetic research into symptom onset and severity remains limited. AIMS We investigated: (a) age at onset of behavioural symptoms and low weight, including sex and gender differences; and (b) the single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based heritability and cross-trait polygenic associations of symptoms, onset, and severity. METHOD Participants (n = 24 973) of genetically derived European ancestry were from the National Institute for Health and Care Research BioResource, including the Genetic Links to Anxiety and Depression Study, the Eating Disorders Genetics Initiative UK and the COVID-19 Psychiatry and Neurological Genetics study. Symptoms were assessed with the ED100K questionnaire. We described sex-stratified onset of binge eating, low weight, self-induced vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, excessive exercise, and fasting. SNP-based heritability was estimated with genome-wide complex trait analysis using genomic-relatedness-based restricted maximum-likelihood. We tested associations with 26 polygenic scores (PGS), which were calculated using SBayesRC. RESULTS Symptom median onset ranged from 16 to 20 years: vomiting (16 years), fasting and excessive exercise (17 years), binge eating (18 years), laxatives (19 years), diuretics (20 years) and low weight (20 years). Males were disproportionately likely to report adult onset. In females, behavioural symptoms and low weight showed substantial heritability (SNP-based h2 = 0.31-0.78), but age at onset and cognitive symptoms were less heritable. PGS analyses identified distinct pathways: in females, higher childhood obesity PGS was linked to earlier binge eating onset (approximately 7 months), and higher educational attainment PGS to earlier low weight onset (approximately 6 months). CONCLUSIONS Eating disorder symptoms begin in adulthood as frequently as adolescence, challenging stereotypes and underscoring investment needed in adult services, particularly for males. Although behavioural symptoms and low weight were strongly heritable, age at onset and cognitive symptoms showed limited genetic contribution. Symptom-level PGS analyses highlight distinct biological and developmental pathways. Larger sample sizes and more accurate phenotyping are needed.

title: Механизмы формирования когнитивных нарушений у детей, перенесших коронавирусную инфекцию
abstract: Введение.Выявление причин формирования когнитивных нарушений, их ранняя диагностика, прогнозирование и реабилитация пациентов остаются актуальными задачами педиатрической практики.Цель исследования— изучить механизмы формирования и определить факторы риска развития когнитивных нарушений у детей, перенесших легкую и среднетяжелую формы COVID-19.Материалы и методы.Под наблюдением находились 147 детей в возрасте от 7 до 18 лет, перенесших инфекцию SARS-Co V-2. В 1-ю группу вошли 22 ребенка с когнитивными нарушениями, во 2-ю — 125 детей без нарушений. Группы были сопоставимы по полу и возрасту. Когнитивные нарушения оценивали с помощью синдромного факторного анализа нарушений высших корковых функций человека, предложенного А.Р. Частоту и тяжесть астенического синдрома определяли по шкале Л.Д. Статистическая обработка осуществлялась с использованием IBM SPSS Statistics 23. Значимость принимали при p <0,05.Результаты.Когнитивные нарушения выявлены у 13,6% детей с первых дней заболевания SARS-Co V-2 и сохранялись до трех лет. Introduction.Identification of the causes of cognitive impairment, early diagnosis, prediction, and rehabilitation remain important tasks in pediatric practice.The aim— to investigate the mechanisms underlying the development of cognitive impairment and to identify risk factors in children who have had mild to moderate COVID-19.Materials and methods.The study included 147 children aged 7–18 years who had SARS-Co V-2 infection. Group 1 comprised 22 children with cognitive impairment, while Group 2 included 125 children without impairment. The groups were comparable in terms of age and sex. Cognitive impairment was assessed using the syndrome-based factor analysis of higher cortical functions proposed by A.R. The frequency and severity of asthenic syndrome were evaluated using the Malkova–Chertova scale (modified for adolescents). Transcranial duplex ultrasound of cerebral vessels was performed. Statistical analysis was conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics 23. Differences were considered statistically significant at p <0.05.Results.Cognitive impairment was detected in 13.6% of children from the early stages of SARS-Co V-2 infection and persisted for up to three years. Moderate and severe asthenia were associated with an increased risk of cognitive deficit. The likelihood of cognitive impairment was also influenced by the severity of infection symptoms, the presence of neurological manifestations, as well as the child’s sex and age.

The frequency and severity of asthenic syndrome were evaluated using the Malkova–Chertova scale (modified for adolescents). Transcranial duplex ultrasound of cerebral vessels was performed. Statistical analysis was conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics 23. Differences were considered statistically significant at p <0.05.Results.Cognitive impairment was detected in 13.6% of children from the early stages of SARS-Co V-2 infection and persisted for up to three years. Moderate and severe asthenia were associated with an increased risk of cognitive deficit. The likelihood of cognitive impairment was also influenced by the severity of infection symptoms, the presence of neurological manifestations, as well as the child’s sex and age.

title: Optimizing Place-Level Closure Decisions for Strict Epidemic Control: An Agent-Based Simulation and Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the challenge of designing intervention policies that suppress transmission while limiting economic disruption. Although lockdowns effectively reduce infections, prolonged restrictions impose substantial social and economic costs. Balancing these competing objectives is therefore a central problem in epidemic policy design. This study proposes a reinforcement learning framework for the selective closure of community places, treating each place as an individual decision unit. We develop a spatial agent-based simulation model in which infection spreads through place-based contacts and individual mobility follows a gravity-based formulation that captures place attractiveness and locality. The epidemic state is represented as spatial maps and processed by a deep neural network to learn closure policies that minimize the combined health and economic costs of epidemic control. We evaluate the learned policies under a cost formulation that explicitly balances infection burden against economic losses caused by place closures, weighted by the health and economic cost coefficients ch and ce, respectively. Simulation experiments were conducted in a small-scale virtual city under a strict epidemic-control scenario. The learned policy reduces total cost relative to threshold-based lockdown policies. The reduction is statistically significant when economic losses receive moderate or greater weight in the objective (ce = 0.04 and 0.06), whereas the difference is not statistically significant at ce = 0.02 (p = 0.12). Beyond the conventional emphasis on high-risk places, the results identify locality as an important determinant of efficient closure decisions. These findings suggest that spatially informed, place-level interventions can improve the efficiency of epidemic control while mitigating economic losses.

title: Case Report: Sustained pubertal suppression for 68 months with a single histrelin acetate implant in central precocious puberty
abstract: The subcutaneous histrelin acetate implant is FDA-approved for 12 months of continuous gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonist therapy in central precocious puberty (CPP). Published data demonstrated sustained suppression with a single implant for up to approximately 24 months; however, efficacy beyond this duration has not been reported. A 7 years 5 month old female patient presented with bilateral Tanner 2 breast development, a bone age of 10 years, and laboratory findings consistent with early central activation. Treatment was delayed 11 months due to disruptions in care during the COVID-19 pandemic, and a histrelin implant was placed at age 8 years 5 months. The patient was lost to follow-up and returned at nearly 14 years of age, approximately 68 months after the implant placement, with primary amenorrhea and pubertal arrest. Laboratory evaluation before implant removal showed suppressed but detectable gonadotropins with a prepubertal estradiol, consistent with sustained partial suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis sufficient to arrest pubertal progression. Her predicted adult height (PAH) of 167.6 cm (66 inches) approximated her mid-parental height (MPH) of 166.4 cm (65.5 inches). This case demonstrates that a single histrelin acetate implant may maintain clinically meaningful pubertal suppression for at least 68 months. These findings support broader investigations into the pharmacokinetics of extended implant use, given implications for reducing surgical burden and healthcare costs in CPP management.

title: How do middle-income states select vaccine partners? Projected capacity across sectors in Argentina
abstract: How do governments select vaccine-production partners when sector-specific capacity is incomplete? The COVID-19 pandemic made this question especially pressing, as vaccine nationalism constrained external supply and pushed middle-income states to expand domestic production despite unproven capacities. Tracing Argentina’s vaccine strategy from 2020 to 2022, this article develops the concept of projected capacity: a mechanism through which states infer potential capacity in one sector from firms’ resources, credibility, and structural position in another. Policymakers rely on proxies for vaccine-production capacity, including industrial legacies, firm–state familiarity, and alignment with health-sovereignty goals. State selection then provides firms with resources, alliances, and legitimacy, transforming projected capacity into sector-specific structural power. The article contributes to debates in political economy and public policy by showing that structural power is not only a pre-existing source of influence over the state; it can also be created through state decisions that select and support firms.

title: A Human-Centered Web Technology for Reproducible Statistical and Machine-Learning Analysis of Heterogeneous Data
abstract: The analysis of heterogeneous tabular datasets remains challenging for non-specialist users because data preparation, statistical diagnostics, algorithm selection, model evaluation, and result interpretation are frequently distributed across separate software environments. This manuscript presents a reproducible web-based technology that integrates data ingestion, automated data-quality assessment, statistical validation, transparent rule-based analytical guidance, supervised and unsupervised machine learning, and interactive visual analytics within a unified workflow. The platform supports commonly used tabular formats and employs a modular, containerized architecture to support portability and reproducible analytical execution. Rather than autonomously selecting a supposedly optimal model, the recommendation mechanism identifies the analytical task, screens incompatible methods, detects semantic ambiguity, generates methodological warnings, and prioritizes compatible candidate models using explicit and inspectable rules. Final supervised-model selection is based on empirical cross-validation within the training data. The technology is evaluated through functional tests on heterogeneous health and financial datasets, predictive and clustering experiments, controlled recommendation-engine and schema-robustness experiments, computational benchmarks, and a usability study involving users with limited programming experience. In a COVID-19 dataset containing 95,839 records, the platform supported two-code and three-code patient-classification experiments, descriptive clustering, and data-quality analysis while transparently identifying class imbalance, predictor missingness, repeated predictor profiles, and performance limitations. A grouped-profile sensitivity analysis further showed that the principal classification results did not deteriorate when identical selected predictor configurations were prevented from occurring in both the training and held-out partitions. Controlled schema-robustness experiments correctly identified all prespecified unambiguous analytical tasks, detected all prespecified semantic ambiguities, rejected incompatible supervised configurations, and produced no silent acceptance of ambiguous or invalid cases. The recommender-specific evaluation also showed that the highest-ranked rule-based candidate does not necessarily coincide with the cross-validation-best model, reinforcing its role as a decision-support mechanism rather than an autonomous model-selection procedure. An exploratory laboratory usability evaluation with twelve non-specialist participants produced an average task-success rate of 95.3% and a mean System Usability Scale score of 86.7±5.2. These values correspond to aggregate results recorded during the original laboratory experiment. Because the participant-level observer logs and individual SUS responses were not retained in the available study materials, the usability results are interpreted descriptively and are not presented as population-level estimates. The results indicate that the proposed architecture can reduce technical barriers while preserving analytical traceability, methodological transparency, and user control. The platform therefore provides an extensible foundation for human-supervised, reproducible analysis of heterogeneous tabular data rather than an autonomous statistical or machine-learning decision-making system.

title: Calendar month seasonality of HbA1c and its phase relationship with climatological temperature in 633,838 clinical measurements
abstract: HbA1c reflects glucose exposure over the preceding 8–12 weeks. We characterised the lagged seasonal association between monthly climatological temperature normals and HbA1c in a 12-year hospital cohort and examined whether a similar pattern was present in patient-level records. We analysed 633,838 HbA1c measurements (387,678 patients; 633,737 with complete covariates) from a Chinese tertiary hospital (2014–2025). Cross-correlation was assessed for lags of 0–6 months using monthly HbA1c means and fixed monthly climatological temperature normals. Patient-level distributed-lag regression with cluster-robust standard errors and generalised estimating equations was used as a complementary analysis. HbA1c was inversely correlated with the climatological temperature series most strongly at a 2-month lag (r = −0.297, P < 0.001) rather than concurrently (r = −0.127, P = 0.14). Pooled by calendar month, the lag-2 seasonal association was strong (r = −0.977, R2 = 0.955), with a seasonal HbA1c amplitude of 0.235% (2.6 mmol/mol; peak March, trough September), strongest under age 60 and attenuated during COVID-19. Patient-level regression showed a similar lag pattern, with the largest coefficient at lag 2 (β = −0.0088% per °C; 95% CI −0.0093 to −0.0082; P < 0.001), and the individual-level partial R2 was 0.15%. The study identified a reproducible seasonal HbA1c pattern that aligned most strongly with the 2-month-shifted climatological temperature series, with significant correspondence also at 1 and 3 months. Because the exposure was a fixed calendar-month normal, the findings should be interpreted as a lagged seasonal association rather than evidence of a causal temperature effect or a specific 2-month biological delay. The small individual-level partial R2 (0.15%) also argues against applying the population amplitude directly to individual treatment decisions. Future research should evaluate whether seasonal contextualisation can optimise laboratory monitoring and re-testing strategies near diagnostic thresholds.

title: Cryo-EM Analysis of Adenovirus Vector Reveals Purification Conditions Leading to Loss of Viral Fiber Proteins and Reduced Infectivity.
abstract: Vaccines and gene therapies require efficient delivery of genetic material to host cells. Viral vectors leverage viruses' ability to enter host cells to achieve this. Following the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine and novel gene therapies that utilize adenovirus vectors, there has been an increase in the demand for large-scale production of vectors. A benefit of adenovirus vectors is that they can act as a "plug and play" tool for any future emerging diseases for the development of vaccines. A key obstacle was the heterogeneity that is found in the final product. This can reduce the functionality of the vector and affect immune responses. A possible origin of heterogeneity is the downstream processing, specifically the bind and elute steps of anion exchange chromatography (AEX), which is widely used at scale. To better understand the heterogeneity that AEX could elicit on the adenovirus capsid, cryogenic-electron tomography was used to assess the capsid integrity after a variety of chromatography conditions in comparison to a cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation purified control. To investigate the effect of absorption time during chromatography, AEX conditions with a 5, 10, and 20 min on-resin absorption periods were evaluated. Following AEX binding at pH 6.5, samples showed a reduction from 17% in the CsCl purified control to 10% infectious particles. When examined using electron microscopy, the virions exhibited aggregation and a decrease from 70% to 54% in fiber occupancy. After a 20 min AEX hold at pH 6.5 there was almost complete loss of infectivity and fiber occupancy decreased from ~70% to below 30%. Samples run at pH 8 did not show the same loss in infectivity when held bound for 20 min. This suggests that purification conditions can cause removal of the fiber protein, which was likely causing the decrease in infectivity, due to the fiber's role in cell entry. We hypothesize that fiber removal was caused by a combination of hold time and weakened binding between the fiber and penton base due to the low pH conditions that are often used during AEX. This work demonstrates a link between fiber loss and reduced adenovirus vector functionality and how purification conditions can impact vector functionality. Through studying the relationship between structure and function, we can hopefully minimize loss of infectivity during purification by optimizing processing conditions, reduce manufacturing cost and improve the quality of adenovirus vaccines and gene therapies.

title: Comparing language models and machine learning classifiers for detecting humorous vaccine misinformation on social media
abstract: Misinformation embedded in humor on social media can be difficult to detect and mitigate. This study investigates the effectiveness of traditional machine learning (ML) models, pre-trained neural language models, and large language models (LLMs) in identifying humor-laden misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines on Twitter. A dataset of 1,500 tweets was randomly sampled from a corpus of 17,945 humorous vaccination disclosures, with human coders annotating the presence of misinformation. We compared logistic regression, a linear support vector classifier (SVC), RoBERTa, and OpenAI’s GPT-4o with a zero-shot and a few-shot prompt, together with a keyword baseline. The few-shot GPT-4o prompt had the highest mean recall and F1 score for the types of misinformation indicated in the prompt and had higher recall and F1 than a keyword baseline built from those same terms. RoBERTa’s accuracy, precision, and F1 score did not differ significantly from GPT-4o’s, and its performance changed little with smaller training sets. Logistic regression and SVC showed lower accuracy, recall, and F1 scores than RoBERTa and the few-shot GPT-4o prompt. This study underscores the potential of LLMs to augment human efforts in detecting complex forms of misinformation on social media and highlights the importance of model selection based on task requirements.

title: Mapeamento da produção e colaboração acadêmica entre especialistas brasileiros em inteligência artificial e machine learning aplicados à saúde: uma análise bibliométrica
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence in healthcare has shown great potential over recent decades. In Brazil,this approach follows the expansion of research and academic collaboration in that field. In this regard, thisstudy conducts an exploratory analysis of the scientific production and the collaboration among Brazilianresearchers working on artificial intelligence and machine learning applied to healthcare. A quantitativeapproach was employed, using scriptLattes software to map data from the Lattes platform from 2008 to2024. The analyses covered temporal evolution, geographical distribution, the most recurrent institutions and fields of concentration, keywords, and collaboration networks, assessing trends and gaps in the field. The results demonstrate significant growth in scientific production, concentrated in the Southeast region, and predominance of terms associated with the technologies employed and diagnostic applications, withemphasis on covid-19. Furthermore, the need for greater interdisciplinary and interinstitutional collaboration as well as greater attention to ethics, governance, and regulation is evident.

title: Successful treatment of metformin-associated lactic acidosis without hemodialysis
abstract: Abstract Objectives Metformin-associated lactic acidosis (MALA) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition. Hemodialysis is often recommended, but evidence of successful nondialytic management in children is limited. We report a girl with MALA successfully treated with supportive medical management without dialysis. Case presentation We report a girl with nondialyzed chronic kidney disease (CKD) and non–insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (NIDDM), and dyslipidemia who developed MALA after 18 months of metformin, insulin, and sodium bicarbonate therapy. She presented with dyspnea, palpitations, and vomiting. She was lethargic, afebrile, tachypneic, tachycardic, hypertensive, and had Kussmaul breathing. Laboratory results showed blood glucose 55 mg/dL, potassium 6.7 mEq/L, arterial pH 7.038, pCO2 <5 mmHg, and lactate 19.55 (0.56–1.39) mmol/L. She was diagnosed with CKD and NIDDM complicated by acute kidney injury and MALA. She was treated with intravenous glucose, sodium bicarbonate, respiratory support, and rectal calcium polystyrene sulfonate and then referred to our hospital, arriving 9 h after the initial presentation. For MALA, hemodialysis (HD) or continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) was considered, but predialysis COVID-19 testing requirements delayed immediate initiation. Intravenous fluids were maintained at 100–150 cc/h with urine output of 200–220 cc/h. Seven hours after arrival, laboratory results improved (pH 7.361, lactate 11.7 mmol/L), so HD/CRRT was deferred. Serum bicarbonate and lactate normalized at 25 and 29 h, respectively. Conclusions This report supports that pediatric MALA can be successfully treated without renal replacement therapy, using liberal hydration, alkali therapy, and measures to ensure adequate urine output.

title: Resource Efficiency and Eco‐Tourism Performance in Asia: A Cross‐Country Panel Analysis
abstract: The resource‐efficiency coefficient is not statistically significant in our full‐sample model of tourism receipts. The other estimates show why the outcome measure and the treatment of the pandemic period matter to its interpretation. We examine this relationship in a static panel of 14 Asian economies from 2002 to 2022. Inclusion in the sample is determined by data availability in the current World Bank extract. Resource efficiency is the primary explanatory variable, measured as GDP produced per unit of CO 2 ‐equivalent emitted. The Fixed Effects baseline uses country‐clustered standard errors and controls for population, electricity consumption, internet access, and urbanisation. Receipts as a share of exports yield a positive, statistically significant association with resource efficiency ( β = 1.318, p < 0.001); visitor arrivals do not yield a significant association ( β = 0.346, p = 0.608). Isolating or controlling for the COVID‐19 period strengthens the receipts result, with marginal significance in the pre‐COVID specification ( β = 0.753, p = 0.055). Taken together, these results favour evaluating resource‐efficiency policy in tourism‐dependent Asian economies in terms of the economic value generated by tourism, while retaining the conditions under which the association does and does not hold.

title: Misinformation environments and social risk: a communication perspective
abstract: Misinformation is widely recognised as a significant social risk, yet conceptual disagreement persists over how the problem should be defined, analysed and managed across disciplines. Within risk analysis, misinformation is typically approached as a problem of encoding: a product of poor practice in risk assessment or risk communication, addressed through stronger scientific fundamentals and greater transparency. This article argues that such an approach, while necessary, is insufficient. Drawing on communication and systems theory, it advances an alternative account in which misinformation is significantly a decoding phenomenon, produced between senders and receivers and situated within cultural and media environments that risk analysts have limited power to influence. The argument is explored through the case of Australia's renewable energy transition, focusing on the contested offshore wind sector, where growing community opposition has become entangled with misinformation about environmental and social risks. The article identifies several features of the Australian public sphere, including concentrated media ownership, uneven institutional trust, the legacy of strict Covid-19 restrictions and historic ties between fossil fuel interests and media ownership that make it particularly susceptible to misinformation. The analysis suggests that even sound, evidence-based risk assessments can be relabelled as misinformation within such environments. The article concludes by considering the implications of this systemic, environmental view of misinformation for risk analysis practice, arguing for closer integration between risk science and communication science.

title: Geopolitical shocks and global stock markets: panel evidence and neural network insights (2016–November 2025)
abstract: This study aims to analyze how geopolitical, climate and monetary news affects stock market returns and volatility. First, this study developed eight news indices covering geopolitical, economic and environmental topics, and measured their impact on the returns and volatility of 26 global stock markets (15 emerging and 11 developed) from January 2016 through November 2025. The proposed models include panel econometric methods (OLS, DOLS and FMOLS) and a multilayer perceptron artificial neural network. It is suggested that the response of developed markets is limited compared to that of developing markets. For developed countries, Russia–Ukraine conflict, Trump announcements, the supply chain pressures and the conflict between China and the US are statistically significant news indices. These results could be explained by the fact that several of the developed markets studied are in Europe and are directly affected by the conflict. On the other hand, Trump’s announcements also affect his main trading partners (the Netherlands, Germany, among others). The response of developing markets is oriented toward COVID-19, changes in Federal Reserve interest rates, global warming, the supply chain and news about the war. This response is related to the fragility of these markets and their dependence on foreign investment flows from developed markets. This research stands out and contributes in several ways: i) the sample size, which includes both developed and developing countries, allowing for a comparison of the response of each type of economy; ii) the creation and proposal of new indices with three impact windows and iii) the comparison of different types of econometric and artificial intelligence-based models. The results are crucial for economic policy communication, portfolio investment and its coverage, as well as market sentiment reactions to new information related to critical issues.

title: Digital ageing among mid-life and older 2SLGBTQ+ adults: expanding the health equity promotion model with a technological dimension
abstract: Abstract As society becomes increasingly digital, greater attention is needed to understand how diverse ageing populations engage with technology and how digital platforms affect their health and wellbeing. This article examines the role of technology in supporting the social health of mid-life and older adults who identify as Two-Spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, queer or another non-cisgender or non-heterosexual identity (2SLGBTQ+). Thematic analysis of focus group data from 23 participants aged 50 and older living in Canada during the Covid-19 pandemic revealed how digital platforms helped participants manage their social health needs. While technology operated as a social health resource that enabled connection, intimacy and community participation during this global health crisis, participants also described losses associated with diminished visibility, uneven digital access that reinforced social inequities and physical and mental health challenges linked to prolonged and intensified technology use. Notably, some participants credited the resilience they developed during the AIDS epidemic for their ability to navigate technological and Covid-related challenges. Beyond its empirical contribution, this article theoretically develops the health equity promotion model with the addition of a technological dimension. The adapted model’s application to the Canadian context shows how technology functions simultaneously as a protective and a risk factor, impacting the social health and broader health outcomes of ageing 2SLGBTQ+ populations. By recognizing technology as a determinant of health in this model, this article advances queer gerontological theory and offers a framework for understanding and promoting health equity in ageing 2SLGBTQ+ populations, with implications for health promotion research and practice.

title: The neurological, cardiac, and hepatic toxic effects of ivermectin and hydroxychloroquine and the ameliorative role of vitamin C: a biochemical, histological, and immunohistochemical experimental study
abstract: Physicians ought to be cautious about the toxic impact of an extensive range of potentially unproven medications when evaluating or managing disease outbreaks. This work aimed to evaluate the potentially toxic effects of ivermectin and hydroxychloroquine, which were used in the pandemic COVID 19; and in other various diseases, and then to assess the potentially protective effects of vitamin C in alleviating the toxic effects of these two drugs. Sixty Wistar albino rats were grouped into six groups (control, vitamin C-treated, ivermectin-treated, hydroxychloroquine-treated, ivermectin + vitamin C-treated, and hydroxychloroquine + vitamin C-treated groups). Serum biomarkers were measured, and the rats’ tissues were subjected to biochemical studies; oxidant and antioxidant biomarkers, histological and immunohistochemical examinations. Ivermectin and hydroxychloroquine significantly elevated serum biomarkers, MDA, and NO levels in examined organs and lowered GSH and SOD levels in brain and liver while elevated antioxidants levels in cardiac tissues. Additionally, they induced marked histopathological changes, increased collagen deposition, and increased expression of Cleaved Caspase-3 immune reactivity in neural, cardiac, and hepatic tissues. With the help of vitamin C, all alterations began to revert to their normal state. It was confirmed that administering repeated doses of ivermectin or hydroxychloroquine could induce detrimental toxic impacts on the cerebral cortex, heart, and liver through various analytical mechanisms. The use of vitamin C had significant protective capacities against these toxic effects. Ivermectin cause alterations in neural, cardiac, and hepatic cells in exposed rats. Vitamin C alleviates oxidative stress by reverting the antioxidant, and ROS levels. Vitamin C inhibits the inflammation and apoptosis and lowers cleaved caspase-3. High-dose vitamin C protects effectively ivermectin or hydroxychloroquine toxicity.

title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes.
abstract: BACKGROUND Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. RESULTS We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R2 > 0.95) across 5-105 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

title: Dolor abdominal agudo en el síndrome inflamatorio multisistémico pediátrico post-COVID
abstract: Introducción: El síndrome inflamatorio multisistémico pediátrico (PIMS) se caracteriza por síntomas gastrointestinales que pueden parecerse a un cuadro de abdomen agudo, principalmente a una apendicitis, lo que conlleva un reto diagnóstico importante en pediatría.Objetivo: Describir las características clínicas y epidemiológicas de los pacientes pediátricos con PIMS y dolor abdominal agudo, para identificar elementos clave para el diagnóstico diferencial con apendicitis aguda, en un hospital de tercer nivel en México.Material y métodos: Se realizó un estudio observacional, retrospectivo y transversal.Se incluyeron pacientes de 1 a 18 años con diagnóstico confirmado de PIMS entre marzo de 2020 y diciembre de 2024, quienes presentaron dolor abdominal agudo.Se analizaron variables clínicas, bioquímicas, de imagen y de tratamiento, además de la evolución clínica intrahospitalaria.Resultados: Se incluyeron 46 pacientes.El 80% presentaron a su ingreso dolor abdominal, el 63% además presentó vómito y el 17% diarrea.En todos los casos se observó elevación de biomarcadores inflamatorios.En el 10.8% de los casos (n = 5) se realizó apendicectomía, con confirmación histopatológica de apendicitis en fase I en 4 pacientes y en fase II en 1 paciente.En estos casos, el ultrasonido mostró líquido libre en la cavidad abdominal y adenitis mesentérica.Todos recibieron tratamiento farmacológico con esteroides; 11 casos requirieron también gammaglobulina y ácido acetilsalicílico.La media de la estancia hospitalaria fue de 12 días.Conclusiones: El PIMS debe sospecharse en niños con dolor abdominal agudo y antecedente reciente de COVID-19.Una evaluación clínica completa, apoyada en marcadores inflamatorios e imagenología, permite diferenciarlo de causas quirúrgicas como la apendicitis.El reconocimiento oportuno evita cirugías innecesarias y permite iniciar tratamiento inmunomodulador, con evolución favorable en la mayoría de los casos.

title: Coronavirus spherules are supported by a novel triple-layer protein lattice
abstract: Coronaviruses (CoVs) cause significant disease in humans and animals, with a track-record of cross-species transmission. Despite their global significance, available control strategies are limited, especially for emerging CoVs. A deeper fundamental understanding of the virus life cycle is essential to underpin development of control measures. A critical step of the CoV life cycle is the rearrangement of host cell membranes into replication organelles (ROs). This is conserved across all CoVs and ROs comprise double membrane vesicles (DMVs), the site of viral RNA synthesis, and double membrane spherules. CoV spherules are complex structures requiring both positive and negative curvature of paired membranes so are predicted to have a high energy cost to maintain. To date they have an entirely unknown function. Interestingly, although always present, abundance of spherules in CoV infected cells varies with Betacoronavirus Middle East Respiratory Syndrome coronavirus, Gammacoronavirus infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) and porcine deltacoronavirus in particular producing a considerable number. Here, using cryo-bioimaging we identified for the first time that CoV spherules are embedded with a complex and organised triple-layered protein lattice and that spherules always contain a cargo that appears arranged as a shell inside the vesicle. In addition, we confirmed the presence of a double membrane spanning molecular pore in Gammacoronavirus DMVs and further identified a population of potential DMV formation intermediates. Together, this work provides a foundation for understanding a fundamental yet unresolved aspect of coronavirus replication.

title: Trends in Patient Complaints in a Pediatric Emergency Department: Comparison of Pre- and Post-Pandemic Periods
abstract: Introduction: Patient and caregiver satisfaction is a key indicator of health care quality and is particularly relevant in pediatric emergency care. Patient complaints represent an important source of information regarding organizational weaknesses and unmet expectations. The COVID-19 pandemic and recent changes in referral pathways have modified the functioning of these services. This study aimed to analyze patient complaints registered in the pediatric emergency department of a level II hospital between January 2020 and June 2025, characterizing temporal trends, main reasons for dissatisfaction, and patient profiles, and comparing findings with the pre-pandemic period. Methods: A retrospective, observational, descriptive study based on the analysis of all complaints. Complaints were classified according to the Reader et al. taxonomy, evaluating demographic, clinical, and organizational variables as well as institutional response time. Data from January to June 2025 were available; annual estimates based on linear extrapolation were generated when required for descriptive comparisons. Results: A total of 166 complaints were analyzed among 153,088 pediatric emergency department visits, corresponding to an overall complaint rate of 0.11%. After reaching their lowest values in 2020 and 2021, complaint rates fluctuated annually, with the highest observed complaint rate recorded during the first semester of 2025. Waiting time remained the main reason for dissatisfaction. An increase in complaints related to staff attitude, hospital logistics, institutional rules, and prior referral processes was observed during the post-pandemic period, including the period following implementation of the “Call Before, Save Lives” project. Most complaints were submitted by mothers and concerned children aged 1 to 9 years. Institutional response time varied over the study period, with the shortest response times observed during the first semester of 2025. Conclusion: Patient complaints provide valuable information on persistent structural challenges and evolving patterns of dissatisfaction in pediatric emergency care, representing a useful tool for quality improvement initiatives.

title: Post-pandemic strategic evaluation of food supply chains using hybrid decision models
abstract: The increasing complexity and disruptions in global food supply chains (FSCs), particularly after COVID-19, have emphasized the need for resilient and adaptive strategies. This study conducts a comparative analysis of various FSC structures, such as Centralized, Decentralized, Digitalized, Localized, and Hybrid models. The comparison was carried out by applying two integrated multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods: Entropy-based MOORA and Entropy-based MARCOS. title: A evolução dos dashboards na análise de dados de saúde pública: um estudo bibliométrico
abstract: This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of the use of dashboards in public health data management between 2012 and 2024. The aim is to identify scientific trends, key authors, countries, journals, and the most frequent terms using VOSviewer software. Fifty-five articles selected from the PubMed database were analyzed. The research reveals a growth in publications, especially after 2019, peaking in 2024, driven by the covid-19 pandemic. Collaborative networks among researchers are also observed, with a predominance of authors affiliated with institutions in the United States. The results highlight the increasing relevance of dashboards in monitoring and decision-making in public health. It is concluded that there is a need for further collaborative and interdisciplinary research on the subject.

title: From APTs to advanced persistent biological threats (APBTs): a taxonomy and large-scale metadata audit of genomic surveillance infrastructure
abstract: Open genomic repositories have become critical infrastructure for pathogen surveillance, variant tracking, outbreak reconstruction, and public health decision making. However, many of these repositories were designed to support rapid scientific data sharing rather than adversarial verification, creating potential security gaps. This paper introduces Advanced Persistent Biological Threats (APBTs), as a framework for understanding how malicious cyber biological actors can gradually disrupt genomic surveillance without entering a laboratory or releasing a biological agent. Instead of altering biological material, an attacker targets the sequence data, metadata, reference datasets, and analytical models used by surveillance systems. We present, to our knowledge, the first integrated multilayer taxonomy of APBTs, structured around a four phase lifecycle, and investigate whether the metadata weaknesses identified by this framework are present in an operational genomic repository. To assess this, we audited 100,000 SARS-CoV-2 BioSample records obtained from the NCBI. A framework of 23 checks was applied across five metadata layers: temporal, geographic, host and specimen, provenance, and technical metadata. Every record triggered at least one APBT relevant metadata vulnerability indicator, with a mean of 7.34 indicators per record (SD = 1.34). Overall, 97.3% of records were classified in the High or Critical severity categories. Every record also contained at least one indicator in both the provenance and technical metadata layers. These results largely reflect the optional status of several fields in the current BioSample submission model rather than isolated errors by individual data contributors. Temporal and geographic information was comparatively complete, while fields needed for provenance reconstruction, chain of custody assessment, technical validation, and analytical interpretation were frequently missing. These findings do not indicate deliberate manipulation. However, the structural incompleteness of BioSample metadata creates vulnerabilities that an adversary can exploit to introduce poisoned, misleading, or weakly traceable metadata into genomic repositories. As a result, maliciously altered metadata can appear plausible, remain undetected, and influence downstream genomic analysis and surveillance. The findings therefore show that widely used pathogen genomic repositories already contain structural weaknesses that can support metadata poisoning as part of an APBT operation.

title: PRE-CISE: A PRE-calibration Coverage, Identifiability, and SEnsitivity analysis workflow to streamline model calibration
abstract: PurposeWe introduce PRE-CISE, a pre-calibration workflow integrating coverage analysis, local sensitivity, and collinearity diagnostics to streamline model calibration. We demonstrate PRE-CISEs benefits using two testbeds (a Sick-Sicker Markov model and an SIR transmission model) and a COVID-19 case study. MethodsPRE-CISE uses coverage analysis to verify that model outputs generated from the prior distribution span calibration targets, followed by local sensitivities to quantify parameter influence, guiding the resizing of prior bounds to improve coverage. Identifiability is assessed via collinearity analysis; large indices indicate practical nonidentifiability. Bayesian calibration was used: for the testbed models (3 and 2 parameters, respectively) to match their targets; for the COVID-19 model (11 parameters) to match daily confirmed incident cases. ResultsCoverage analyses flagged initial misfits; local sensitivities identified that the Sick-to-Sicker transition probability has a greater effect on model outputs, and resizing its prior distribution bounds improved coverage. Collinearity analyses indicated that using multiple calibration targets over different time points enabled identification of all three parameters. For the SIR testbed, collinearity indices declined as target points accumulated, crossing the identifiability threshold once the data spanned the epidemic peak. In the COVID-19 model, local sensitivity analyses prioritized time-varying detection rates and contact-reduction effects, reducing the search space. Daily incident case calibration targets yielded collinearity indices below practical thresholds for all parameter combinations, whereas indices for weekly calibration targets were larger. PRE-CISE achieved greater calibration efficiency gains for denser posterior sampling and more complex models. ConclusionsPRE-CISE provides a practical, transparent pathway that helps modelers refine prior distribution bounds and calibration targets before intensive calibration, improving uncertainty reporting and strengthening the reliability of model-based health policy analyses.

title: An Examination of Psychosocial Processes Related to Quality of Life in Pregnancy
abstract: Perinatal anxiety and potential protective processes are often poorly understood compared to other types of perinatal distress. The present study investigated the relationship between perinatal anxiety and quality of life or life satisfaction in a pregnant sample. Psychological flexibility and self-compassion were examined as moderators of these associations. COVID-19 and other external factors were examined on an exploratory basis. Results indicate significant correlations between perinatal anxiety and satisfaction with life, as well as psychological flexibility and perinatal anxiety; proposed interaction effects were not significant. This study may enhance understanding of these processes and contribute to the growing field of reproductive psychology.
journal: Journal of prenatal & perinatal psychology & health

title: Human lung organoid modelling of tissue-resident antiviral T cell responses
abstract: Tissue-resident immunity constitutes a first line of defence against pathogens and enables rapid innate and adaptive memory responses1-3. However, experimental studies have been hindered by a lack of holistic human in vitro models that enable epithelial infection in the context of tissue-resident immune subsets. In lung, differing notions of transient versus sustained residency of tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM cells) have challenged the extent to which anamnestic recall immunity to respiratory pathogens occurs locally or in concert with secondary lymphoid organs4-6. Here we generated long-term adult human distal lung organoids from intact tissue fragments in 3D air-liquid interface culture, which co-preserved epithelial and stromal components with endogenous lung-resident immune cells (T cells, B cells, natural killer cells and myeloid cells). The organoid T cells expressed residency and memory markers and preserved T cell receptor repertoires of cognate fresh tissue. SARS-CoV-2 infected the organoid lung epithelium, stimulated inflammatory cytokine production and, crucially, induced SARS-CoV-2-specific, tissue-resident T cell responses. Furthermore, boosting T cells within intact organoids with SARS-CoV-2 peptide pools blunted subsequent SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with a component of virus-specific protective TRM cell function in the absence of secondary lymphoid tissues. Overall, this immunocompetent lung organoid system demonstrates functional control of viral infection by lung-intrinsic memory T cell responses, provides a rationale for local vaccination strategies and validates a general platform for investigation of human tissue-resident immunity in health and disease.

title: Mortalidade por tuberculose e factores associados à co-infecção por HIV: estudo de coorte no distrito municipal de Kamaxaqueni, cidade de Maputo, 2017-2021
abstract: Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar a mortalidade por tuberculose e os fatores associados à coinfecção pelo HIV no Distrito Municipal de KaMaxaqueni, no período de 2017 a 2021. Para tanto, realizou-se um estudo de coorte retrospectivo utilizando dados do SISMA, abrangendo 4.077 casos notificados de tuberculose. O Risco Relativo (RR), com intervalo de confiança (IC) de 95%, foi calculado utilizando o software Epi Info 7.2. Os resultados indicaram uma taxa de letalidade geral de 7,7% [314/4.077]. Entre os pacientes com coinfecção TB-HIV, a taxa de letalidade foi de 10,1% [245/2.417], enquanto entre os pacientes com TB sem HIV foi de 4,2% [69/1.660]. O RR encontrado foi de 2,40 [IC 95%: 1,85-3,11; p<0,001]. Verificou-se também que 59,3% dos casos apresentavam coinfecção TB-HIV e que o maior risco de óbito ocorreu durante as primeiras 8 semanas de tratamento. Foram registradas 24 comorbidades, destacando-se a COVID-19 [33,3%] e o sarcoma de Kaposi [25,0%]. Diante desses achados, conclui-se que a coinfecção pelo HIV duplicou o risco de óbito por TB. Portanto, recomendam-se o rastreamento ativo, o início precoce da TARV/TPT e o monitoramento intensivo durante as primeiras 8 semanas.

title: ADA-3D: adaptive dimensional attention with dynamic fusion for 3D medical image segmentation
abstract: 3D medical image segmentation is frequently challenged by voxel anisotropy, low-contrast boundaries, and discontinuous inter-slice structures. This paper proposes Adaptive Dimensional Attention (ADA), a lightweight plug-and-play attention module for volumetric segmentation. ADA decouples feature calibration into hierarchical channel attention, anisotropic spatial attention, and slice-aware context attention. It further introduces a content-aware dynamic fusion mechanism (DFM) to adaptively balance these dimensions for different anatomical structures. By being integrated into nnFormer after patch embedding, ADA performs early feature calibration before Transformer encoding, enabling the subsequent encoder to receive features with stronger anatomical consistency. Experiments on ACDC cardiac MRI and COVID-19 CT segmentation show that ADA consistently outperforms representative attention modules including SE, CBAM, ECA, and EMA. Ablation results further verify that DFM and anisotropic spatial modeling are the key contributors to the performance gain.
journal: Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Signal Image Processing

title: Hugging Suit: Pneumatically-Actuated System Design for Remote Haptic Experiences
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic emphasised the importance of remote emotional communication and highlighted a gap in existing technologies that lack haptic channels. While video calls maintain visual and auditory presence, they cannot convey the emotional depth of physical contact, especially hugging, a universally recognised form of intimacy and support. To explore this challenge, we developed the Hugging Suit, a pneumatically-actuated wearable system that enables users to simulate and receive remote hugs in real time. Unlike prior haptic systems that focus solely on tactile sensation, our approach integrates both technical and experiential considerations. The system integrates a programmable Air Actuator Matrix (AAM), a portable high-pressure pneumatic unit, and a fabric-based pressure sensor layer, enabling precise, wearable haptic feedback while remaining lightweight and mobile. Guided by a Research through Design (RtD) methodology, we iteratively refined the prototype to improve tactile resolution, overall usability, and user comfort, while introducing modular components to support flexible and scalable haptic configurations. In parallel, we explored how specific contextual factors, such as lighting, privacy, and the visibility of the remote partner, might shape the emotional and perceptual experience of receiving a remote hug. Preliminary feedback suggests that low-lit, private spaces, especially when users could also see their remote partner via video, improved emotional engagement and comfort during mediated haptic experiences. Our low-cost, maker-space-friendly approach contributes to affective haptics applications in long-distance relationships, emotional regulation, and remote therapeutic support.

title: Large-scale assessment of socioeconomic, demographic and health system structures with US county excess mortality, 2020-2024
abstract: Socioeconomic, demographic, and health system structures may have shaped COVID-19 pandemic impact across populations, but past analyses typically examined few factors. We systematically examined correlates of COVID-era excess mortality, considering 2,745 county-level variables of demography, race/ethnicity, income, insurance, education, employment, housing, and health system. Pearson correlation coefficients (CCs) were obtained for the most recent available pre-pandemic value against age-standardized county excess-death for each year during 2020-2024. Counties were population-weighted. Variables were grouped by meaning into 11 semantic super-clusters. Overall, 17.3% of variables reached at least a moderate correlation level (|CC| > 0.30) and 2.8% reached strong correlations (|CC| > 0.45). Strongest correlations were seen for college attainment (CC -0.54), uninsurance among adults 40-64 (+0.53), and high income (-0.53). At least moderate correlations were seen for 9.1% of variables in 2020 and 8.5% in 2021, but only 1.8%, 0%, and 1.3% in 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. Similar patterns of concentration of moderate correlations in the first two pandemic years appeared in both elderly and non-elderly populations. Of 472 variables with |CC| > 0.30, 362/395 moderate-band and 77/77 strong-band variables belonged to demography and socioeconomic super-clusters. Only 7% of health system variables reached |CC| > 0.30, versus 31% of socioeconomic and demographic variables. Using the most recent available value until 2023 or 2015, different population weighting, and Spearman correlations yielded similar results. Overall, these ecological analyses suggest strong relationships of socioeconomic structure and demographics rather than health-care resources/supply with excess mortality across US counties especially during 2020-2021.
